deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs: SystickClock gains a last_us AtomicU64 monotonic floor; now_us() clamps its raw wraps-based reading up to the max previously returned. The raw reading steps BACKWARD when the SysTick exception is delayed past a wrap boundary on Cortex-M4F/M7 (lazy FP-context stacking + the cooperative executor's interrupt-disabling critical sections lengthen ISR latency), so `wraps` lags the hardware. Two named divergences from zenoh: (1) `saturating_sub` for the `now < lifespan` underflow (zenoh's plain NTP64 Sub debug-panics / release-wraps → would wipe both registries on an unset-RTC boot; wz collects nothing); (2) `latest` (the tombstone map) is NEVER swept — it is the authoritative newer-wins record, so GCing it would resurrect deleted keys; GC bounds ONLY the registry memory (the documented "tombstones retained unbounded" divergence). zenoh's `latest_updates` GC is an INVERTED-predicate bug (retain(ts < limit) keeps OLD) wz sidesteps by not GCing latest.

crates/wz-session-core/src/ntp64.rs: + `Ntp64::from_duration(span: Duration) -> Self` — the span constructor (byte-identical to uhlc `From<Duration>` on any representable span; reuses `from_unix`, the NTP64 SSOT, NOT a hand-rolled `(secs<<32)|frac`). Reads VLE(pair_count) via SceCursor::read_vle_u64 then count length-prefixed key/value strings via the crate::vle read_zbuf SSOT (the read inverse of write_zbuf), byte-faithful to pico ze_deserializer_deserialize_sequence_length + ze_deserializer_deserialize_string (serialization.c) and the z_sub_attachment.c decode loop. KEY DESIGN (3-agent DESIGN review + direct-read arbitration): select_link disqualifies a reliability-mismatched link BEFORE the priority band (faithful to zenoh universal/tx.rs select), so a 2-link aggregate segregates on ONE axis only; with QoS ON all links are UNIFORM Reliable (new multilink_pref_for) so the priority band is the live discriminant, with QoS OFF the y205 even/odd reliability spread is unchanged (mutually-exclusive 2-link modes). This is a DIRECT MIRROR of a real zenoh multilink-over-TCP deploy (a TCP link is always is_reliable, so zenoh's per-link priority ranges ride all-Reliable links, tx.rs:86-88). New multilink_priority_range(id) assigns by FaceId parity (even -> HIGH [Control..=InteractiveLow], odd -> LOW [DataHigh..=Background]; non-overlapping + jointly covering 0..=7 so every priority is a full match on exactly one link). The band threads a feature-independent (Priority, Priority) tuple (NOT the all(multilink,qos)-gated LinkPriorityRange, which in a pub signature would break the transport-multilink && !transport-qos CI lane -- the y218 qos:bool discipline) through the two _with_multilink entrypoints, applied via set_link_priority_range inside `#[cfg(transport-qos)] if qos`; retained across re-add in ml_dial_endpoints (grown to a 3-tuple) so a flapped link restores its band (a fresh-id band would flip parity + collapse the split). A DEPLOY-active in-process e2e (real peer_loop qos=true max_links=2) sends an EXPRESS (Control) + a LOW (Background) reliable Put and asserts they arrive on DISTINCT faces (is_qos()==true asserted FIRST so the DEFAULT-clamp cannot false-green). SCOPE (deliberate split, user-approved): the joined-face DELIVERY gap (a joined secondary link is not a forwarder face, so the real LinkStateForwarder drops data/control routed onto it -- latent since y205, first exposed by priority routing) + the demo --express flags + the black-box 2-proc e2e are y219b. full run-ci pending the batch push; per-atom host lanes green (deploy e2e 3/3 + unit 2/2 + e2e 5+6 + readd 1 + all clippy -D warnings + fmt).

A joined (aggregated secondary) multilink link was never registered as a forwarder face, so the real LinkstateForwarder DROPPED any data/control the sender routed onto it (forward_push / dispatch_local_subscribers early-return on faces.get(inbound)=None). Latent since y205 (DEFAULT priority always routes to first_alive=primary, so the secondary carried no data), first EXPOSED by y219a's priority routing (a non-DEFAULT Put deliberately rides the secondary; also DEFAULT=Data(5) falls in the LOW band, so post-y219a even a plain DEFAULT publish on a qos aggregate rides the possibly-secondary LOW-band link). KEY DESIGN ARBITRATION (3-agent DESIGN + direct-read): the naive call-site re-attribution (drive_joined_face forwards the PRIMARY id) BREAKS the receiver-side per-face observation that MULTIPLE committed+PUSHED tests rely on (the y205 deploy_active_two_links reliability-segregation assert_ne! on faces, and the y219a priority-segregation faces.len()==2) -- the DESIGN agent's "no observer" claim was wrong, the test forwarders ARE observers. So the fix is FORWARDER-INTERNAL (option D'): drive_joined_face is UNCHANGED (forwards the physical id), and only the REAL LinkstateForwarder resolves a joined FaceId to the session's PRIMARY registered face at the TOP of forward() -- via a new joined_faces map populated by two new FaceForwarder default-no-op methods register_joined/deregister_joined the accept loop calls at the JOIN / secondary-death. Observation-only test forwarders keep seeing the physical id (per-face witnesses unaffected), while the routing forwarder presents ONE logical face per aggregate (the faithful zenoh model: an aggregated transport is one FaceState; also unifies the per-link keyexpr alias table). The delivery fix is proven directly by a LinkstateForwarder lib unit (a Put on the joined FaceId is DROPPED before register_joined, DELIVERED after, DROPPED after deregister_joined -- diagnose-first verified RED when register_joined is neutered), and the accept-loop WIRING (register_joined called with secondary-not-registered -> primary-registered) by an assertion in the y219a deploy e2e. Round 311y259.decision_summary: R311y259 -- give the inventory a CROSS-IMPL PROOF axis, and discover the honest number is far below the folk number. R311y257 made "what is BUILT" a CI line; the north star ("zenoh + zenoh-pico FULL") does not turn on building 212 atoms, it turns on WITNESSING them against the real zenoh-pico C stack and the real zenoh-full router -- and that number existed only as a hand estimate ("~75% foreign-proven") in a memory file whose own text says it was never recomputed and whose cited authority does not exist in this repo. Layer A4 now derives it. The design took three adversarial reviews to get right and the first version was wrong in five load-bearing ways, all recorded here because the corrections ARE the design: (1) "derive, then gate" was FALSE -- a cfg site cannot lie about itself, which is why A3 inv#3 works, but a `// wz-proves:` doc-comment is inert prose that can; moving the claim from inventory prose to test prose relocates the lie, it does not derive it. The missing second arm was already in the tree: an atom that is not in the enabled-feature CLOSURE of the binary under test compiles to NOTHING in it, so it CANNOT have been witnessed -- a compiler-grounded refutation that kills the "list ten, witness one" class. (2) The corpus predicate ("proves iff it SPAWNS a foreign binary") EXCLUDED the strongest proofs: the 25 layer3_* tests LINK the real vendored zenoh-pico C library and byte-compare wz's encoder against pico's _z_*_encode, and they are the ONLY foreign proofs hosted CI runs unconditionally. The incentive was inverted -- adding a differential codec test would have LOWERED the number, adding a never-executed #[ignore]d zenohd test would have RAISED it. Linking the foreign impl is a stronger proof than spawning it. (3) The percentage was not well-formed: the numerator was not a subset of the denominator (an UNBUILT atom could be claimed proven), so it could exceed 100%. (4) The denominator was a DOCUMENTED error -- R311jl already ruled the wz-catalog denominator invalid for parity claims -- and 25 of the 185 built atoms are foreign-NON-observable by construction (platform/runtime substrate, caches, seams, cargo aliases, switchboard), so an unproven list built on it could never reach zero, and a gate nobody can close is a gate everyone ignores. (5) A boolean per atom prints claims the corpus FORBIDS IN WRITING (wz_priority_to_pico_zsub.rs:30: "Do not read this single test as a full 'qos cross-impl proven' claim") -- the real unit is (atom x carrier x direction x peer), so the axis records direction, and `partial` is never folded into proven. The result: 68 corpus files / 133 tests, every test declaring; proven=50 partial=16 unproven=94 against a NAMED denominator of 160. NO percentage is printed, deliberately -- a single number against an unnamed denominator is the error this axis exists to stop, and it would invite comparison with the legacy ~75%, which is a zenoh-pico-parity figure with a different denominator. The gate immediately earned itself: containment REFUTED two live over-claims (transport-qos, on tests where it is not even compiled), and the A4-6 contradiction gate fired on `switchboard`, upheld on arbitration. The exclusion set is falsifiable BY DESIGN: witness one of the 25, and A4 fails and the exclusion was wrong.

Picked from the 94-atom list by the rule y259 established: a proof that hosted CI actually RUNS is worth more than one it does not, and a pico-CLI witness lands in Layer E (every push) whereas a zenohd witness lands in Layer Z (which hosted CI never even builds). That failure mode is silent and nasty: the payload arrives intact and is labelled the wrong media type, so an application/cbor sample surfaces as application/cdr in the foreign consumer. The new test publishes one Put per id 0..=52 and pairs pico's two consecutive output lines (`Received ('demo/enc': 'enc-<id>')` then `with encoding: <mime>`, z_sub_attachment.c:59,61) to correlate each id to the MIME zenoh-pico's OWN table resolved for it, then checks every one against wz's `mime_for_id`. Result: all 53 agree; wz and zenoh-pico share one encoding table, proven on a real socket. Grading is deliberately NOT uniform: the 52 non-default ids are DISCRIMINATING (a dropped encoding field would make pico print the default zenoh/bytes instead of the expected MIME), but id 0 (`encoding-empty`) is not -- pico prints zenoh/bytes both when wz sends id 0 explicitly and when the field is absent -- so encoding-empty is claimed `partial` with that stated in the header, even though wz demonstrably does put id 0 on the wire (push_build.rs::gated_encoding_field special-cases nothing). `pubsub-encoding wz->pico` also stays `partial`: the SCHEMA sub-field (id << 1 | 1, then schema bytes) is exercised only pico->wz, by pico_pub_attachment_to_wz_sub, and this test does not close it. Round 311y261.decision_summary: R311y261 -- close the QUERY-KNOB cluster of the A4 backlog, and do it in the STRONGEST execution class available. The y260 selection rule says pick the next cluster by whether hosted CI would actually RUN the witness; this round pushes that rule one notch further. A pico-CLI proof lands in Layer E, which hosted CI runs but only via --ignored; a CODEC-PARITY proof links the real vendored zenoh-pico C encoder in-process and runs in Layer C1 (cargo test --workspace) with NO #[ignore] at all -- on every push, unconditionally, with no external binary to provision. So the six query knobs, all of which are codec surface, were proven that way rather than through a CLI. Diagnosis first, per the rule that direct read is the arbiter: zenoh-pico DOES decode the Request exts (_ext_target / _ext_budget / _ext_timeout_ms, network.h:139-141) and the Query body fields (_consolidation / _parameters / _ext_attachment, message.h:104-111) and it DOES have the Response ERR arm (_Z_RESPONSE_BODY_ERR) -- but it exposes NO public getter for target/timeout on z_loaned_query_t, so a stock z_queryable CANNOT print them and the CLI route would have needed an invasive example patch to witness what the C encoder can byte-compare directly. wz's side is the production path, not a test-only shim: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/querier.rs drives the same RequestQueryBuilder these tests exercise. What the round proves: wz's REQUEST-level target ext and timeout ext, the QUERY-body consolidation (Q_C flag + mode byte), selector parameters (Q_P flag + length-prefixed slice) and attachment ext, and the RESPONSE(Err) arm, are each byte-identical to what zenoh-pico's own C encoder emits for the same value. Each test carries an ANTI-VACUITY guard asserting the knob-bearing encoding differs from the bare default envelope -- without it, a wz that silently DROPPED a knob and a pico whose sentinel logic emitted nothing would agree by both encoding the same 4 bytes, and the compare would pass proving nothing. The err arm matters disproportionately: every prior Layer 3 response compare drives the REPLY arm, so wz's ERROR path -- the one a queryable takes when it cannot answer -- was structurally unproven against zenoh-pico, and a disagreement there is worst-case invisible (the happy path interoperates; only failures mis-decode). An adversarial post-build review then downgraded ALL SIX claims from full to PARTIAL, and that downgrade is the honest result rather than a footnote. The tests are ENCODE-ONLY byte differentials, and -- except query-attachment -- they never compile the code the atom is DEFINED as: `query-target`'s cfg sites are in querier.rs (QueryOptions::with_target), while RequestQueryBuilder::request_target is UNGATED, so turning the query-target feature OFF leaves the test compiling and passing while still claiming the atom foreign-proven. A4's containment arm cannot catch this (the feature IS in the closure); only reading the test can. The same class the y260 EncodingHint over-claim fell into, and the sibling `query-value` -- same file, same shape, with STRICTLY MORE evidence (a codec-parity byte test AND a live pico-queryable test) -- is itself graded partial, which settles it. The atoms' own definitions confirm the grade: query-selector-parameters is `F=selector param PARSE` (a DECODE-side concern an encode test cannot reach); query-consolidation is `C=indep reply dedup` and query-target `C=indep query routing knob` -- neither of which a byte comparison exercises. The review also forced three real FIXES: (a) the magic enum literals (1 / 2 / _tag = 1) were hand-transcribed copies of pico's constants, so an upstream renumbering would have degraded the differential from "wz vs pico" to "wz vs my copy of pico" -- they now import the bindgen consts; (b) NOTHING pinned the knob-LESS builder against pico's default, so a builder that spuriously emitted a sentinel-valued ext would have broken a real pico queryable with zero test failures -- a converse test now closes it; (c) the err test drove `build_response_err_empty`, a shape PRODUCTION NEVER EMITS -- the real reply_err path requires a literal keyexpr (mapping_id=0 panics without a suffix) and always stamps an encoding, so a second test now byte-compares that N-flag + E-flag shape, which is the branch that actually crosses the wire. Net Layer A4 movement: the six atoms go UNPROVEN -> PARTIAL, not -> proven. All-lanes unproven 87 -> 81 and hosted-CI-executed unproven 108 -> 102; `proven` correctly does NOT move, because encode-side byte parity is not full cross-impl proof of a behavioural knob.

Round 311y262.decision_summary: R311y262 -- close keyexpr-includes and keyexpr-mapping, and pick them by the rule y261's failure taught: check FIRST that the test will compile the code the atom is DEFINED as. y261 downgraded six query atoms because their codec-parity byte differentials never crossed the atoms' own cfg gates (the gates live in querier.rs; the builder the tests drove is ungated), so this round front-loaded that check: keyexpr-includes is ACTIVE and its entry point `keyexpr_includes_patterns` is ITSELF `#[cfg(feature = "keyexpr-includes")]` (keyexpr_match.rs:567) -- turn the feature off and the differential does not compile, let alone pass. The claim binds. WHY THE ATOM NEEDED ITS OWN WITNESS, and why the sibling intersects differential was not enough: INCLUDES IS DIRECTIONAL WHERE INTERSECTS IS SYMMETRIC. `a ∩ b` asks whether some key matches both; `a ⊇ b` asks whether EVERY key b matches is also matched by a. An implementation can agree with zenoh-pico on every intersects answer and still get the subsumption backwards -- `*` and `**` intersect in both directions, but `**` includes `*` while `*` does NOT include `**`. Nothing in the repo had ever checked that asymmetry against a foreign implementation, and the corpus here contains the pairs where includes and intersects genuinely disagree, so an includes-aliased-to-intersects wz FAILS (3 of the 5 tests, first at the pair ("a","*")). The witness is zenoh-pico's real `_z_keyexpr_forward_includes`, the worker `_z_keyexpr_includes` dispatches into -- emitted by the SAME macro-template instantiation that produces the intersects worker the sibling test already uses (keyexpr.c:565-568), so it is exposed the same way (a hand-written forward decl in the sys wrapper header + one allowlist line) and it runs in Layer C1 on every push, unconditionally, with no external binary to provision. keyexpr-mapping was not a new test at all but an UNDER-CLAIM: pico's z_put calls z_declare_keyexpr and then Pushes by mapping id with NO suffix on the wire, so wz's alias table MUST resolve it or `SUBSCRIBER FIRED` is unreachable (a table miss returns None and the dispatch is dropped silently) -- ap_demo_round_trip has been witnessing wz's resolver against a FOREIGN-declared mapping all along, and wz_publisher_aliased_to_zsub the reverse, and neither said so. Under-claiming makes the unproven list wrong in the same way over-claiming makes the proven list wrong. An adversarial review then caught three real defects, all fixed: the algebra test was NOT a differential (it checked wz=>wz and pico=>pico independently and never compared the two -- a wz returning `false` unconditionally passed it, and its doc-comment asserted the opposite); the `$*` corpus never reached the ordered sub-part walk, which is exactly where includes and intersects diverge (a bare `a$*` short-circuits on both sides); and one input, a lone `$*` chunk, is NON-CANONICAL -- both canonizers rewrite it to `*`, so it sits outside both matchers' stated "assume canonized chunks" precondition and no production path can emit it. Both atoms are `partial`, honestly: the corpus is a bounded alphabet with no @-verbatim chunks, and the mapping claims witness the alias table's PRESENCE, not its content.

THE DIVERGENCE, and it is a standing fact about the two implementations rather than a task: zenoh-pico's NTP64 composer adds one tick that zenoh's own uhlc does not (pico protocol/core.c:70 `... / NANOS_PER_SEC + 1` vs uhlc-0.8.1 ntp64.rs:292 with no +1). wz mirrors uhlc, so wz agrees with zenoh and PICO IS THE OUTLIER. Same instant, stamps one NTP64 tick (~233 ps) apart. It does not break the wire (each side decodes the other's word faithfully -- proven byte-for-byte) but it means a cross-impl timestamp COMPARISON is not exact. Do NOT "fix" wz to match: wz's reference is zenoh, and bending it to one pico off-by-one would put it out of step with every zenoh peer. `layer3_ntp64.rs` pins the anomaly and FAILS if upstream pico ever drops the `+ 1` -- at which point time-ntp64 can go from partial to full. Worth reporting upstream to zenoh-pico.

Round 311y263.decision_summary: R311y263 -- an UNDER-CLAIM sweep of the corpus, and the cross-impl divergence it turned up. Two premises drove the round. FIRST: under-claiming is a defect of the same kind as over-claiming. y262 found keyexpr-mapping sitting at ZERO claims while two tests had been witnessing it all along, and an unproven list that names an atom nothing has ever failed to prove is exactly as wrong as a proven list that names one nothing proved. So the corpus was swept against the 79-atom unproven list under the same bar the claims themselves are held to (foreign participation / DISCRIMINATING witness / crosses the atom's own cfg gate). The sweep's REJECT list is the more valuable half and is recorded here, because it stops twelve future over-claims: time-system-clock (the timestamp test HAND-SETS the value, so wall_clock_ntp64 is never called), ext-pubsub-serde-codec (the attachment tests agree with pico's ze_serializer ON THE WIRE but wz's serialize_kv_attachment is built on crate::vle and never touches serde_codec -- the exact trap that cost y261 six downgrades), transport-keepalive ("the session stayed up" is not discriminating -- nothing asserts a KeepAlive), transport-batching (zero corpus tests call batch_start/batch_end), session-reconnect (no corpus test re-dials against a foreign peer), session-matching (the only matching listener in the corpus is PICO's, not wz's), liveliness-get (its only caller is a wz<->wz test, which A4-3 forbids from claiming), liveliness-history (no corpus binary passes history=true, so the per-call gate is never crossed), scouting-active/-static/-multicast, and locator-tcp/-udp (a locator string is a LOCAL config artifact each side parses with its own parser -- nothing forces the two grammars to agree). Only two atoms were genuinely under-claimed: attachment-bytes (the attachment CODEC -- encode_attachment_ext / serialize_kv_attachment -- is a DISJOINT code body from pubsub-attachment, which gates the field plumbing; both attachment tests IMPORT the gated module and cannot compile without it) and time-ntp64. SECOND: the sweep named a cheap gap in the strongest lane -- every Push/MsgPut differential drove the DEFAULT no-flag shape, so the body-level timestamp and attachment slots had a live wire witness but NO byte-compare against pico's own C encoder. That is now closed against the PRODUCTION builder (build_push_literal_with_meta, the SSOT Session::publish routes through), and it passes byte-for-byte. AND THEN THE REAL FIND. Chasing time-ntp64 to a FULL grade meant proving the other half of the atom -- the word's CONSTRUCTION, `(seconds, nanos) -> secs << 32 | frac`, which a byte-compare of an already-composed word structurally cannot reach -- so a differential was written against zenoh-pico's own composer. IT FAILED, and it was right to: zenoh-pico's `_z_timestamp_ntp64_from_time` (protocol/core.c:66-72) adds `+ 1` to the fraction, which zenoh's own reference does NOT (uhlc-0.8.1/src/ntp64.rs:287-293). wz mirrors uhlc exactly, so wz agrees with zenoh and ZENOH-PICO IS THE OUTLIER: for the same instant a pico stamp sits one NTP64 tick (2^-32 s, ~233 ps) above a wz/zenoh stamp -- including at (0s, 0ns), where zenoh says 0 and pico says 1. The divergence is UNIVERSAL (verified pico == wz + 1 across all 40 (secs, nanos) probes) and wz is pinned to uhlc's formula, recomputed in the test so it binds to the REFERENCE rather than to itself. wz is NOT bent to match: its reference is zenoh, and matching one pico off-by-one would put it out of step with every zenoh peer. The test therefore PINS the anomaly and claims NO atom -- a locked disagreement is the opposite of an interop proof, the same treatment the corpus already gives the known pico canon anomalies -- and time-ntp64 stays `partial` on the wire claim with the composer divergence named as its residual. The codec agreeing does not make the atom whole. Layer A4: unproven 79 -> 77, proven 52 -> 53, partial 29 -> 30 (hosted-CI-executed unproven 100 -> 98).
verification_bullets: The NTP64 divergence is verified against the REFERENCE, not asserted: `uhlc-0.8.1/src/ntp64.rs:287-293` (what zenoh stamps through) is `(secs << 32) + ((nanos * FRAC_PER_SEC) / NANO_PER_SEC)` with NO +1; `vendor/zenoh-pico/src/protocol/core.c:66-72` is `nanos * 2^32 / 1e9 + 1`. wz's `Ntp64::from_unix` matches uhlc. Round 311y265.decision_summary: R311y265 -- the whole-session review round (3 independent adversarial agents over y259..y264, pre-push), and it caught the session reproducing its own headline failure mode one lane over. THE FALSE GREEN: R311y264 wired Layer E2 into hosted CI, but E2 was prereq-SKIP on six wz-e2e-* subset binaries that NOTHING builds -- not run-ci.sh, not the workflow. It passed locally only because those binaries linger in target/ from an earlier session; a fresh runner has none. And because Layer A4 derives "this lane runs in hosted CI" from ci.yml, wiring the step made A4 COUNT E2's pico proofs as EXECUTED while a fresh runner would have SKIPped every one of them, green. That is precisely the hazard the same commit's ZENOHD_ALLOW_CLONE comment was written to guard against (a SKIP is green), reintroduced next door -- and it would have shipped. The fix is structural, not a workflow step: a lane now BUILDS its own wz binaries, the way E6 / E8 / Z already build wz-ap-demo, and the rule is stated where it can be applied again -- SKIP on a FOREIGN binary (a machine may legitimately lack the zenoh-pico CLI or zenohd), NEVER on a wz binary we can just build. Layer E was carrying the same latent hole (it SKIPped on a missing wz-ap-demo and was saved only by an explicit workflow step) and now builds its demo too. Layer Z's remaining SKIPs are on genuinely external binaries, so they stay SKIPs on a developer's box -- but the hosted job GUARANTEES them, so it now sets WZ_Z_REQUIRE=1 and every one of them escalates to a FAIL there, the exact shape of the existing WZ_QZ_REQUIRE ("a should-run lane that SKIPs is the burn"). No hosted lane can now SKIP green on anything the job provisions. TWO OVER-CLAIMS, both of the family that has bitten every round of this session, both DOWNGRADED (and both lower the headline number, which is the correct direction): codec-keep-alive was FULL on a comparison of two EMPTY VECTORS -- the atom is a fieldless struct whose encoder is a no-op, so deleting its body leaves the gate green, and the file's own doc concedes the atom's only real wire contribution (the MID byte) is written by the enclosing envelope and out of scope; the irony is that y263 rejected `transport-keepalive` for non-discrimination while `codec-keep-alive` sat at FULL next door. And `pubsub-encoding pico->wz` was FULL from a ONE-VALUE witness whose schema bit is SET, so a decoder that ignored the bit and always parsed a schema string would pass while corrupting every schemaless encoding pico sends -- while the wz->pico sibling, a 53-id sweep with strictly more evidence, is itself graded partial. y261's settling rule applies verbatim. A FROZEN LEDGER CORRECTION, which is why this entry exists rather than an edit: Round 311y263's decision_summary states that `liveliness-history` was rejected because "no corpus binary passes history=true, so the per-call gate is never crossed". THAT IS FALSE. wz_to_zenohd_router.rs:911 passes `--liveliness-subscribe-history`, and wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs:427 sets `liveliness_options.history` from it. The CONCLUSION (leave the atom unproven) stands, but for a different and weaker reason the test's own doc-comment supplies: history was added there to REMOVE AN ORDERING RACE, so the leg passes on the plain live-routing path too, and nothing asserts a REPLAYED token as distinct from a ROUTED one -- the witness is not discriminating. This matters because y263 itself argued its REJECT list is the more valuable half; a reject list whose stated reason is a false claim about the corpus fails OPEN, since a future round would read the frozen reason, see that history=true is now passed, and claim the atom. Also corrected: y263's reject list is thirteen atoms, not "twelve"; y264's "64 of the corpus's tests are #[ignore]d" is 65 on HEAD (the figure was carried over from y259's 64-of-133). The verification bullets of both entries were exact; only the summary prose drifted. Round 311y266.decision_summary: R311y266 -- the gate-integrity half of the whole-session review, and it found that the gate was lying in a way nobody was watching. Layer A4's disclosure line read "E7/M only in the local full run-ci (pre-push)". FALSE FOR M: Layer M guards itself with `ONLY_LAYER != "M" && WZ_RUN_LAYER_M != 1`, and the pre-push hook invokes run-ci.sh with neither -- so M runs on NO default path at all, hosted or local. Three atoms (router-multicast-faces, transport-link-udp, transport-multicast) were sitting inside the headline `proven` on the strength of tests that execute NOWHERE, and nothing named them: `promoted_by_unrun` only catches the partial->full promotion case, so the strictly worse population -- proven with ZERO hosted-CI witness of any kind -- was visible only as an unexplained delta between the two headline counts. Both are fixed: the roll-up now prints PROVEN WITH NO HOSTED-CI WITNESS AT ALL and names them, and `opt_in_lanes()` derives "runs nowhere" from the guard itself, so the disclosure cannot drift back into a lie. THE GATE'S KILL SWITCH WAS ONE NETWORK BLIP AWAY. audit-crossimpl-proof.sh exits 0 when mnemosyne-cli is absent, and hosted CI installs it behind a deliberately fault-tolerant `|| { warning; skip }` fallback -- so a transient upstream failure would have left EVERY invariant unchecked (a malformed claim, an atom renamed out of the inventory, a wz<->wz test claiming foreign proof) on a green build. WZ_A4_REQUIRE=1 in the workflow turns that skip into a failure. THE SAME SHAPE, ONE LEVEL DOWN, ACROSS EVERY HOSTED PROOF LANE: E / E2 / E6 / E8 all SKIP green on a missing zenoh-pico CLI, and E6's three pico legs skip INDIVIDUALLY, so deleting one workflow step would have taken every pico proof out of hosted CI while A4 -- which reads "this lane is in ci.yml" as evidence its proofs executed -- kept counting them. A shared `_pico_cli_unavailable` helper now escalates under WZ_PICO_REQUIRE, set on the interop job. The rule these three fixes share, and the one worth carrying: a SKIP on a binary the job PROVISIONS is a provisioning regression wearing a green badge (WZ_QZ_REQUIRE's "a should-run lane that SKIPs is the burn", now applied to A4, to the pico CLIs, and to Z). Also fixed, each a latent false-green rather than a live one: the zenohd cache was keyed on the version alone with no content hash of the build script, so a cache once populated WITHOUT the storage-manager plugin would have stranded that proof behind a green SKIP for the life of the key -- it is now keyed on hashFiles(build-zenohd.sh) and a step ASSERTS both artefacts are present after restore rather than trusting it; `cf.binary`'s ternary had two IDENTICAL branches, so a file driving several wz binaries silently got the alphabetically-first (wz-ap-demo, the fattest 110-feature closure) and its claims would have been validated against a union it does not have -- the audit now unions the closures of every binary a file drives, which is a superset and so can never false-FAIL; `#[ignore]` written ABOVE `#[test]` left has_ignore False, so a skipped test counted as "runs on every push via C1"; and helper_classes() splits lib.rs on a hard 4-space fn indent, so a reformat would have silently returned {} and shrunk the corpus AND every derived number with it, still green -- it now raises instead. The interop job's timeout goes 60 -> 120: a cold cache must build the pico CMake tree, the whole zenoh workspace in release, four differently-featured wz-ap-demo builds, six wz-e2e-* binaries and then Layer Z's serial sweep. DISCLOSED, NOT FIXED: `ci_executes` is still derived from what the shell INTENDS to run, not what it DID run. The SKIP holes it could not see are closed by escalation rather than by modelling, and the only sound version of that predicate joins the claims to libtest's actual `test <name> ... ok` output. Until then, "executed by hosted CI" is a well-guarded assertion, not a measurement. carry_forward_bullets: R311y267 = the footprint gate fix. THE DURABLE LESSON, and it is a new shape of the one this session keeps re-learning: A GREEN LOCAL GATE IS NOT A GREEN GATE. run-ci passed on every one of those ~20 pushes; hosted CI was red the whole time and nobody looked, because the workflow trusts pre-push. Check `gh run list` at kickoff -- the local gate and the hosted gate are two different gates, and only one of them is the one that ships.

THE DEEPER CLASS: an absolute-byte gate is only meaningful against a fixed build environment, and NOTHING was fixing it -- not the compiler (dtolnay@stable floats) and not the build path (rustc bakes it into .rodata, which berkeley `size` counts as text). Any gate whose number depends on WHERE and WITH WHAT it was measured will eventually report the environment as a code regression. Both variables are now removed by construction rather than compensated for with a rebased number.

DO NOT re-derive the retired rule. "The footprint baseline is CI-arm-gcc-specific; local gcc emits ~68 B less; rebase from the CI log numbers" was FALSE -- the gcc/binutils/newlib packages are byte-identical on both machines, and that recipe would have pinned a floating compiler's number at one machine's path (going red again at rustc 1.98, and leaving the local gate 4 bytes from red). The 68 B it described was path length, not codegen.

BUMPING THE PIN IS A ROUND, NOT A DRIFT: rust-toolchain.toml + the check-footprint baselines + the §6.7/§6.9 caveats move together in one commit, so the ledger always records which compiler each footprint number was measured under. The pin also removes a lint-drift class the portability/ci jobs were exposed to (a floating stable can newly fail -D warnings on a commit that changed nothing).

NEXT: the ~20-push red streak is cleared by this commit, but CONFIRM IT on the first hosted run -- Layer Q must report +0 deltas on the runner, which is the real test of the path-normalisation claim (the container reproduction predicts it). Then resume the cross-impl proof axis: adminspace (8 atoms) is the biggest unblocked cluster, per R311y265.

Round 311y267.decision_summary: R311y267 -- the footprint gate was measuring its own build directory's path length, and hosted CI had been RED for ~20 pushes because of it. The kickoff read of `gh run list` (not of run-ci, which was green) found the last green at 99e42828 and every push since e81d7a50 (2026-07-09) failing on Layer Q's mcu-multicast-e2e footprint. The code never regressed: a clean local build of HEAD reads 51116 at rustc 1.96 -- byte-identical to the CI number of the last GREEN run. TWO ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES WERE BEING GATED AS IF THEY WERE CODE. (1) rustc floats: every job used dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable, and stable went 1.96.1 -> 1.97.0 on 2026-07-09 -- the exact day the red streak begins -- moving codegen ~+48 B on this binary. The workspace rust-version field is an MSRV LOWER BOUND and never pinned the build compiler, which is what a byte-exact ROM gate needs; the project already knew this (build-zenohd.sh pins zenoh's 1.85.0 channel with the comment that building on another channel "is not a reproducibility trade this project makes") and had simply never applied it to its own build. (2) rustc embeds ABSOLUTE BUILD PATHS (panic Location strings, cargo registry sources) in .rodata, and `size --format=berkeley` counts .rodata inside its `text` column -- so the gated number encodes the length of the path it was built at. Proven by construction, not inferred: the same commit and same rustc measured 50964 built at /w, 51164 at /home/coin/watching-zenoh, and 51344 at the runner's /home/runner/work/watching-zenoh/watching-zenoh -- a 380 B spread on identical code against a +/-256 B band, ordered exactly by path length. An ubuntu:22.04 container mounted at the runner's path reproduced CI's 51344 to the byte, which is what turned a theory into a diagnosis. THE PRIOR EXPLANATION WAS FALSE AND HAD TO GO: the standing "footprint baseline is CI-arm-gcc-specific, local gcc emits less" rule (§6.7 caveat (r), and the recipe of rebasing baselines from CI log numbers) blamed arm-gcc -- but CI and this host carry byte-identical gcc 10.3.1 / binutils 2.38 / newlib 3.3.0 packages, and following that recipe would have pinned a number produced by a floating compiler at one machine's path, going red again at the next rustc and leaving the local gate 4 bytes from red. FIXED BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY REBASING THE NUMBER: rust-toolchain.toml pins rustc 1.97.0 and owns components + targets (they must follow the PINNED toolchain -- left on a floating stable they would install on a toolchain cargo does not use, and run-ci.sh SKIPs a target it cannot find, so the footprint gate would have gone quietly green having measured nothing: a SKIP is green, one lane over); Layer Q exports --remap-path-prefix for every MCU build; and check-footprint.sh now re-asserts path purity on the ARTIFACT, FAILing a binary that still embeds the repo root or CARGO_HOME rather than measuring it. Verified: host and runner-path container now agree byte-for-byte (50956), and the negative test confirms the new gate actually fires. Baselines rebased once onto the reproducible measurement; all six deltas +0. Layer Q pass, RUNCI_EXIT=0.
verification_bullets: Diagnosis is reproduced, not inferred: an ubuntu:22.04 container mounted at the CI runner's path (/home/runner/work/watching-zenoh/watching-zenoh, CARGO_HOME=/home/runner/.cargo) built mcu-multicast-e2e at 51344 -- byte-identical to hosted CI's failing number. The same container at /w gave 50964 and this host gave 51164, on the same commit and same rustc: the spread is path length.

rustc was isolated as the second variable from CI's own logs: the last GREEN run (99e42828) ran rustc 1.96.1 and measured multicast thumbv7m=51116; the first RED run (e81d7a50, same day) ran 1.97.0 and measured 51444. All ARM packages are identical on both machines (gcc-arm-none-eabi 15:10.3-2021.07-4, binutils 2.38-3ubuntu1+15build1, libnewlib 3.3.0-1.3), as is the cc crate (Cargo.lock) and the lwIP submodule -- so gcc was never the variable the standing rule blamed.

Reproducibility PROVEN after the fix: this host (/home/coin/watching-zenoh, its own CARGO_HOME, deploy/*/target) and the runner-path container (different CARGO_HOME, different CARGO_TARGET_DIR) both emit mcu-multicast-e2e thumbv7m text=50956. Different OS install, different paths -- same byte count.

The gate would have caught this defect at its origin.

carry_forward_bullets: R311y268 = the read-back round. THE LESSON: R311y267 fixed a real defect, shipped green, and STILL over-claimed -- it asserted six byte-identical axes from one container-verified target. Verifying the fix on the machine it was written for is not optional bookkeeping; it is what separates "the gate is green" from "the claim is true". Read the numbers BACK off the runner.

KNOWN RESIDUAL, carried: multicast thumbv7em-none-eabihf reads +4 B on the runner (51100) vs this host (51096). Cause is .text alignment jitter from cargo's path-derived crate metadata hash -- NOT a path-length leak (.rodata is byte-identical; --remap-path-prefix fully eliminated that term). 5 of 6 gated axes are +0 across environments. Do not "fix" it by rebasing the baseline to the runner's number; that would just move the 4 B to the local side.

IF IT EVER MATTERS: the only complete fix is building the footprint artifacts at a CANONICAL PATH (a containerised footprint build, which this session already prototyped -- an ubuntu:22.04 image at a fixed mount point reproduces the runner to the byte). Round 311y268.decision_summary: R311y268 -- the read-back round, and it caught R311y267 over-claiming. R311y267 shipped and WORKED: the hosted runner's Layer Q went green on the first attempt after ~20 red pushes, with qemu-demo x4 and multicast thumbv7m all reading +0 against the rebased baselines and the pin confirmed active on the runner (rustup: "overridden by /home/runner/work/watching-zenoh/watching-zenoh/rust-toolchain.toml"). But reading the runner's own numbers back -- rather than trusting the claim -- surfaced one axis that does NOT match: multicast thumbv7em-none-eabihf reads 51100 on the runner against 51096 here, a +4 B residual. R311y267 asserted the figures were "byte-identical on this host and on the runner"; that assertion was extrapolated from ONE container-verified target (thumbv7m) onto all six, and it is false for thumbv7em-hf. Frozen-ledger: R311y267's body stands, this entry corrects it. ROOT-CAUSED, not waved through: a container at the HOST path reproduces 51096 and the same container at the RUNNER path reproduces 51100, so the residual is genuinely path-correlated -- but an ELF diff of the two (Q.5 artifacts, after first discovering the on-disk binary was Q.6's loopback-multicast variant overwriting the same path) shows .rodata BYTE-IDENTICAL and the entire 4 B living in .text. So the path-LENGTH term -- the 380 B one that caused the incident -- really is fully eliminated by --remap-path-prefix; what remains is .text alignment jitter, because cargo derives each crate's metadata hash from its package PATH, which perturbs symbol hashes and hence padding. It is not proportional to path length (5 of the 6 gated axes are +0 across environments), it is 1.5% of the +/-256 B band, and eliminating it would require building at a canonical path (a containerised footprint build) -- disproportionate. CARRIED as a named residual, with the honest framing recorded where it will be read: "reproducible" does NOT mean "bit-identical" here; the unbounded term is gone, a few bytes of layout jitter are not.

carry_forward_bullets: R311y269 = the ordering-invariant fix. Q.6's loopback-multicast ELF no longer uplifts over Q.5's footprint artifact; it builds into its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR. THE MECHANISM WORTH REMEMBERING: cargo's FINAL binary path is keyed on (target dir, triple, profile, bin name) ONLY -- the feature set lives in the deps/<bin>-<hash> intermediate, and the last build hard-links over the same stable path. Any two lanes that build the same --bin with different features into the same target dir WILL clobber each other's artifact, silently.

THE PATTERN, third time this session: a gate that is correct only by an invariant nobody declared. R311y267 = a footprint number that depended on the build path; R311y268 = a claim that depended on one verified target out of six; R311y269 = a measurement that depended on lane ordering. Each was green. Prefer making the bad state unrepresentable over checking that it has not happened yet.

Round 311y269.decision_summary: R311y269 -- Layer Q.6's ELF stops overwriting Layer Q.5's footprint artifact, and the comment that claimed it never did is retracted. Q.6 (the loopback-multicast QEMU runtime proof) builds the SAME crate, triple, profile and --bin as Q.5 (the footprint artifact), differing only in --features loopback-multicast and WZ_LWIP_PORT. Cargo keys a binary's FINAL path on (target dir, triple, profile, bin name) ONLY: the feature set is hashed into the intermediate deps/<bin>-<hash>, and the last build then UPLIFTS (hard-links) over the same stable path. Demonstrated on disk -- two feature-hashed intermediates coexist in deps/ while the final path shares an inode with whichever built last, and after a full Layer Q that is always Q.6's (bss 287244, against the footprint bin's 272268). Q.6's own comment asserted "a SEPARATE ELF ... so the Q.5 baseline stays byte-identical"; the ELF was never separate. THE MEASUREMENT WAS NEVER WRONG -- Q.5 gates immediately after its own build, before Q.6 runs -- but that made the gate's correctness rest on LANE ORDERING, an invariant nothing enforced and nothing stated: a future round reordering the lanes, or footprinting anything after Q.6, would have silently measured the wrong binary. THE ATOM IS THE GATE, NOT THE WRITE. adminspace-write's F= is the `permissions.write` gate on the config-write PUT path (zenoh adminspace.rs:396, default-DENY per PermissionsConf), so a test that merely showed a write LANDING would witness the plumbing while saying nothing about the atom. In-memory BTreeMap mirror + write-through: put/delete serialize to a self-describing record (magic WZS1 + key + NTP64 time + zid + encoding + payload + FNV-1a checksum, all length fields u32), atomic-write via a process-unique .wztmp temp then rename, fsync the file (sync_all) before the rename and the directory after (delete fsyncs the dir after the unlink). Filenames are fixed-width (k + 16-hex FNV-1a of the key, _<n> probe on collision) with the full key stored IN the file, so an arbitrarily long key cannot overflow NAME_MAX; None (mount-root exact-prefix slot) -> the __root__ sentinel. open() rebuilds the mirror from file CONTENT, sweeps only our own .wztmp leftovers, ignores foreign files (never read, never deleted), and quarantines (rename .corrupt + log) our own unreadable/corrupt files while continuing to load the rest. get() -> &StoredData from the mirror; get_all_entries / delete / Inserted-vs-Replaced match MemoryStorage semantics exactly (no timestamp comparison in the bare backend). Round 311y285.decision_summary: R311y285 -- api-compat-pico R1 IMPL-review fixes (§5.27). A 3-agent independent adversarial IMPL review of R311y284 (memory-safety/UB, ABI-fidelity vs ~/zenoh-pico, correctness/integration/honesty), arbitrated by direct source read + an empirical test. The most damaging flagged item -- "z_put from inside a subscriber callback panics on Handle::block_on and poisons the driver mutex, killing the session" -- is REFUTED empirically: a new echo test publishes from within the callback and the sample is delivered; the reviewer traced pico's scouting/response send_blocking(block_on) path, but the unicast pub path enqueues via the writer channel (the same path the in-runtime drive loop uses, which is why it never panics). Real fixes applied: (1) SessionState::close now uses tokio Notify::notify_one instead of notify_waiters -- a CONFIRMED lost-wakeup hang, since the drive task parks its .notified() waiter only after z_open returns, so a fast z_close/z_session_drop could drop the signal and block on join() forever on a healthy link; notify_one stores a permit so the shutdown is never lost. (2) The outbound C subscriber callback is now wrapped in catch_unwind so a panicking callback cannot unwind across the extern "C" boundary and tear down the drive thread. (3) z_open always-initializes its *zs out-param before any fallible work (pico contract). (4) Nine compile-time size_of static_asserts turn the byte-match claim into a build-enforced gate. (5) The wz api-compat-pico feature now also enables runtime-tokio, so the runtime-XOR compile_error fires for api-compat-pico + runtime-coop (previously it silently linked both runtimes). Round 311y294.decision_summary: R311y294 -- api-compat-pico R3a review remediation: the 3-agent IMPL review of R311y292 returned MUST-REVISE from all three lenses (unsafe-soundness / pico-faithfulness / SSOT-structure), and this round closes every finding plus corrects two FALSE claims R311y292 froze into the ledger. Direct read arbitrated throughout, and it overruled a reviewer once. THE ROOT PATTERN across the findings: R3a stated correct principles and then did not apply them -- the reviewers' phrase, and it holds. FIXED HERE. (1) FIDELITY, the big one: pico ENFORCES zenoh's reply-subset-of-query contract -- `!query->_anyke && !_z_declared_keyexpr_intersects(&query->_key, keyexpr)` -> _Z_ERR_KEYEXPR_NOT_MATCH (src/net/primitives.c:437-440) -- while R311y292's comment asserted the OPPOSITE ("pico lets the queryable pass any keyexpr") and forwarded any key with Z_OK. Now enforced. The `_anyke` half needed no upstream change once read properly: it is not a wire field but a SELECTOR PARAMETER (Z_SELECTOR_QUERY_MATCH "_anyke", api/constants.h:18) -- the sender appends it when accept_replies==Z_REPLY_KEYEXPR_ANY (codec/message.c:399-423), reception forces _implicit_anyke=false (codec/message.c:488-490), so the responder derivation collapses to `_anyke = _z_parameters_has_anyke(parameters)` (net/query.h:104), and QueryView::parameters() already carries them. pico's boundary-checked parse is ported verbatim (query_params.c:46-70). (2) The related z_query_reply_del STRING-EQUALITY reject was the wildcard-match-by-equality anti-pattern breaking the COMMON case (a wildcard queryable's query key is a PATTERN), and R311y292 dressed it as a "named divergence" whose stated cost was FALSE -- the reviewer proved the codec arm needs NO change, so wz-session-core gained send_reply_keyed_del + the ReplyOut::reply_keyed_del default (~10 lines, the Del-arm mirror of the Put arm's long-existing keyed family). It was a cost-deferral wearing a divergence's clothes; the seam is built and the divergence is GONE. (3) SOUNDNESS made mechanical: queryable_options now pins Locality::Remote. Locality::Any::allows_local() is TRUE (locality.rs:70-72), so an Any queryable would have made `unsafe impl Sync for CQueryClosure` FALSE the moment R3b's z_get lands with default locality -- a C-thread get would drain a local queryable job on the C thread while a drive thread ran call on another face, the exact unsound-Sync bug R311y288 fixed on the publish plane. R311y292's faces.rs doc argued FOR Any in the same commit whose Sync impl depended on local never happening. Remote is also pico-FAITHFUL: Z_FEATURE_LOCAL_QUERYABLE defaults to 0 (CMakeLists.txt:353). (4) The moved options->attachment was LEAKED and silently dropped (z_bytes_* IS exported, so a C program can build one) -- now consumed on every path and carried via ReplyOut::reply_keyed_attached. (5) Two more FALSE comments corrected: a NULL reply keyexpr does NOT mean "reply under the query's key" (pico has no null handling and SEGFAULTS) -- now a defined Z_ERR_NULL; and congestion_control's default is Z_CONGESTION_CONTROL_BLOCK=1 (api.c:2118,2181), not 0 (=DROP). (6) The valid/AtomicBool tripwire is REMOVED: its doc claimed multi-threaded C while the sibling UnsafeCell doc claimed pico's single-thread contract -- mutually exclusive anchors -- and with a callback-scoped marshal the flag can never usefully fire, since after the frame dies READING it is the use-after-free it meant to catch. It documented a protection that did not exist. (7) z_query_accepts_replies EXPORTED (it is the _anyke accessor governing #1, and was missing); z_query_source_info disclosed as withheld (needs the source-info family). DIRECT READ OVERRULED THE REVIEWER on z_queryable_id: it is #if defined(Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API) (primitives.h:2884) which defaults 0 (CMakeLists.txt:316), so a default build has no such symbol and it is NOT a missing export. (8) SSOT: session_state deduplicated into session.rs (it cast types owned by neither pubsub nor query); CClosure/CQueryClosure unified onto ONE generic ffi::CClosure<C> owning the drop-once Drop, with Sync deliberately NOT blanket-implemented so each plane still writes its own proof and R3b's reply plane cannot inherit one silently. (9) NO-FLAKY-EVER: the wire test's 300ms-sleep + single-query bet replaced by the sibling pubsub_roundtrip's bounded convergence loop (a get is idempotent, so re-asking is convergence on declaration propagation, not a retry-pass); it now finishes in 0.10s instead of always burning 5.00s. Round 311y295.decision_summary: R311y295 -- correct R268's stale cancel-safety rationale on drive_session_until_terminal. DOC-only; no code, no behavior, no inventory change. Surfaced by the R3b DESIGN review and then arbitrated by direct read, which went FURTHER than the review did. R268 removed the per-iteration on_tick hook and justified it two ways: (a) YAGNI -- every caller passed a no-op, so it was dead surface; (b) a HAZARD -- "sub-second sweep cadence belongs in a peer task that does not race poll_and_dispatch_one (which is not cancel-safe for length-prefixed drivers -- cancelling between the u16 length read and the payload read drops captured bytes)". Reason (a) stands and is untouched. Reason (b) is FALSE as of R311et and is corrected. Two independent falsifiers, both direct-read: (1) the ONE length-prefixed driver was FIXED -- R311et hoisted the partial-read buffers into &mut self (ReadState, lib.rs:1321-1339) over cancel-safe AsyncReadExt::read, and its own doc (lib.rs:1309-1318) names R264's "sub-second sweep cadence inside drive_session_until_terminal race-cancelled poll_and_dispatch_one 10x/s" as the fixture that surfaced it -- so the hazard R268 cites is precisely the hazard R311et closed, and two files in one crate have contradicted each other since; (2) NO OTHER driver is length-prefixed -- udp_pipeline:179 / ws_pipeline:138 / quic_datagram_pipeline:127 are datagram flows with no reassembly (ws's own comment says "datagram flow, no length-prefix reassembly"), serial_pipeline:282-288 documents its own cancel-safety ("Cancel-safe: the only .await is the single read... a dropped read consumes no bytes"), and quic_pipeline:102 delegates inward -- so the clause never applied to them at all. This is stronger than the review's position, which conservatively verified only TCP and proposed relying on capi-pico being TCP-only as containment-by-convention; direct read shows no containment is needed because the hazard class is empty. Also recorded: cancellation is neither new nor hypothetical -- this loop's own tokio::select! (session_glue.rs:811-867) ALREADY drops an in-flight poll_and_dispatch_one on every lease/keepalive wake, so a finer wake deadline changes that cancellation's FREQUENCY, not its correctness. WHY THIS IS WORTH A ROUND rather than a comment fixed in passing: the stale prose was not inert. It had already propagated -- it shaped this session's own R3b carry ("poll_and_dispatch_one is not cancel-safe, so do not just add a select! arm"), steering the next round away from the correct shape toward a sweep task that would be UNSOUND for a C-ABI callback context. A false rationale in a doc that a future round must consult is a trap, and it fires exactly when someone trusts the codebase. R268's live clause ("can re-introduce a similar hook when an actual consumer materialises") is preserved and now points a future consumer at folding its deadline into the loop's existing wake min.

carry_forward_bullets: R311y296 = api-compat-pico R3b (get), the last of the R3 split. R1 (binary drop-in pub/sub) + R2 (non-blocking multi-peer listener) + R3a (queryable) + R3b (get) are all BUILT and 3-agent-IMPL-reviewed. The api-compat-pico TRACK's core is now closed; what remains on it is the withheld set below, not a missing plane.

NEXT (highest value, design-review-first): wz-CORE consolidation. The inventory's query-consolidation atom is active and, until this round, claimed C=indep reply dedup -- a behaviour NO code implements. wz only transmits the Q_C wire ext. pico's LATEST suppresses the per-reply callback entirely, dedups by keyexpr keeping the newest timestamp, and flushes at the last final (query.c:143-181, 239-247), and AUTO resolves to LATEST absent a _time= selector, so this is the DEFAULT get path: pico delivers ONE reply where wz delivers two. This is NOT a capi-pico gap -- Session::query already takes with_consolidation, so wz's own Rust API is equally unfaithful, and the fix belongs in ReplyRegistry (where pico puts it). Blocked on 2 real core seams: (1) a ReplyView TIMESTAMP -- the wire decode has it and discards it (reply.rs, `timestamp: _`) -- without which "keep the newest" is undecidable; (2) a BoundedVec-safe per-pending reply cache the no_std MCU profile can carry. Under the Arc-refcount completion design the flush must run in a Drop that fires `call` for each cached reply BEFORE drop(context). MONOTONIC is NOT part of this (pico's drop flag gates only its cache, never the callback -- wz matches). Do NOT bolt this onto the binding.

A3 grammar note for that round: query-consolidation stays `active` (the Q_C ext IS a real cfg knob, so invariant #3 holds) -- the grammar cannot express "active but half-built" (PARTIAL requires reserved, and reserved requires zero cfg sites). If that is judged a real gap in the model, it is a separate audit round, not a status hack.

R3b's own NAMED DIVERGENCES (re-openable): (a) consolidation apply-half, above. (b) The owned-reply family (z_reply_clone / _take_from_loaned) -- withheld so a channel-based get fails at LINK rather than silently dropping replies; needs the same retained-responder seam the owned-QUERY family needs. (c) z_reply_err_encoding -- needs the encoding family. (d) The querier family (z_declare_querier / z_querier_get) -- NOT a bound get: pico's _z_declare_querier emits a Declare(DeclareQuerier) that wz has no path for, so mapping it onto a repeated z_get would produce a querier that never declares. (e) congestion_control / priority / is_express on a get -- pico maps them to a _z_n_qos_t on the Request; wz's QueryOptions has no QoS arm. (f) An out-of-enum consolidation int: pico emits Q_C with the raw byte (its != DEFAULT predicate can never elide for a get, since AUTO is already resolved away), wz elides -- garbage input, not worth an upstream raw-byte escape hatch.

INHERITED, unfixed, and named: free_port() TOCTOU in the capi-pico tests (bind :0, read the port, drop, re-bind). Same pattern as pubsub_roundtrip.rs:89, so R3b inherits rather than introduces it -- but the repo rule is no-flaky-ever and this is the one genuinely nondeterministic thing in the suite. A real fix is a shared port allocator or open-retry, crate-wide.

LESSON (durable): a DESIGN review can be right about the mechanism and still incomplete. The settled R3b plan said "fold the reply deadline into the drive loop's wake min" -- necessary but NOT sufficient, because the loop is normally PARKED in select! on the previous wake and never re-reads the deadline. A deadline that can be revised asynchronously needs a revision SIGNAL; that is the missing half of the mechanism, not an optimisation. The test caught it at 3.11s, matching the predicted keepalive cadence to within noise. Falsify every gate.

THE CORRECTION, and it is the important half: R311y299's decision/carry asserted that keyexpr-includes' reason is FALSE -- "no internal consumer yet" against "6+ live consumers (linkstate_forward.rs:1550, router_forward.rs:4816, ...)". THAT ASSERTION IS ITSELF FALSE, and the reason is CORRECT. The atom's cfg gates TWO functions in keyexpr_match.rs: keyexpr_includes_target (:433) and keyexpr_includes_patterns (:567). The reason's C= clause NAMES keyexpr_includes_patterns specifically, and that function has ZERO src consumers (2 test sites) -- "no internal consumer yet (exposed+tested)" is precisely true of the function it names. The 13 src consumers are of the OTHER function, keyexpr_includes_target. The error was a loose `grep keyexpr_includes` that conflated the two without reading which symbol the C= clause binds to -- i.e. exactly the violation of [[feedback-claim-binds-to-atom-code]] that R311y299 itself shipped a memory about, committed in the same session. CONSEQUENCE for the headline number: R311y299's "2 of 7 stale = 29% error rate" is WRONG; only storage-aligner is stale, so it is 1 of 7 = ~14%. storage-aligner's staleness is RE-CONFIRMED at symbol precision (both named residuals are done: `pub mod storage_aligner_service` exported at wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs:1105 = 1178 lines with `pub struct AlignerService`, plus a storage_aligner_convergence_e2e.rs; facade forward present at wz/Cargo.toml:645). WHY THE THESIS SURVIVES AND IS STRENGTHENED, NOT WEAKENED: three INDEPENDENT parties -- the implementing agent and BOTH adversarial review agents (design-scope and whole-session) -- graded keyexpr-includes identically wrong, each by the same loose grep, and the whole-session reviewer offered it as independently "confirmed". 3 of 3 failed on the FIRST atom examined. So the danger is not merely that reason prose rots; it is that GRADING reason prose requires binding to the exact symbol its C= names, and a majority of careful readers do not do that unprompted. A prose-driven mass re-tag would therefore have been MORE dangerous than R311y299 estimated, not less -- the corrected 14% is a measure of prose staleness, while the 3-of-3 misgrade is a measure of AUDITOR error, which is the compounding one and which no amount of review consensus catches (consensus was the thing that was wrong). R311y317 -- a REAL wire-observable gate hole, found by testing y316's own carry
instead of trusting it, and closed. Three atoms (query-target /
query-consolidation / query-timeout) were emitting their wire bytes in builds
that do not contain them. MEASURED, not argued: with each atom off, assigning
the `pub` field on QueryOptions -- rather than calling the gated `with_*`
setter -- put Q_T (0x34, header 124->252), Q_C (0x23) and the timeout ext
(0x26, varint 1000) on the wire. `#[non_exhaustive]` blocks struct-literal
construction, NOT assignment onto a `QueryOptions::get()` value, so the
setter's body gate was never the enforcement point it was documented to be.
ROOT CAUSE, and it is structural rather than a per-slot oversight: the split is
exact. `build_request_query_with_meta` (session-core, the TX SSOT) cfg-gates 4
of 7 metadata slots -- value / source-info / attachment / selector-parameters --
and threads 3 ungated. Every gated one forwards to a same-named wz-session-core
feature; every ungated one (query-target / -consolidation / -timeout) is
runtime-tokio-TERMINAL, so session-core cannot name the atom, let alone gate it.
The runtime layer is the last hop that knows these three exist. THE TRAP I WOULD
HAVE WALKED INTO: gating only the wire threading fixes the bytes and leaves the
local ReplyRegistry deadline armed, because `Session::query` reads
`opts.timeout_ms` DIRECTLY at two sites that never touch `query_metadata()` --
and my wire-byte test would have gone GREEN while it happened. Two adversarial
reviews caught it independently; I then falsified it by hand (reverting only the
deadline half makes the wire assertion pass and the deadline assertion fail).
PRECEDENT, which I had backwards: I argued this against y316's BorrowedQuery
ruling. Review found y316 contains no such ruling, and that the governing
precedent is R311y308/y309 -- which adjudicated THIS EXACT SHAPE on the pubsub
side (an ungated pub-field `qos` reaching a subscriber / changing Frame count +
SN) and closed it with `metadata_gated!` + `push_metadata`. The query side never
followed. querier.rs even claimed it "mirrors push_metadata verbatim" -- a
fossil, false since y309. RETRACTED FROM y316: its carry (a) called
queryable.rs's ungated re-projection "the strongest remaining query-value gap".
It is not a gap: that file gates on query-queryable / transport-unicast only and
names NONE of the four metadata atoms -- OwnedQueryEvent relays all four
identically. It is a uniform relay design, not a query-value hole. I took one
reviewer's framing and froze it as fact; that is the same failure this round's
predecessors kept making.

R311y322 -- the whole-session review of R311y321 landed after y321 was frozen. It

and every finding below was verified by my own direct read before I acted on it.
THE BUG -- ConsolidatingSink consolidated Err replies. zenoh cannot, and does not
express that as a rule but as STRUCTURE: its consolidation match lives entirely
inside send_response's ResponseBody::Reply arm, while ResponseBody::Err is a
DISJOINT arm that calls callback.call(new_reply) directly. It could not
consolidate an Err if it tried -- Reply.result's Err variant is a bare
ReplyError { payload, encoding } with NO keyexpr, and the consolidation arms key
on result.unwrap().key_expr, unreachable for an Err by construction. wz cannot
borrow that structure: the wire dispatcher resolves keyexpr_literal BEFORE the
body match, so every InboundReply arm has a keyexpr and an Err arrives fully
cache-able. Consequences on the DEFAULT pico path (AUTO -> LATEST), both
directions: against a stamped Put the Err failed displaces_cached and was
silently swallowed; against an unstamped Put it won the tie and EVICTED the good
reply. Guarded now -- ReplyKind::Err forwards before the mode match and never
caches. WHAT HID IT: my own comment, which asserted an Err "ties with an
unstamped Put and is forwarded -- matching zenoh, which runs every reply through
the same match". zenoh does not run every reply through the same match. The
comment reasoned from the tie rule and never read the upstream arm split, and
mod consolidating_sink_tests had no Err test at all -- its only fixture was
fn put(). A claim I wrote became the reason I did not look.

drops its whole cache" -- FALSE. sweep_timed_out fires the swept entry's

reviewer probe measured it. y321 BUILT the timeout flush and then booked it as

and the write. Read before editing, cited after: the exact R311y309 lesson, in
the round that quotes it.

because it names no feature profile. The real figures are 1137 --all-features

R311y323 -- the Err("Timeout") synthesis, y322's carry item (1). Built on BOTH

WHAT THE CARRY GOT RIGHT AND WHAT IT MISSED. Right: only the synthesis was
missing (y321 had already built the flush without noticing, and y322 corrected
that). Missed: the LIVELINESS sibling. zenoh's timeout arm is TWO arms -- the
z_get task off state.queries and a twin off state.liveliness_queries, both
calling back Err(ReplyError::new("Timeout", Encoding::ZENOH_STRING)). wz mirrors
the split exactly (ReplyRegistry vs LivelinessGetRegistry, two tables, two
sweeps), so fixing only z_get would have manufactured the asymmetry this session
keeps catching in other people's work. Both legs land here.
THE ASYMMETRY THAT WAS ALREADY IN THE TREE, unnamed by any round: the RELAY leg
already emitted the Err. synthesize_expired_query_returns builds
build_response_err_empty(rid, b"Timeout") toward the inbound face on a reaped
branch and cites zenoh's QueryCleanup::run in its own doc. So a wz querier
BEHIND a wz router got Err("Timeout") on a relayed timeout while the SAME
querier timing out locally got a bare final -- one atom, two legs, opposite
behaviour. I went looking for a residual to justify keeping PARTIAL and found
instead that the residual I feared was already paid, and that the hole was on
the leg I was fixing.
THE SEAM. ReplySink gains on_timeout(rid) with a DEFAULT of synthesize-then-
final. The default is the whole contract for a stateless sink -- the AP closure
adapter, an MCU closed enum, the liveliness sinks -- which is why this is a
defaulted method and not a breaking addition. ConsolidatingSink OVERRIDES it,
because ORDER is observable: zenoh flushes the Latest cache BEFORE the error
(data first, then the reason the stream stopped), and the default's
on_reply->on_final would emit the error FIRST and the cached data after it, so a
caller treating an error as terminal would lose data it had already earned.
flush_latest is extracted so the normal-final path and the timeout path cannot
drift apart on the Latest condition.
NO GATE, AND NONE IS POSSIBLE. wz-session-core does not declare query-timeout
(measured via cargo: it and query-consolidation are both wz-runtime-tokio
TERMINAL features), so the sweep cannot gate on it where it lives. It does not
need to: the runtime gates by ARMING -- effective_timeout_ms() reads 0 with the
feature off, deadline_ms stays None, and the sweep loop is empty by
construction. The gate is the arming, not the sweep. Same shape as y321's
consolidation wiring: gate at the runtime, drive session-core by DATA.
ENCODING -- it reads like an inconsistency and is faithful mirroring. The
client-side synthesis carries ZENOH_STRING (packed_id 2: zenoh's ZENOH_STRING is
{id:1,schema:None} and wz packs id<<1|schema_bit); the router leg carries
err_body's encoding:None. zenoh does exactly this -- ReplyError::new(.., 
Encoding::ZENOH_STRING) on the client, Encoding::default() in QueryCleanup. wz
reproduces the upstream's own inconsistency rather than tidying one leg into a
divergence.
FALSIFICATION EARNED ITS KEEP AGAIN. Neutering the trait DEFAULT left all 12
tests GREEN -- because every test drove ConsolidatingSink, which overrides it,
and nothing exercised the default the LIVELINESS leg actually rides. That is the
y321 Err bug's shape verbatim: one fixture shape, and the arm it never builds is

WHAT I PROPOSED AND WHY IT WAS WRONG. query-queryable: I read session/mod.rs's
R311y321 note assigning the loopback selection gap to "the query-target atom's
PARTIAL residual" and concluded `complete` was not this atom's problem. That
note names only HALF the predicate. zenoh's rule is (queryable.complete ||
target != AllComplete): `target` is the REQUESTER-side operand and is
query-target's; `queryable.complete` is the RESPONDER-side operand, which is
verbatim this atom's C= ("indep responder-side"). Plumbing target alone could
never close it -- the predicate would have no `complete` to read. Measured:
wz-session-core/src/query.rs contains ZERO occurrences of `complete`;
QueryableOptions::complete reaches the wire declare (mod.rs:2999/:3015) and never
the local registry, so a SessionLocal queryable with .with_complete(true) is a
SILENT NO-OP. pico keeps the sibling wz drops -- _z_session_queryable_t stores
`bool _complete` ADJACENT to _allowed_origin (session.h:129/130) and reads it
locally (filtering.c:148, queryable.c:189/:286). A prose sentence assigning the
gap elsewhere is what would have let this atom be tagged COMPLETE with its own
C= surface unbuilt.

query-get: two independent blockers, neither mine. (1) Its OFF arm is
COMPILE-ONLY. Exactly three not(query-get) sites exist and all three are the
production arms; ZERO tests carry that gate. On the `queryable-only` lane -- the
very subset where this atom is off -- SEVEN sibling atoms' OFF guards run
behaviourally and its three do not. The standard is the repo's own
(session_glue.rs:1445-1452, R311hw/R311hx): a compile/footprint proof "does NOT
prove the consumer-side signature-stable emit path BEHAVES correctly when off".
(2) A homeless RX default divergence, the LEG A shape that refuted query-timeout
at y325: zenoh defaults accept_replies to MatchingQuery and states it as a
GUARANTEE (session.rs:1181); pico agrees (constants.h:291). wz NATIVE has no

bullets name the failing test and the runs grepped `FAILED|panicked at`, which IS

Round 311y334.decision_summary:
R311y334 -- wire queryable.complete into the LOCAL query dispatch, closing
query-queryable's primary C= blocker (residual 1) and query-target's loopback
residual; a review-found feature-gate bug on the new loopback leg was caught and
fixed before landing.

THE GAP. options.complete reached only the wire declare (the QueryableInfo ext)
and NEVER the local dispatch table: Queryable<C> stored id/pattern/allowed_origin
/sink with no `complete`, and fire_matching_queryables selected purely on
matches(keyexpr, is_remote). A SessionLocal queryable declared .with_complete(true)
was a silent no-op. Symmetrically, build_loopback_query DROPPED the query target,
so an AllComplete self-get fired every matching local queryable, complete or not.

UPSTREAM, read directly (zenoh 1.5.0 src/api/session.rs:2427-2431, handle_query):
the filter is `(origin==Any || local==(origin==SessionLocal)) && (queryable.complete
|| target != AllComplete) && key_expr.intersects(..)`. The `local` flag gates ONLY
the locality conjunct; the completeness conjunct applies on the loopback path too,
and the SessionLocal call site passes the caller's real target. So the old loopback
drop was NOT faithful -- both operands are real on one host: `complete` is the
RESPONDER-side operand (query-queryable's C=), `target` the REQUESTER-side operand
(query-target's).

THE FIX. Queryable<C> stores `complete`; register_sink (the SSOT) threads it, and

Round 311y337.decision_summary:
R311y337 -- residual (5) closed: a RESOLVABLE query that matches ZERO queryables
now gets its ResponseFinal. query-queryable reaches COMPLETE.

THE DEFECT, found by the R311y336 review and confirmed by direct read of all four
legs. `dispatch_messages` staged the stream terminator only `if matched > 0`. But
`matched == 0` arises three ways and only two of them legitimately owe nothing: a
non-Query body, and an un-resolvable keyexpr. The third -- a resolvable query that
simply matched NOBODY -- silently inherited "owe nothing", and the requester was
left to wait out its own timeout for an answer that was never coming.

BOTH UPSTREAMS TERMINATE IT, and their structure is the fix's design. zenoh's wire
entry `Primitives::send_request` (src/api/session.rs:2769-2792) reaches
`handle_query` ONLY for a resolvable Query body: a non-Query body never enters the
match arm, and an unresolvable wire_expr takes `Err(err) => error!("Received Query
for unknown key_expr")` and returns. Inside `handle_query`, `QueryInner` is built
WITHOUT consulting the queryable set (:2440-2450); only the callback loop is gated
on `!queryables.is_empty()` (:2451), so a zero-match query never moves the inner
into a `Query`, drops it at scope end, and `impl Drop for QueryInner`
(src/api/queryable.rs:75-83) sends the ResponseFinal. pico states it outright:
`if (qle_nb == 0) { ...; _z_session_send_reply_final(zn, qid, is_local); return
_Z_RES_OK; }` (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/session/queryable.c:246-252) -- and it passes
`is_local`, so BOTH legs owe it. So the debt is "entered handle_query", NOT the
match count.

AND WZ'S OWN TWO LEGS DISAGREED -- the sibling tell that keeps finding real defects
here. The loopback leg already emitted `deliver_local_final` unconditionally; only
the wire leg keyed on matches. The loopback agreed with both upstreams; the wire leg
was the wrong one.

THE FIX. `dispatch_request` returns `DispatchOutcome { dispatched, matched }` and
the Final keys on `dispatched` -- wz's boundary equivalent of entering
`handle_query`. The two `NOT_DISPATCHED` returns map 1:1 onto zenoh's two
pre-`handle_query` exits. Every path that reaches the table and then fires nothing
-- empty table, locality filter, the y334 completeness filter, a non-intersecting
keyexpr, a chunk overflow -- lives INSIDE `fire_matching_queryables`, i.e. after
`dispatched = true`, so all of them owe a Final; that matches zenoh exactly, where
all three filter conjuncts run inside `handle_query` after the inner is built.
`Option<usize>` was rejected: it is `#[must_use]` and would have churned ~35
statement-position test call sites; a plain outcome struct does not.

R311y334 WIDENED THIS HOLE and that is why it surfaced now: the completeness filter
manufactures `matched == 0` on an ordinary path (ask AllComplete while only an
incomplete queryable is registered). A round closing one gap opened the road into
another.

TWO TESTS PINNED THE DEFECT and both were inverted:
`..._skips_final_when_no_queryable_matched` asserted `finals.is_empty()`, and
`..._emits_final_for_each_matched_request` asserted "unmatched rid 12 dropped".
`..._skips_final_when_keyexpr_unresolvable` was NOT touched -- it guards a real
arm that owes nothing, and it still passes under the reverted predicate, which is
what proves the two categories are distinguished rather than merged.

TWO INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWERS, arbitrated by direct read. Both clean. The
defect hunt found no double-Final: the four Final producers are disjoint (the wire
push is once per Request; the two drains empty the SAME Vec so the second sees it
empty; the loopback is requester-side; the router is a separate plane with its own
pending table), and `expected_finals` still matches the producer count. The COMPLETE
hunt could not refute the tag: wz's `Queryable` fields are 1:1 with zenoh's
`QueryableState` and pico's `_z_session_queryable_t`, the locality conjunct is
equivalent by truth table, replay re-stamps `complete`, and post-y337 the wire and
loopback legs agree.

THE REVIEW ALSO CORRECTED MY OWN PROSE, twice. (a) The reason credited only C1j for
this atom's hosted proofs and omitted C1e -- which matters, because wz-session-core
