Round 311y338.decision_summary:
R311y338 -- R311y337's fix broke an e2e fixture, because the fixture was built
on the defect. Rebuilt it on a peer that owns its own silence, and the rebuild
found a second, subtler version of the same mistake in my own design.

WHAT HAPPENED. y337 made a resolvable zero-match query get its ResponseFinal.
The pre-push gate then failed Layer E on
wz_ap_demo_query_timeout_fires_final_callback: "FINAL fired too early
(50.5ms)". R264 had built the --query-timeout-ms e2e on an acceptor that
declared no queryable, and documented the mechanism in its own header:
"Inbound Request(Query) has no matching responder, so no Response/ResponseFinal
goes back on the wire ... The Query effectively sinks at the peer." That was
never a property of the acceptor's configuration. It was y337's DEFECT. The
fixture had been standing on it for ~70 rounds, which is precisely why the
defect survived: a test depended on it.

THE RULE THIS ROUND BUYS: A FIXTURE'S PRECONDITION MUST BE OWNED BY THE
FIXTURE. If it is instead an emergent property of the code under test, the day
that code is correctly fixed is the day the test starts lying. R264's
precondition ("no reply ever arrives") was emergent, so the correct fix
inverted it.

THE REBUILD. `wz-e2e-silent-peer` -- a new wz-e2e-* test double whose only job
is to never answer. It completes the handshake, stays transport-alive
(keepalive / lease are driven, so the peer is UP and merely mute -- exactly
what a query timeout defends against), and hands inbound events to nobody. The
three rejected alternatives, each for the same reason: SIGSTOP-ing the acceptor
puts the silence in the OS's hands (racy, Unix-only); an unresolvable-keyexpr
peer puts it in the resolve path's current behaviour (rots when that changes);
a query-queryable-OFF wz-ap-demo puts it in a feature combination AND enshrines
a zenoh divergence as the reference fixture. All three borrow their silence.

THEN THE REBUILD FAILED THE SAME WAY, and this is the round's real finding. The
first cut leaned on the double's MANIFEST: omit codec-response /
codec-response-final / query-queryable and answering is "unrepresentable by
construction". `cargo tree -p wz-e2e-silent-peer -e features` agreed -- no
response plane. The e2e still failed at 50 ms. Cause, measured: I had built it
with `cargo build -p wz-ap-demo -p wz-e2e-silent-peer`, and CARGO UNIFIES
FEATURES ACROSS PACKAGES BUILT IN ONE INVOCATION. The double linked a `wz`
carrying the demo's response plane and answered the query. A manifest describes
a PACKAGE; unification is a property of the BUILD GRAPH. My "unrepresentable"
claim was true only of a solo build -- and the fixture would have gone green as
a happy-path test the first time someone folded the two builds into one line:
the same rot, one level up, in the very crate built to prevent it. (This is also
the project's own `-p A -p B` trap, which I had filed under `--all-features`
only.)

SO THE SILENCE MOVED INTO CODE THE DOUBLE OWNS: `run_silent_acceptor_e2e`
(wz-e2e-harness) drives the FSM with a deliberately empty dispatch closure, so
inbound events reach no application plane whatever the build graph enables.
PROVEN unification-proof: the e2e passes under the adversarial
`cargo build -p wz-ap-demo -p wz-e2e-silent-peer` that defeated the manifest.
The manifest's omission stays as defence in depth, and now says so instead of
claiming to be the guarantee.

ALSO PINNED: the two `DispatchOutcome::NOT_DISPATCHED` arms now have their own
registry-level proofs, so "a non-Query body / an unresolvable keyexpr owes
nothing" is no longer load-bearing for an e2e timeout fixture. The
non-Query-body arm had only a callback-level check; it now has a Final-level
one, completing the truth table: dispatched => exactly one Final whatever
`matched` is; not dispatched => none, ever.

AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN DIAGNOSIS. I first blamed y337 for the Layer E
failure and said so. A bisect in an isolated worktree refuted it: e3926f3,
0ab8657 (y334), 658fac0 (y336) and 99073f7 (y337) ALL pass the original fixture.
y337 did break it in the pre-push run (a wz-ap-demo acceptor legitimately
answers post-y337) -- but by the time I re-ran it, MY OWN unified build was
producing the identical 50 ms symptom from a different cause. Two causes, one
timing signature, and I had asserted the wrong one. Measure per commit; a
matching symptom is not a matching cause.

Round 311y339.decision_summary:
R311y339 -- the FIXTURE RULE audit y338 owed. Three parallel sweeps over the
whole fixture surface (108 e2e files, the 8 wz-e2e-* doubles, the unit and
test-support crates) found it CLEAN of R264's shape. The round's finding is
elsewhere: a claim family that has been retracted three times still had a live
member, sitting in the doc of the test that drives the very method where one of
those retractions landed.

THE AUDIT. R264's tell was never "depends on an absence" -- it was a fixture
header that states current wz behaviour as a RULE and rests its design on it.
Swept for exactly that. The a-m range is structurally incapable of the defect:
28 of its 32 files are layer3_* codec-parity DIFFERENTIALS, where an absence is
either fixture-constructed or the assertion itself, so a broken precondition
points at the disagreement instead of fabricating silence. The w-prefixed e2e
(where absence-shaped preconditions can exist at all) are clean -- every
negative arm gates on a POSITIVE witness first. The doubles are clean;
wz-e2e-silent-peer is the reference shape.

FOUR HYPOTHESES OF MY OWN, ALL REFUTED -- recorded so nobody re-asks them.
(1) The interest plane is the query plane's SIBLING, so it should carry y337's
zero-match-Final defect. It does not: router_forward.rs proves "empty current
dump -> only the terminating DeclareFinal", and local_token.rs stages the Final
OUTSIDE the match loop, documented "even when no token matched". y337's defect
did not generalise. (2) respond_to_interest_borrowed drops its Final under a
full staging buffer (`let _ = pending.push(Final)`). Unreachable:
MAX_LOCAL_TOKENS=8 + 1 <= MAX_PENDING_DECLARES=32, and every drain site drains
per EVENT -- one chain per window. The `let _` is dead defence. (3)
link_emitter_b6's pass-with-warning skip is vacuous in CI. False: the `ci` job
builds sce-codegen before Layer C1, and no sce-less job runs that crate. (4)
Another lane carries y338's `-p A -p B` unification trap. False: no multi-`-p`
single invocation exists in run-ci.sh or ci.yml.

WHAT THE SWEEP FOUND, and it is not a fixture. reply.rs's sweep_timed_out test
doc said "`effective_timeout_ms()` reads 0 with the feature off, so
`deadline_ms` stays None and this sweep sees nothing". y325 RETRACTED that exact
generalisation -- inside ReplyRegistry::sweep_timed_out, the very method the
test drives -- and named the shape: "true of the path the author was looking at,
false of its siblings". The retraction then landed only on the code y325 was
reading, and missed the test doc in the same file. The claim is false:
`register` is pub and ungated, and wz-ap-demo arms `deadline_ms` straight off
`--query-timeout-ms` (runner.rs:278-287) carrying ZERO `feature =
"query-timeout"` sites. The family's four other members are healthy -- y326
corrected session/mod.rs and advanced_subscriber.rs, and querier.rs's own doc
records TWO prior retractions plus y318's warning that "a retraction lands where
the author is looking". The rule was written into the code and the copy was
still missed.

AND THE SIBLING ASYMMETRY IT LED TO. query_with_timeout_ms_is_silent_noop_*
argued "one wire-parity assertion is the complete guard", and its assert message
claimed "no local deadline is armed" while observing only the frame. Its own
pub-field twin, 40 lines down, refutes it in prose: "a wire-only fix leaves this
armed and the assertion above still passes -- so the wire check alone cannot
guard this atom". C1j's lane comment repeated the same argued coverage. Of the
three metadata twins ONLY query-timeout has a non-wire observable -- which is
precisely why only its twin had to argue, and it argued wrong. It now OBSERVES.

Round 311y341.decision_summary:
R311y341 -- y340 called the dropped DeclFinal "THE REAL DEFECT, OWED A ROUND".
It is not a defect. It is unreachable, and I found that out the only way that
would have worked: by trying to REPRODUCE it instead of arguing about it.

THE ROUND'S SHAPE. y339 refuted the dropped Final with bad reasoning. A reviewer
broke the reasoning and asserted the defect was real, with closed-form arithmetic
over quoted code (8 tokens x 4 Interests in one frame = 36 items > 32 slots) and
an explicit note that no repro was executed. y340 accepted it. y341 wrote the
repro FIRST, per the rule y340 itself had just banked -- and the test PASSED.
That is what exposed the truth. The arithmetic was right; the profile was wrong.

WHY IT CANNOT HAPPEN. `BoundedVec<T, N>` has two backings, and its own
`capacity()` doc says so: "Advisory on the `alloc` backing (AP may exceed it);
the hard limit `push` enforces on the no-alloc backing."

- AP (`alloc`): the backing is `Vec<T>` and N is IGNORED -- `push` returns
  `Ok(())` unconditionally. Batching is real here (`dispatch_messages` threads
  one `&mut pending` across every Interest in a frame), so chains DO accumulate
  -- and nothing can ever be dropped, because there is no bound to hit.
- MCU (no-alloc): the backing is `heapless::Vec<T, N>` and N IS the hard limit --
  but `dispatch_messages` / `respond_to_interest` / the observer's fan are ALL
  `alloc`-gated. Nothing batches. The consumer drives
  `respond_to_interest_borrowed` per Interest; one chain is MAX_LOCAL_TOKENS + 1
  = 9 against 32. The only no-alloc caller in the tree,
  `deploy/mcu-noheap-probe`, answers a single Interest.

THE BATCHING AND THE HARD BOUND SIT ON OPPOSITE SIDES OF THE `alloc` CFG. The
profile that can overflow does not batch; the profile that batches cannot
overflow. Both the reviewer and I built a defect out of one profile's batching
and the other profile's bound.

THE UNIT WAS THE PROFILE. y340's own carry says "validate the bound against the
right UNIT" -- I banked that lesson and failed it again in the same hour, on the
same code, because I accepted a finding whose unit I had not checked. Three
strikes on one atom family: a per-frame buffer sized per-chain (y340), a
per-accessor gate labelled per-setter (y340), and now a cross-profile arithmetic
(y341). What broke the streak was not better reasoning. It was running the thing.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG -- THE DOCS THAT MISLED US BOTH. `caps.rs` justified
MAX_PENDING_DECLARES with "the buffer accumulates across the Interests in a
single poll batch, so the bound is sized generously". That sentence straddles two
profiles that never meet: the accumulation is the AP path, where the constant
bounds nothing at all, and the "generous" sizing implies a limit that only exists
on the profile with no accumulation. It is the sentence the reviewer quoted at me
as proof, and it was true of neither build. `respond_to_interest_borrowed`'s own
doc had the complementary half-truth -- "the bound is sized so a single
Interest's chain always fits" -- correct, but silent on the fact that a single
chain per buffer IS the contract, not an incidental margin. Both now state the
per-backing split, name the `let _ = push(Final)` as the swallow it is, and say
plainly that its unreachability is a property of the cfg split rather than a
guarantee: a future no-heap consumer that fans a frame's Interests through one
buffer breaks it silently, and should reserve the Final's slot before staging
tokens.

NO TEST SURVIVES THIS ROUND, deliberately. The repro I wrote passes under `alloc`
for a reason that has nothing to do with what it claims to test -- the bound it
names does not exist in the only profile where the test module compiles
(`--no-default-features --features liveliness-token` does not build: 96 errors,
the test module needs std). Keeping it would have been y339's vacuous assert

instead, which is where it is actually enforceable today.

Round 311y342.decision_summary:
R311y342 -- the user asked why I keep trying to prove things by READING code, and
why a test cannot confirm it outright. The question was right, and this round is
the answer: a real wire defect, found by reading, PROVEN by a failing test, and
fixed. First production behaviour change in four rounds.

THE DEFECT, and the test that proved it. wz emitted a keyexpr alias id that
NEITHER upstream can hold. zenoh types `DeclareKeyExpr.id` as `ExprId`, and
`pub type ExprId = u16` (zenoh-protocol core/wire_expr.rs); zenoh-pico's
`_z_decl_kexpr_t` holds `uint16_t _id`. wz's `send_declare_keyexpr` takes a u64
and validated only `== 0`. The codec carries the id as VLE u64 deliberately (the
shared wireexpr shape, per decl_kexpr.scxml), so an out-of-range id encodes
cleanly HERE and is structurally unreadable THERE.

Not argued -- measured. The new guard failed first, and its failure is the
evidence: `an alias id neither upstream can hold must not reach the wire: ()` --
`expect_err` panicking on `Ok(())` means `send_declare_keyexpr(65_536, ..)`
SUCCEEDED and put the frame on the wire. Then the gate, then green.

THE TELL WAS SIBLING ASYMMETRY. The id space has two ends. The lower one
(`== 0`) has had a gate AND a test since R300. The upper one had neither. And
after gating the declare half I swept the sibling again and found the SAME defect
unfixed in the retraction half: `send_undeclare_kexpr` emits without consulting
the mapping table (its own doc's "removing an absent id is a no-op" idempotence),
so gating declare never bounded it. It has no error channel, so its drop is
silent -- consistent with the contract that already drops its emit on a dead
link. Four tests: reject-too-wide + admit-u16::MAX, on both halves, so no
off-by-one hides in either.

FOUR OFF ARMS THAT ONLY PROSE DEFENDED. `decl_listener.rs` holds two listeners
whose feature-OFF arms are character-for-character identical
(`let _ = callback; Err(DeclListenerError::FeatureDisabled)`) and only the
subscriber one was ever pinned -- one file, two twins, one guarded. And

Round 311y344.decision_summary:
R311y344 -- the round set out to RATIFY a grammar widening and instead found the
machine underneath it broken. Three adversarial reviews killed the exemplar; then
measuring the machine's own output killed the machine. SIX distinct defects in
R311y343's atom<->test derivation, all live, all invisible, all one round old.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE, and this is the whole lesson: R311y343 shipped
atom_test_graph.py CALIBRATED -- "47 of 47 COMPLETE atoms pass" -- and that
calibration was TRUE the entire time the derivation was wrong. A gate that only
ever passes cannot tell a correct derivation from a broken one. Every one of the
six was found by measuring the OUTPUT against the source; not one was findable by
re-reading the code, which is exactly the claim R311y343 itself was built to
make about atoms, applied one level up to the gate that makes it.

THE SIX, each proven by a fixture that is RED on 940b710 and green now:
  1. A cfg on an enum VARIANT is not a cfg inside a body. The walk-back looked
     only for an enclosing `fn`, sailed past the `enum` that actually encloses
     the variant, and landed on the last fn before the type. Measured on the real
     tree: `transport-link-vsock` OWNED `with_quic` -- a fn gated by
     `#[cfg(feature = "transport-link-quic")]`, 95 lines earlier.
  2. Same for a struct-form variant (`Udp { socket: .. }`).
  3. A cfg'd `impl` block declares no name, so it is not an item either -- 42
     sites, the largest class. `#[cfg(feat)] impl UdpDriver` resolved to
     `send_declare_final`. `impl<T> Trait<T> for WsDriver<T>` resolved to `poll`,
     a method of the PREVIOUS impl block.
  4. `const` is both an item kind and an fn modifier. Read left-to-right,
     `pub const fn encode_keep_alive()` parsed as a const ITEM whose NAME is the
     keyword `fn` -- an owned "symbol" no test can ever name.
  5. A test module is not the TAIL of its file. The src arm took the FIRST
     `#[cfg(test)]` and harvested every identifier to EOF. 161 src files carry
     top-level PRODUCTION items after their first test module; wz-runtime-tokio/
     src/lib.rs donated 58 of them (including `pub mod vsock_pipeline`) and one
     file donated 171. Production code was reading as test evidence.
  6. A TEST THAT NEVER RUNS IS NOT A TEST. The reference arm never looked at
     `#[ignore]`. 78 of this tree's 332 test regions execute NOTHING and every
     one of them was supplying evidence. This repo has named that disease twice
     ("a proof that never runs is not a proof"; "a skip is green") and it was
     installed in the gate built to enforce it.

THE EXEMPLAR DIED FIRST, and it died the right way. The design retagged
`transport-link-vsock` UNVERIFIED on the strength of its reason -- "the backend
is genuinely built ... but the round-trip is #[ignore]d" -- reading that as a
pure LANE gap. A reviewer refuted it and direct read confirmed: `bind_locator`
returns `io::Result<TcpListener>` by signature and wires only `Proto::Tcp`
(session_open.rs:780/:789); the vsock arm returns `unsupported` (:826-829) in the
SAME words the design quoted to disqualify quic. vsock shares the accept-seam
residual, so "no code is missing" is false. The reason had not rotted in its
cites -- every line number was exact -- it rotted by OMISSION: R311y305 audited
vsock, quic and quic-datagram in one round, named the accept gap for two, and
left it out of the third. Only the SIBLING sweep catches that, and I did not do
one. The right discriminator was there all along and I reached past it: quic's
e2e RUNS (quic_e2e.rs:17 "Fully runnable (NO #[ignore])", C1ac at run-ci.sh:1127
passes no --ignored), which is why quic is not UNVERIFIED.

Round 311y345.decision_summary:
R311y345 -- the user asked whether the test cases for zenoh+pico FULL were all
in place. They were not, and the honest answer to why is that R311y339-y344 spent
SIX rounds on the audit machinery and none on the thing it audits. This round
stops describing the gap and starts closing it: two atoms move from "no foreign
witness at all" to proven, each by a test whose RED was demonstrated first.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT ACTUALLY SAID. `preset-ap-full` is 136 atoms, read from the
Cargo preset -- the SSOT -- rather than the store section, which says of itself
that it was "transcribed from Cargo preset-ap-full". FORTY of the 136 had zero
cross-impl proof: not scattered, but whole planes at once (all 8 locators, all 5
scouting atoms, 4 session extensions, the 3 access-* interceptors). Catalog-wide
the axis read proven=58 partial=31 unproven=71 against a denominator of 160, and
the corpus behind it was 78 files / 157 tests, of which only SIX witness zenohd.

TRANSPORT-KEEPALIVE -- the sibling-asymmetry tell, again. It had a dozen
host-side tests and zero foreign proof, while its codec twin `codec-keep-alive`
was proven against pico by layer3_keep_alive.rs's byte-parity. The BYTES were
checked against pico and the BEHAVIOUR never was -- and a KeepAlive that is
byte-perfect but emitted too late keeps nothing alive. The new test makes pico's
own lease timer the judge: the demo holds its burst 14s past Established, wider
than the 10s adopted lease, and a Put that still lands proves the KeepAlive held
the line open. Nothing in wz asserts it.

RED, and it was exact: with the emit suppressed, the demo's own log reads
`publisher_task holding the burst` at :21 and `session ended: Terminated` at :31
-- EXACTLY the 10s lease -- with `ActionTrace { .. send_keep_alive: 0 .. }`
naming the cause. Ten seconds of silence, and pico expired wz.

TRANSPORT-BATCHING -- COMPLETE on A3, and never once witnessed. Its A3 tag says
"a REAL measured TX buffer ... No residual"; its A4 line said unproven. That
combination is exactly what the north star turns on: the code is built, and
nobody had checked that the frame it emits is one a foreign peer can read. Not a
hypothetical -- wz's batcher is deliberately STRICTER than the pico primary it
mirrors (its own reason: pico "blind-appends mixed reliability" where wz enforces
zenoh's CurrentFrame/NewFrame homogeneity), so the two ends do NOT agree by
construction, which is the case only a real peer settles.

RED, and it VALIDATED THE ASSERTION'S SHAPE, which is the round's sharpest
result: dropping ONE byte from the flushed chain makes z_sub surface 4 of 5 --
not 0. pico walks the chain, decodes four, and stops at the truncated fifth. So
`wait_for_substring("Received")` -- "at least one arrived", the shape every
sibling test in this family uses -- PASSES that corrupted frame. Only a COUNT
catches it. Measured, not reasoned, and it is the difference between a test and
a decoration.

TWO DEMO KNOBS, and why they had to exist. Layer E's witness is `wz-ap-demo`, and
its publisher was a fixed script: wait for Established, then burst 5 Pushes at
200ms. No knob could produce an idle window (the default fires at once;
`--reconnect`'s long-lived mode publishes on a cadence), and none could produce a
batched frame -- the demo never called `batch_start`, so `batch.active` was
always false and the demo had NEVER batched. `--publish-after-ms` and `--batch`
are the two orderings, both in the family of the existing `--connect-after` /
`--unsubscribe-after-data`. `--publish-after-ms` is deliberately NOT cfg-gated on
transport-keepalive: it is a pure delay, and it MUST stay inert with the feature
off, because the keepalive-OFF build is exactly the anti-vacuity arm the proof
rests on.

BOTH TESTS OWN THEIR PRECONDITION (R311y338's fixture rule). A 14s wait that
succeeds would ALSO pass if the burst fired at t=0, and 5 receipts are
indistinguishable batched or not -- so each test asserts the demo's own bracket
lines FIRST, in order, and refuses to conclude anything until the window it needs
is confirmed open.

WHAT I FOUND OUT ABOUT THE REST, and it is not encouraging. Of the 38 ap-full
atoms still unproven, only TEN are in `preset-ap-client`, the preset the demo
builds; the other 28 need a different binary or preset. Within the ten,
liveliness-get/-history need an ordering the demo cannot produce, session-reconnect
needs a listening peer (pico CLIs are all clients, so it means zenohd -- absent
here, and hosted CI never runs Layer Z), and locator-tcp/-udp raise a question
this round did not answer: a locator string is LOCAL configuration a foreign peer
never sees, so whether those 8 belong in A4's denominator at all is a design
question, not a missing test.

Round 311y346.decision_summary:
R311y346 -- the user said "pay ALL the debt". The first honest finding is that the
debt was not five items, it was nineteen; the second is that the ratify the user
CHOSE should not land; and the third is that the answer I proposed to the round's
other open fork was refuted on four axes, three of which I had read with my own
eyes before writing the opposite.

THE RATIFY IS REFUSED, and this discharges it -- a determinable design question is
settled, not asked. Widening IMPL_TAGS["UNVERIFIED"] {reserved} -> {reserved,active}
dies three independent deaths. (1) MY OWN STRONGEST ARGUMENT FOR IT IS TEXTUALLY
FALSE. I argued :513's "the tag is PARTIAL and the residual is 'unproven by any
lane'" manufactures a mis-typed tag because PARTIAL means a CODE residual. It does
not: :195-196 reads "built ..., with a named residual" -- no "CODE", type-unbounded.
Only UNVERIFIED's column specifies a type ("-> a CI lane, not code"), and that
distinguishes UNVERIFIED's remaining WORK, it does not bound PARTIAL's residual. So
:513 is CONSISTENT with the gloss it was accused of contradicting. The gun was never
loaded. (2) IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE MOVE. UNVERIFIED's gloss is a CONJUNCTION: "code
portable BY CONSTRUCTION, but no lane proves it". platform-macos satisfies the first
conjunct honestly -- cfg=0, it is the very std+tokio code the linux lane already
runs, so portability follows by construction. An ACTIVE atom gates its OWN code
(invariant #3), so no other lane runs it and "by construction" is unavailable to it.
The widening silently DROPS a conjunct: a semantic change wearing a set-expansion
costume. R311y299's PARTIAL move needed no gloss edit because :195-196 was already
status- and type-neutral. The analogy breaks exactly there. (3) THE INVENTORY HAS
ALREADY DECIDED THIS, TWICE, IN WRITING. transport-compression and
transport-lowlatency are COMPLETE + active and carry "LOCAL-ONLY (off-default) --
a proof-axis gap, NOT an A3 implementation residual". A lane gap creates no tag
crisis; it is recorded as prose on the orthogonal axis, by design. And the widening
moves no answer in IMPL_TAGS / IMPL_TAGS_BUILT / TAGS_REMAINING -- the exact

R311y347 -- the user's correction was the round's premise: ap AND pico must ALL be
full, so BUILD, do not grade. R311y339-y346 were seven rounds on the audit
machinery and none on the coverage it audits. This round closes `session-matching`

WHY THIS ATOM, DERIVED RATHER THAN PICKED: of `preset-ap-full`'s 38 atoms with no

leaves four, and `session-matching` is the one whose witness is strongest.

WHAT MAKES THIS ATOM UNUSUAL, AND WHY IT IS THE BEST WITNESS IN THE FOUR: wz does
not have to SEND anything for the proof to bind. A matching listener fires on every
status TRANSITION caused by an INBOUND remote Declare/UndeclSubscriber. So pico is
not a receiver being checked against wz's bytes -- pico is the CAUSE and wz is the
thing under test. That inverts the corpus's usual shape, and it is exactly the
axis rule "pico does not implement X" != "pico cannot witness X".

BOTH EDGES ARE PICO'S, and the second one is free: z_sub.c's loop breaks once its
-n count is met and then runs z_drop(z_move(sub)) (:91), which retracts the
declaration. So `z_sub -n 1` gives a declare AND an undeclare with no demo-side
choreography at all. wz has no local subscriber in this fixture, so nothing else
could have raised the status.

THE RED, and it is the sharp half: suppressing ONLY the undeclare arm's
matching_watches.reevaluate (declare/subscriber.rs) left matching=true firing
normally and matching=false never arriving. So the second edge is load-bearing --
a listener that fired once and latched would pass a one-edge test -- and the twin
arm surviving is what proves the assertion NARROWS rather than disables. Measured
on the real binary, not argued.

THE CFG SPLIT IS THE DESIGN FINDING, and it decides what the test may touch.
`Publisher::declare_matching_listener` is
`#[cfg(all(feature = "session-matching", feature = "declare-subscriber"))]`, but its
sibling `Publisher::get_matching_status` is gated on `declare-subscriber` ALONE and
conservatively returns false when that registry is elided. So the POLL is not this
atom's code: a proof that polled would have bound the claim to the wrong atom and
looked entirely reasonable doing it. The knob installs the CALLBACK for that reason
and no other.

MY OWN TEST CAUGHT MY OWN DESIGN BUG, which is the case for anti-vacuity arms.
The first run FAILED at the "listener installed" assertion, not at an edge -- the
demo installs its handles at run_demo scope, which it reaches only AFTER a peer
connects, so waiting for that line BEFORE spawning z_sub deadlocked the test
against the demo. Without that arm the failure would have been a timeout on
matching=true and I would have gone looking at pico. The ordering that replaced it
is safe STRUCTURALLY rather than luckily: an inbound Declare is dispatched by the
drive loop, and the drive loop starts after install_session_handles returns.

Round 311y348.decision_summary:
R311y348 -- the user stopped me mid-round: "why do you keep READING? didn't we agree
to build the test and let it decide?" They were right, and the cost of my being
wrong was about to be a headline number. I had spent the round reading, had built an
argument to EXCLUDE the 8 locator-* atoms from A4's denominator (160 -> 152), and had
just handed it to two reviewers to ARGUE about. One 12-second run settled it instead,
and settled it against me.

THE FORK IS ANSWERED: THE 8 STAY. R311y345 raised it on the premise that "a locator
string is LOCAL configuration a foreign peer never sees". THE PREMISE IS FALSE. Run
wz-ap-demo --peer + a real pico z_get at `@/**` and pico prints:
`@/<zid>/peer: {"locators":["tcp/127.0.0.1:58501"], ...}`. wz PUTS its locators on
the wire and a foreign implementation reads them. The exclusion would have been
wrong, and every step of the argument for it was individually defensible.

AND THE ARTIFACT IS THE ATOM'S, measured both ways before a line of test was
written: handed the BARE `127.0.0.1:P` (no scheme), pico reads back
`tcp/127.0.0.1:P`; handed `tcp/127.0.0.1:P`, pico reads back the same canonical
form. So wz's locator layer PARSED the bare form, canonicalised it, and rendered it
into a payload that crossed the wire. The `tcp/` cannot be an argv echo. That round
trip is `locator-tcp`, and pico decoding it is the foreign half.

WHAT MY ARGUMENT WAS, AND WHY IT LOOKED SOUND -- this is the part worth keeping. The
8 reasons all say "the parse is always-on; the cfg toggle is forward target
transport-link-X; cfg=0". Their cargo keys are `locator-tcp = ["transport-link-tcp"]`
-- byte-for-byte the shape of `link-batching = ["transport-batching"]`, which IS
excluded as a category-(2) alias. And crossimpl_audit.py's own comment (:420) says of
the alias-shaped FOUNDATIONALs -- a list that NAMES the 8 -- "which is why an alias
belongs in that set". Reasons, cargo shape, and the file's own sentence all agreed.
They were all agreeing about the wrong thing.

THE REVIEWER LANDED THREE KILLS I DID NOT HAVE, and the first is aimed at me. (1)
ALL EIGHT CITATIONS IN THOSE REASONS HAVE ROTTED: locator-tcp cites "locator.rs:144
Proto::Tcp"; :144 is inside a doc comment, the arm is :183. Same for all eight, dial
side included. I quoted eight reasons VERBATIM as my evidence and opened NOT ONE of
them -- the exact defect this repo has named repeatedly, committed by me in the round
where I was reasoning about whether prose can be trusted. (2) The premise is false on
THREE surfaces, not the one I found: the scouting HELLO carries a locator list behind
_Z_FLAG_T_HELLO_L (wz-codecs/src/lib.rs:677, scouting_glue.rs:453-457), linkstate
advertises per-node locators, and the adminspace renders them. My test found the
third. (3) locator-tcp is PROVEN-BUT-UNTAGGED today: pubkey_zenohd_interop.rs:164
calls parse_any_locator("tcp/127.0.0.1:{port}") in-process and dials a real zenohd,
claiming only the extauth atoms. Confirmed by direct read.

MY NARROWING WAS CHERRY-PICKING, and the reviewer's discriminator is better than
mine. I derived 18 sibling-aliases from cargo, found 3 in the exclusion set, and
narrowed to the 8 on the judgement that "io_uring is a different capability that
merely REQUIRES tokio". That judgement is right and it is NOT derived -- and applied
to locator-tcp it gives the OPPOSITE answer: the parse grammar is a different

THE DISCRIMINATOR, now stated properly (the reviewer's, and it is better than mine):
DOES THE VEHICLE'S OWN FOREIGN PROOF NECESSARILY WITNESS X'S OBSERVABLE?
  YES -> X is a re-view; its witness IS V's witness; category (2); exclude.
  NO  -> X names a SEPARABLE observable that merely happens to be co-resident in V's
         compile unit. A distinct capability REQUIRING V. Keep it; it owes a witness.
Operational, and falsifiable: CAN YOU WRITE A TEST THAT WITNESSES X AND FAILS WHILE
V'S OWN PROOF STILL PASSES? For locator-tcp the answer is yes and y348 WROTE it --
transport-link-tcp's dial proofs pass regardless of whether the canonical string ever
renders. The test was the right answer to a question its own ledger asked wrong.
The trap this kills: "compiled together" != "same artifact". Cargo shape cannot
discriminate -- if X = [V] and X has 0 cfg sites, `--features X` and `--features V`
are byte-identical builds, and that is equally true of link-batching (a real re-view)
and scouting-gossip (not one). Which is exactly why reading the cargo keys produced a
confident wrong answer twice.

Round 311y352.decision_summary:
R311y352 -- scouting-static earns a foreign witness, and the round's two best findings
are both REFUTATIONS of things this project already believed.

THE ATOM. `scouting-static` is the static-mode alternative to discovery: a configured
list, tried in order, first Established wins. It has sat unproven on the cross-impl axis
since the axis existed. It is now proven, by a real zenoh-pico peer, and the test that
does it is NOT the test that first suggested itself.

THE OBVIOUS TEST WOULD HAVE PROVEN THE WRONG ATOM -- R311y347's finding, hit again from
a different direction. The entrypoints are asymmetrically gated and session_open.rs
says so in its own comment at :2244-2245: `open_session_static` is
`#[cfg(feature = "scouting-static")]` (:2246) -- the atom's code -- while its sibling
`open_session_at` is UNGATED, "since active scouting feeds it too". So "point wz at a
configured address and watch it connect" reaches Established through the UNGATED
sibling, passes whether or not the atom was ever compiled, and proves nothing. Read the
cfg on BOTH surfaces of a pair before writing the test; the natural-looking surface is
not the atom's.

WHAT THE ATOM ACTUALLY OWNS is the LIST: synth_static_locators, tried in order, skip a
failure, return the first Established. So the fixture is `[dead, pico]` with the dead
entry FIRST -- a shape `open_session_at` structurally cannot express, since it takes one
locator. That is R311y349's separability discriminator answered YES: the test witnesses
scouting-static and fails while every `open_session_at` proof still passes.

REFUTATION 1 -- `locator-udp` IS NOT ACTIONABLE, and the agent-memory triage table that
said "fork now CLOSED, so unblocked" was wrong. The demo answered in one run:
"wz-ap-demo: listen/accept is wired only for tcp; Udp acceptor is a not-yet-wired
extension point". All three render surfaces the y348 review enumerated (adminspace,
scouting HELLO, linkstate) carry the locators wz LISTENS on, and wz listens on tcp
only -- so there is no place for a `udp/` locator to be rendered, and y348's
render-witness route does not transfer to the sibling. Quoting the table would have
started a test that cannot be written.

REFUTATION 2 -- THE HAND-OFF SAID THE LEDGER DEBT WAS ONE ROUND; IT WAS TWO. The tree
self-identifies: `R311y350` appears at 4 sites (dde45d5's fix) and `R311y351` at
ci.yml:434 (d934c18's split). Ledgering both as one entry would have left ci.yml citing
an entry that does not exist. A hand-off count is a CLAIM.

Round 311y354.decision_summary:
R311y354 -- `liveliness-history` is PROVEN, as a PAIR, and the pair is the point.

THE ATOM. `history = true` on a liveliness subscriber puts the CURRENT bit on the
outbound Interest (wire mode CurrentFuture), so the subscriber is replayed the tokens
that ALREADY EXIST rather than only those declared from now on. runner.rs says the same
from the demo side: history "makes the subscriber order-independent of token declare
time". So the atom's observable is a token declared STRICTLY BEFORE the subscriber
existed -- which is why this fixture's ordering is deliberately the reverse of the
usual: pico declares first, wz subscribes late.

THIS ROUND WAS CHEAP BECAUSE y353 PAID FOR IT. The route was known before a line was
written: a history replay IS an Interest answer, and R311y353 measured that zenoh-pico
NEVER answers an Interest on a unicast transport (interest.c:533-535, "Nothing to do on
unicast"). So the topology is the same one y353 built -- pico(token) -> zenohd(responder)
<- wz(subscriber) -- and no round was spent re-discovering that pico cannot serve it.
That is what a carry is for. The contrast with the blocker note y353 refuted is the
lesson: a reason that is MEASURED transfers, a reason that is ASSERTED costs the next
round.

A SINGLE POSITIVE TEST HERE WOULD HAVE BEEN NEARLY WORTHLESS, and this is the round's
transferable finding. `LIVELINESS SAMPLE PUT` is what `liveliness-subscriber` logs for
ANY token, future ones included. A green positive arm therefore does not distinguish
"the pre-existing token was REPLAYED" (the atom) from "a token arrived somehow" (its
vehicle). The claim only becomes this atom's when the twin exists:

  history ON  -> the sample arrives, carrying pico's exact token.
  history OFF -> identical fixture, one CLI flag removed: the session Establishes and
                 the sample never comes.

Both arms were MEASURED by hand before the file was written (ON -> 1 sample, OFF -> 0),
so the pair was known to discriminate before it was encoded. The two differ in exactly
one flag, so together they say the replay is CAUSED by `history` -- neither says it
alone. This is the y352 twin rule applied to a claim rather than to a fixture's
precondition: there, the twin pinned that a dead port was dead; here, it pins that the
atom's own flag is what produces the observable.

Round 311y355.decision_summary:
R311y355 -- `session-reconnect` is PROVEN cross-impl, and the round's real content is a
methodology failure that a BISECT caught before it shipped.

THE ATOM. session-reconnect is the long-lived supervisor (open_session_with_reconnect)
that re-dials on link loss and REPLAYS the declaration cache (replay_declarations) so
the surviving session resumes. The existing wz-only e2e proves the replay against a wz
acceptor; this proves it against a real zenohd RESTARTED underneath a live wz session --
the cross-impl half no wz<->wz test can reach, because the wz-only one re-handshakes
against wz.

THE OBSERVABLE IS ENGINEERED SO ONLY REPLAY PRODUCES IT: wz subscribes to demo/**;
pico puts demo/pre through zenohd#1 (baseline routes); zenohd#1 is KILLED; a FRESH
zenohd#2 respawns on the same port; pico puts demo/post. zenohd#2 has no memory of wz's
subscription, so a `SUBSCRIBER FIRED keyexpr='demo/post'` line can ONLY mean the
supervisor re-dialled and replayed demo/** to it. Distinct keyexprs (pre/post) make the
witness unambiguous -- no reliance on payload length or ordering.

THE TWIN IS THE POINT, AND IT NEARLY DIED TO A HARNESS BUG. The pair: --reconnect
resumes and delivers demo/post; no --reconnect exits on link loss and never does. The
first hand-verification of the twin RECEIVED demo/post in BOTH arms -- which reads
exactly like a vacuous twin and would have condemned a correct design, or worse, made me
ship a positive-only test believing the twin was impossible. THE CAUSE: I killed zenohd
via `kill $!` where `$!` was a SHELL SUBPROCESS wrapping `timeout zenohd`, not zenohd.
zenohd#1 never died, kept the port, zenohd#2's bind failed, and the still-alive zenohd#1
routed demo/post to a wz that had never reconnected (record_established_at stayed 1). A
BISECT -- kill the REAL pid, assert it is dead, assert zenohd#2 bound -- flipped both
arms to correct: --reconnect -> demo/post + reconnects=1 + record_established_at=2; no
--reconnect -> wz exits, demo/post count 0. "Structurally cannot" is a claim, and so is
"my kill killed the thing"; the harness is part of the experiment and can lie.

WHY THE ASSERTION IS ON DATA, NOT ON THE COUNTER. The demo logs `reconnects=N` only at
graceful shutdown, and an early run showed reconnects=0 while data had already resumed
(the counter commit lagged the teardown). So the PRIMARY assertion is the replayed data
(demo/post, retry-gated, deterministic); reconnects=1 is a corroborating check read
AFTER demo/post is confirmed, when the reconnect has provably happened.

WHY IT IS NOT FLAKY, MEASURED NOT ASSERTED. zenohd restart on the same port is the
proven-reliable pattern the wz-only respawn test already uses (port reservation held
across the sever); the Rust fixture spawns zenohd as a direct Command child so
ChildGuard's kill hits the process, not a shell. Run 3x back to back: 28.2 / 27.2 /
28.0s, all green. The post-put is retried until the witness lands, so the reconnect
window is covered by a bounded loop, not a sleep.

Root design lesson (user: "cost ignored, most long-term-correct"): the first ws cut was a point-fix (a locator_is_ws special-case threaded into accept_locator) that would NOT scale -- repeating it per transport = an ad-hoc-branch anti-pattern. The real defect was that the ACCEPT side was ASYMMETRIC to the DIAL side: dial_locator dispatches scheme->DialedLink cleanly, but bind_locator returned a bare TcpListener (losing the scheme, unable to even represent a UnixListener/QuicEndpoint/UdpSocket). FIX: BoundListener enum = the accept-side mirror of DialedLink. bind_locator -> BoundListener, accept_bound dispatches per variant + runs the scheme handshake, yielding the SAME DialedLink the dial side does (shared wire_* downstream). Adding a transport is now ONE arm in BoundListener + bind_locator + accept_bound -- symmetric to adding a dial_locator arm + DialedLink variant.

carry_forward_bullets: R311y381 = accept-symmetry Stage 4, FOURTH arm and the FIRST datagram accept: the udp accept seam is wired. UDP is the structurally-hardest arm because it has no accept() yielding a per-peer socket -- one bound socket IS the link, addressed to the peer accept_raw learns by PEEKING the first datagram's source (peek does not consume, so the InitSyn stays queued for the read driver). Three design facts distinguish it: (1) single-shot via BoundListener::Udp(Option<UdpSocket>) + take, because there is one socket; (2) the accepted peer is a REAL IP (AcceptedPeer::Ip, the datagram source), so it CAN key a mesh face and needs NO accept_loop change -- the first accept is a real face, the second is an Err the existing EMFILE throttle bounds; (3) cancel-safety required peek-BEFORE-take (a take-before-await lost the socket when a mesh select! cancels the accept mid-peek). code = 5efefdb (117ae11 amended with reviewer C's F1/F2 doc fold-in). 3-agent review ALL SOUND/VALID.

CANCEL-SAFETY LESSON: for an accept arm that must MOVE (not borrow) its listener resource, the take/consume MUST come AFTER the await, never before -- a dropped accept future (a select! choosing another arm) otherwise consumes the resource for nothing. KEY LESSON (pump lifetime): the recv pump must OUTLIVE the BoundListener, because the one-shot accept_bound path drops the listener before the accepted session is driven (the mesh accept_loop instead holds it for life). A plain TokioJoinHandle does NOT abort on drop, and a .closed()-on-listener-drop pump would STARVE the one-shot face -- so the pump is kept alive by an Arc<UdpDemuxPump> (abort-on-drop guard) SHARED by the listener and every accepted face, aborting only when the last holder drops. This was the design-review BLOCKER, caught before code by the 2-agent design review.

FOLLOW-UP (deferred, honestly documented in the BoundListener::Udp doc): (a) the faces HashMap grows one entry per distinct src until a later datagram reaps it -- UDP src is spoofable without a round-trip, so this is a cheaper face-creation surface than TCP; bounded per-face by the cap-256 channels + reap-on-send-error, the map itself uncapped, at PARITY with the uncapped TCP accept_loop (zenoh caps at the transport-manager accept layer, not the link demux). crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/udp_pipeline.rs (pump error handling -- reviewer-C code-review headline fix, folded this round): the pump NEVER returns from either error path; its ONLY termination is the Arc<UdpDemuxPump> abort. A return would drop the stack `faces` map and CLOSE every live face's channel -- and on the one-shot path (listener dropped, an accepted face alive via the guard) a single stray datagram from a NEW (spoofable) src arriving at the listen port would otherwise fail the new-face handoff, return, and tear down the ESTABLISHED session (a 1-packet DoS). Fix: a recv_from error throttles-and-continues (UDP_DEMUX_RECV_ERROR_THROTTLE_MS=100, zenoh UDP_ACCEPT_THROTTLE_TIME parity), and a new src arriving after the listener is gone is simply not accepted (its channel dropped, faces.insert skipped) while the accepted faces keep being served. The prior `return`-on-send-err comment ("via the shared pump guard, so are all faces") was factually inverted (the guard KEEPS faces alive) and is corrected.

A shared base request channel (P_uplink) carries 8-byte invitations (magic 0xDEADBEEF ++ suffix.to_ne_bytes, native-endian, matching zenoh unicast.rs:55-67); each accepted client gets a DEDICATED pipe pair keyed by a random u32 suffix formatted DECIMAL (P_uplink{suffix}/P_downlink{suffix}, matching zenoh get_dedicated_pipe_names). flock (raw libc::flock, == zenoh's advisory_lock crate) is load-bearing on ALL THREE reader ends (listener base + listener dedicated_uplink + client dedicated_downlink) for zenoh's PipeW::new bail-if-lock-free probe, plus suffix-collision detection (retry <=100) + single-listener enforcement. create_fifo_tolerant is no-unlink EEXIST-tolerant (flock is the reservation, not mkfifo). FifoReadEnd unlinks its read node on Drop + releases flock via fd close (zenoh PipeR::Drop parity). UnixpipeAcceptor + UnixpipeAcceptorPump (abort-on-drop). The acceptor task reads invitations serially and bounds each handshake with a HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT (10s, zenoh accept_timeout parity) wrapper -- a SUPERSET over zenoh's serial-UNBOUNDED loop: a stalled/hostile peer is bounded to the timeout (then the acceptor drops the half-open handshake + recovers) instead of wedging the acceptor forever as zenoh's UnicastPipeListener does (review fix for reviewer A's MAJOR; a per-invitation-concurrent variant was tried and reverted -- it hung the 2-dialer test).

carry_forward_bullets: R311y411 = the cross-impl MESH quic-DATAGRAM lane (7 legs, the y407 twin over an UNRELIABLE link) plus the routing-identity defect it EXPOSED: wz's `Zid` was not canonical, so a peer whose zid ended in a zero byte failed to recognise itself when a neighbour's LinkStateList returned it wire-trimmed, entered its own graph as a phantom node, and silently stopped forwarding. Fixed in `Zid::from_slice` (trailing zeros trimmed, matching `uhlc::ID::size()`), pinned by 2 unit tests + a deterministic e2e leg (`--zid 70728300`).

THE DEFECT IS NOT DATAGRAM-SPECIFIC. It fires for ANY wz-ap-demo mesh node whose port-derived zid ends in `0x00` (1 in 256 ephemeral ports) and for any operator passing such a `--zid`. The reliable-quic mesh lane (y407) and every other demo-based mesh e2e carried the same exposure and the same latent ~0.4%-per-bind flake; they are all fixed by this round, but NONE of them has a regression leg of its own -- only the datagram lane pins it (leg 7). A future round could give the reliable-quic sibling the same leg, or better, assert the invariant once at the forwarder level.

PROCESS lesson worth more than the fix: 30/30 then 99/100 then 244/250 measured the RATE and never found the CAUSE. What found it was making the harness observable -- the spawn helper hardcoded `RUST_LOG=info`, which reports topology as COUNTS (`peak 3 node(s)`) while node identity and advertised locators are `debug`. One instrumented run named the phantom. Re-running is measurement, not diagnosis; when a flake resists, unpin the observability first (`WZ_TEST_DEMO_LOG` now exists for that).

PORT-COLLISION flake (the round's first, separately root-caused and fixed): every acceptor-direction test derived its zenohd tcp port as `wz_port.wrapping_add(1)`, justified by a namespace argument that only excludes wz's OWN socket; TIME_WAIT (zenohd sets no SO_REUSEADDR) is the amplifier. Fixed by removing the guess -- zenohd binds `:0` and the test reads the kernel-assigned port back from its announcement.

CARRIED, deliberately not migrated: the `wrapping_add(1)` guess still stands at 10 call sites across 6 files (wz_mesh_quic_acceptor x5, wz_quic_acceptor, wz_quic_datagram_acceptor, wz_tls_acceptor, wz_ws_acceptor, wz_router_ws_acceptor), all in the same hosted Layer Z lane. The CODE is unchanged but the FALSE prose is not -- every site now records the real failure mode and points at `spawn_zenohd_dialer_on_ephemeral_tcp`. Recipe: drop each shared spawn_zenohd_*_dialer's `tcp_port` parameter, delegate to the new helper, RETURN the discovered port. Likewise `wait_for_substring` stays liveness-BLIND at every call site except the new helper's, so any test waiting on a log line from a process that dies still burns its full budget; and 27 sibling count-guards in run-ci.sh remain UNANCHORED (`grep -q 'N passed'` matches a FAILED result line, reviewer-reproduced).

Round 311y411.decision_summary: R311y411 = cross-impl MESH quic-DATAGRAM proof (the y407 mesh-quic leg's UNRELIABLE twin) that EXPOSED and fixed a real routing-identity defect: wz's Zid was not canonical, so a node whose zid ended in a zero byte could not recognise ITSELF in a neighbour's link-state flood. Seven legs: --router-hat routers_net convergence plus a real LinkStateList decode; --peer mutual linkstate edge; a gossip ROUTING neuter; real pub/sub data crossing the accepted datagram mesh link BOTH directions; a TRANSPORT neuter (the SAME listen/endpoint/cert dialed WITHOUT `?rel=0` never brings a face up and must fail as `Terminal`, so a cert regression cannot satisfy it) that pins legs 1-5 to the DATAGRAM data plane since the mesh listen line carries no transport tag; and a REGRESSION leg for the zid defect below. THE DEFECT (product code, not test): zenoh's identity for a zid is the VALUE -- `uhlc::ID::size()` counts significant LE bytes (`MAX_SIZE - leading_zeros(u128::from_le_bytes(..))/8`, uhlc-0.8.1 src/id.rs:67, which `ZenohIdProto` wraps) -- so `[70,72,83,00]` and `[70,72,83]` are ONE zid. wz's `Zid::from_slice` kept the caller's slice length verbatim, making them two. `wz-ap-demo` derives its mesh zid from its listen PORT, so an ephemeral port with a `0x00` low byte (1 in 256) produced a self zid ending in zero; the peer announced it, zenohd canonicalised it on the wire, and the LinkStateList flood came back TRIMMED and no longer compared equal to self. The node then entered its OWN topology graph as a phantom peer with no edges and the spanning-tree next-hop computation silently stopped forwarding -- a `--publish` peer's data never left the box. The wz type doc had already named this corner and dismissed it as "unreachable today"; that assumption is what this round falsifies by measurement. FIXED at the root: `from_slice` now trims trailing zero bytes, so identity is the value and the ordering equivalence the cross-impl edge-jitter tie-break rests on holds unconditionally rather than only for canonical inputs. HOW IT WAS FOUND, and the process correction: a 30-run campaign showed 29/30 and a 100-run campaign 99/100. Re-running is how you MEASURE a rate, not how you find a cause; the investigation only moved when the harness was made observable (the spawn helper hardcoded `RUST_LOG=info`, which reports topology as COUNTS while node identity and advertised locators are `debug`). With that unpinned, 250 instrumented runs produced 6 failures and named the phantom in every one: `discovered peer 7072xx reachable at ["quic-datagram/127.0.0.1:<own listen port>"]`, always a zero-low-byte port. 5 failures were the data-out leg; the 6th was the router tier counting 3 and skipping the exact `(2 node(s))` witness -- one cause, two faces. A SECOND flake, root-caused earlier the same way: zenohd exit 255 "process exited before accepting", because every acceptor-direction test derives its zenohd tcp port as `wz_port.wrapping_add(1)` on a namespace argument that only excludes wz's OWN socket; reproduced deterministically, with TIME_WAIT (zenohd sets no SO_REUSEADDR) as the amplifier. Fixed by removing the guess: zenohd binds `tcp/127.0.0.1:0` and the test reads the kernel-assigned port back from its own announcement. RED+TWIN on every claim: demo without `quic-datagram` -> 7/7 red while the y407 reliable-quic legs stay 5/5 green on the SAME binary; neuter dialing datagram -> leg 6 red; wrong trust anchor -> leg 6 red on the cause assertion; router-hat witness suppressed -> leg 1 red; canonicalisation reverted -> leg 7 red and the pico receives NOTHING; liveness check removed -> the corpse unit test red at 30.05s instead of 0.40s; terminator requirement removed -> the parser unit test red. Two pre-existing Zid tests turned red and were UPDATED, not silenced: they pinned the non-canonical contract (a zero-extended prefix as a distinct, adjacent identity) via a `Vec<u8>` ordering proxy; the load-bearing property their own comment names is agreement with ZENOH, so they now pin that directly. NO atom-count change: A4 measured 78/37/45 at HEAD and after (the ledger's carried 77/37/46 does not reproduce at that commit and is retired here). Full `run-ci.sh` sweep exit 0 (108 lanes) after the core-type change. 3 worktree-isolated adversarial reviewers of sha b75a00a: 0 blockers, 5 should-fix folded.
verification_bullets: ROOT-CAUSE evidence for the Zid defect, from instrumented reproduction (not from re-running): 250 runs with the demo's log filter raised produced 6 failures, and every one named the phantom -- `discovered peer 7072xx reachable at ["quic-datagram/127.0.0.1:<the peer's OWN listen port>"]`. The ports were 33536/49664/39424/54016/56832, i.e. 0x8300/0xC200/0x9A00/0xD300/0xDE00: EVERY failure had a zero LOW BYTE, and the phantom zid was the port-derived self zid with its trailing zero trimmed. 5 failures were the data-OUT leg (pico received nothing); the 6th was the router tier, where the phantom made routers-net count 3 so the exact `(2 node(s))` witness was never logged -- one cause, two faces. Reference rule verified by DIRECT READ, not memory: `uhlc::ID::size()` = `MAX_SIZE - leading_zeros(u128::from_le_bytes(bytes))/8` (uhlc-0.8.1 src/id.rs:67) and `ZenohIdProto` is a transparent wrapper (zenoh 1.5.0 commons/zenoh-protocol/src/core/mod.rs:63-72).

DETERMINISTIC RED/GREEN for the fix, single variable = `Zid::from_slice` canonicalisation, same `--zid 70728300`: PRE-FIX = phantom self-node 1, `peak 3 node(s)`, pico received 0. POST-FIX = phantom 0, `peak 2 node(s)`, pico received 1. CONTROL (post-fix, `--zid 70728301`, no trailing zero) = phantom 0, peak 2, received 1. The 1-in-256 lottery is now a 100% reproduction.

Round 311y412.decision_summary: R311y412 = retire port GUESSING from the zenohd interop harness entirely, and harden the count-guards that were supposed to catch a lane going quiet. After y411 fixed one lane, no test in this crate names a zenohd tcp port any more: every dialer (ws, tls, quic, quic-datagram, unixsock, udp, vsock, unixpipe) plus the unixpipe+tcp LISTENER delegates to `spawn_zenohd_dialer_on_ephemeral_tcp`, which has zenohd bind `tcp/127.0.0.1:0` and reads the kernel-assigned port back out of zenohd's own announcement, then RETURNS it beside the guard. Two guessing routes died: the arithmetic `wz_port.wrapping_add(1)` (10 call sites) and, for the four dialers that used it, `PortReservation::pick`'s reserve-then-release. The second removal is the round's non-obvious result and it was MEASURED, not argued: an adversarial reviewer ran an external process cycling loopback ephemeral sockets and the reserve-then-release lanes failed 5/210 (`wz_udp_acceptor`) and 3/210 (`wz_unixsock_acceptor`) with the exact y411 signature (`process exited before accepting ... status 255`), while the discovery lanes were 0/330 under the same churn. That refutes the intuition -- offered by a second reviewer -- that `bind(0)` immunises the reservation: it does avoid TIME_WAIT, but the window between the release and the child's bind is real and losable. `PortReservation` survives only where the port must be named BEFORE a process starts (a wz-side listen), which this route cannot serve. GUARDS: all 34 lane count-guards are now anchored to `^test result: ok\. N passed`. The old substring form false-GREENED two ways, both reviewer-reproduced: a FAILED summary whose passed-count matches (`FAILED. 5 passed; 1 failed` satisfies a `5 passed` guard) and count inflation (`11 passed` satisfies a `1 passed` guard, the case `set -o pipefail` could never catch). Colour is now FORCED off (`CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never`, previously only a `:-` default) because the hosted workflow exports `always` for the whole job and an ANSI escape would break the new `^` anchor -- one line instead of an ANSI strip at 34 pipelines. HARNESS DEFECTS the review surfaced, all fixed and each proven by running it: the capture file the y411 primitive owns was created with a predictable name and a plain `File::create`, which FOLLOWS a planted symlink and truncates the target -- now `create_new` (O_EXCL), with the unlink ordered so a failed reader open leaks nothing; the wz-demo spawn wait was liveness-BLIND, so a demo that dies at startup cost the full 10s per leg and was then misreported as "did not bind" with its exit status never collected -- now liveness-aware, measured 60.18s -> 0.36s across 7 legs with the real `exit status: 1` reported; `WZ_TEST_DEMO_LOG` had no floor, so a module-scoped override that omitted `wz_ap_demo` silently dropped the witnesses every lane asserts on and turned a HEALTHY run into a convincing false transport diagnosis -- now the floor is appended and the reviewer's failing case passes; `listen_port` lacked the torn-read terminator guard its zenohd-side twin has; and the demo's `--zid` accepted an all-zero zid (binds, then loses face after face forever) and a >16-byte zid, which in RELEASE builds silently corrupts the wire because `handshake_encode`'s `(zid_len - 1) & 0x0F` wraps and a 17-byte zid encodes as length 1 -- both now rejected at the CLI boundary with the zenoh rule named. The two y411 unit twins were REBUILT on the shipped `create_new`/`open` capture pair: they had used `tempfile` + `try_clone`, the shared-offset shape production abandoned, so they were not evidence for what ships. Prose the migration falsified was corrected rather than left standing, including the primitive's own rationale (which described a codebase this round retired) and two test bodies still asserting the refuted "cannot collide" reasoning. Round 311y418.decision_summary: R311y418 -- build the guard R311y417's carry commissioned: a local gate that refuses a store whose schema_version has outrun the pinned CI mnemosyne-cli, so the class that has now fired FOUR times (y15, y401, y406, y416, every one discovered on hosted CI) reds locally instead. MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA lands beside MNEMOSYNE_REV, verified at the pin rather than inherited from prose, and the comparison logic moves into scripts/lib/schema-pin-gate.sh so pre-commit and pre-push share one implementation. Three worktree-isolated reviewers on the frozen first cut found THREE blockers, all reproduced independently before folding: git commit was the only guarded route, so cherry-pick, rebase, merge and --no-verify carried a migrated store straight to the push boundary; the store was graded from the WORKING TREE while hosted CI grades the COMMITTED tree, which both let an index-only staging escape and falsely blocked unrelated commits over an uncommitted migration; and the ceiling was self-asserted, so raising it one character silenced the gate while CI still installed the old reader. The fold grades the INDEX for both halves, adds the same gate to pre-push against every pushed commit, requires the ceiling and the rev to move together, and closes a fail-open where a leading-zero ceiling made bash arithmetic error out inside an if and fall through to green. The round also shipped and fixed its own defect mid-session: the first cut read the pin by SOURCING the index blob, which executed an installer from inside a commit hook. Reading a shell file must not mean running it. Also removed: pre-push's mnemosyne-cli SKIP, unreachable in the flow it was written for and reachable only where the gate matters most. NO Rust source; store schema_version unchanged at 43.

THE SHELL LINT GATE PAID FOR ITSELF ON ITS FIRST RUN, and what it found is the sharpest instance yet of this repo's recurring class. Two prose comments in run-ci.sh started with the word `shellcheck`, so the tool parsed them as malformed DIRECTIVES and abandoned the file -- all ~13k lines, including the very function that runs the linters, had been analysed by nothing, with four real findings sitting behind that silence. R311y418 had hand-checked ~150 new shell lines instead of gating them; hand-checking is exactly what missed this. Then the new gate went red on ITS OWN AUTHOR, on a third such comment written while documenting the trap. The match is a PREFIX, not a whole word -- `shellcheck-backed` triggers it too -- so the first detector regex, which required whitespace after the word, missed the second instance. Never start a comment line with it.

A GATE CAN BE SWALLOWED BY AN UNRELATED TOOL'S ABSENCE. The new sub-lane sat after the actionlint block's early `return 0`, so a developer without actionlint silently skipped the shell lint too, with shellcheck installed and working. Two independent tools sharing one another's absence is the same success-by-silence shape as a SKIP that reports green; resolve shared prerequisites ABOVE the first consumer, not inside the first one that happens to need them.

Round 311y419.decision_summary: R311y419 -- three CI-gate closures, taken in the order R311y418's carry and disclosures named them, with no wire / atom / inventory change: the schema pin now verifies itself against the pinned BINARY, the repo's own shell is linted for the first time, and the three isolated-crate lanes gate hosted. (1) THE PIN CEILING IS NO LONGER SELF-ASSERTED. R311y418 shipped a store-vs-ceiling gate and named its own residual in its carry: nothing proved MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA was MNEMOSYNE_REV's real CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION, since both numbers are hand-set from a hand-read of upstream source, and the co-change gate proves only that they moved together. scripts/verify-mnemosyne-pin.sh closes it by asking the INSTALLED binary: mnemosyne-cli describe-schema --json -> .schema_version, which mnemosyne-ops::describe_schema() populates from mnemosyne_atomic::CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION. Its purity was established by construction rather than from its doc comment -- it reports 43 with no workspace present at all, and 43 unchanged against a store hand-set to schema_version 999 -- so it is a property of the binary and never of the tree it runs in. Grading the binary rather than crates/mnemosyne-atomic/src/lib.rs out of the cargo checkout is deliberate: the source file need not be what cargo install actually built. It grades command -v mnemosyne-cli, i.e. what later CI steps run, so a shadowing earlier-PATH binary is caught rather than bypassed. It is called from the TAIL of scripts/install-mnemosyne-cli.sh rather than wired as a ci.yml step, because that script exists so ci.yml and release.yml cannot drift and a gate bolted onto one workflow reintroduces exactly that drift; every install route now runs it, and the SC2034 disable the constant used to carry is gone because it is live code. DELIBERATELY NOT GATED, recorded so a later round does not "strengthen" it into a brittle check: that the binary was built from MNEMOSYNE_REV. mnemosyne-cli --version embeds git describe --always --dirty=-dirty --abbrev=8, so its output is a bare short hash only while NO tag is reachable upstream and degrades to the literal unknown without .git -- a gate whose truth would depend on another project's tagging policy. Git hooks still never install, so a wrong ceiling stays locally invisible until somebody reinstalls the pinned CLI. (2) THE REPO'S OWN SHELL IS LINTED. Layer 0 gains sub-lane 0.2: shellcheck over 18 tracked files (scripts/*.sh, scripts/lib/*.sh, .githooks/*), a surface disjoint from the workflow run: blocks actionlint covers and, verified by enumerating every gate first, previously linted by nothing. Its first run found a real defect: two prose comments in run-ci.sh began with the word shellcheck, which the tool reads as a malformed DIRECTIVE (SC1073/SC1072) and then abandons the enclosing brace group over (SC1009) -- so all ~13k lines of that file, including the function that runs the linters, had been analysed by nothing. 11 findings were visible at HEAD; 2 of them were that parse-error pair, and clearing them exposed 4 more, for 13 ordinary findings resolved. The gate then went RED ON ITS OWN AUTHOR when a third such comment was written while documenting the trap. One structural fix was load-bearing: shellcheck-presence resolution was hoisted ABOVE the actionlint block, whose early return 0 had been swallowing the new lane whenever actionlint was merely absent -- two independent tools must not share one another's absence. (3) C1m / C1n / C3 GATE HOSTED, on a NEW isolated-crates job. A third genre job rather than a step on an existing one: the transport-modes job states its lane-selection rule and names these three as OUT of it, and both sibling jobs declare disk rather than time as the binding constraint (a fresh CARGO_TARGET_DIR carrying just these three reaches 1.7G). The genre rule is the complement -- the crate CANNOT participate in --workspace feature unification (C1m/C1n force wz-session-core/no_std, which sce-rust-runtime's compile_error! makes exclusive with the http-send std runtime wz-runtime-tokio pulls, so Layers C1/C2 exclude them by construction), or the matrix exists because unification MASKS what isolation surfaces (C3). Hardened FIRST per R311y414's rule that hosting only helps if the lane can go red: 15 _runci_guarded_test steps at measured counts. The hazard was demonstrated, not assumed -- cargo test -p wz-mcu-session-acceptor --test host_acceptor_reassembly_e2e WITHOUT --features reassembly exits 0 reporting 0 passed. Hosted lanes 73 -> 76 of 107; C4c / C4d (the R311y332 gap) and C1bf are the same genre and remain LOCAL-ONLY, stated because R311y413 recorded "class closed" being overclaimed twice. Three commits, no code/Cargo/atom/inventory change: 2bd59d8, 11a3fb3, dfa38d7.

The first harness run reported 7 false FAILs from a minimal PATH lacking `bash` itself -- a harness bug, bisected before touching the gate.

A DISCLOSED HAZARD IS A CLAIM, AND IT INHERITS LIKE ANY OTHER. R311y418 recorded that a reviewer had reproduced a lock-desync sailing through pre-commit on a non-ASCII staged path. R311y419 carried it forward verbatim. Re-measuring it here did not confirm it: git escapes non-ASCII under the default core.quotePath, and even with quotePath=false and genuinely invalid UTF-8, GNU grep 3.7 returns the match. The real mechanism is narrower and was never named -- `grep` on the author's box is an EXPORTED SHELL FUNCTION (a ugrep wrapper) that suppresses the match, and hooks inherit exported functions. This is the same class as R311y418's own inherited "fired twice" count, one layer up: there the number was wrong, here the MECHANISM was. Re-measure a disclosure before fixing it; the fix you write for the wrong mechanism can be correct code aimed at nothing.

MY OWN FIRST REPRODUCTION WAS CONTAMINATED BY THE SAME WRAPPER. Measuring "does grep fail here" through a shell whose `grep` is a function measured the function, not grep. `type -a grep` / `command -v` before trusting any measurement that names a standard tool -- and prefer `command <tool>` inside a gate, so the gate does not inherit whatever the invoking shell has redefined.

GATE ORDERING IS A PROPERTY WORTH DESIGNING FOR. The three schema-pin gates now differ in WHEN they fire, not just in what they read: the store-vs-ceiling gate fires after a migration has landed, the co-change gate only proves two constants moved together, and the new wz_local_cli_pin_gate fires on the condition that CAUSES a migration, before the next mutate. All four historical firings (R311y15, y401, y406, y416) were discovered on hosted CI after the store had been committed and pushed -- which is a statement about ordering, not about coverage.

HARDENING BEFORE HOSTING KEEPS PAYING. Every one of the last three rounds found a real hole while preparing lanes to be hosted rather than in the lanes themselves: y419 found a `cargo test --test <bin>` selecting zero tests and exiting 0, and this round found all three subset matrices reading their SSOT through a process substitution whose exit status the reading loop cannot see -- an empty producer would have passed as a green matrix over zero rows. Round 311y420.decision_summary: R311y420 -- the five items R311y419 carried forward as unresolved, all closed, with one of them REFUTED on re-measurement rather than fixed as described. No wire, atom, inventory or Cargo change. (1) THE DISCLOSED grep HAZARD DID NOT REPRODUCE, and the mechanism that does is different and worse. R311y418 recorded a reviewer reproducing a lock-desync sailing through pre-commit on a non-ASCII staged path, mitigated only by the English-only policy. Re-measured: git escapes non-ASCII under the default core.quotePath, so grep never sees the bytes; and forcing core.quotePath=false with genuinely invalid UTF-8, GNU grep 3.7 still returns the match. What DOES reproduce is that `grep` on the author's box is an EXPORTED SHELL FUNCTION (a ugrep wrapper), which on the same input suppressed a valid match and returned 1 -- and git hooks inherit exported functions, so which grep graded a commit was environment-dependent. The first attempt to reproduce the disclosed claim was itself contaminated by that wrapper, which is how the distinction surfaced. Both staged-path filters now route through one `_staged_matching` helper using `command grep` (bypasses functions and aliases), `-a` (no implementation's binary-detection can suppress a match), and a hard block on rc>=2 (grep FAILING, which `|| true` had collapsed into "nothing staged", i.e. into a pass). A negative control proves the case discriminates: with a bare `grep` the hijack succeeds, with `command grep` it does not. (2) THE LAST mapfile IS OUT OF .githooks. mapfile is a bash 4.0 builtin and stock macOS ships 3.2, so pre-push could not run there at all; it is now a while-read loop, matching what scripts/lib/schema-pin-gate.sh already did. This is NOT a claim of repo-wide bash 3.2 support -- scripts/verify-codegen.sh still uses six, including `mapfile -d ''` forms that are awkward to express portably, and rewriting a working script for a platform nobody has asked for is the wrong trade. The hooks are the part a macOS clone must pass before it can commit at all. A scan for bash-4-only constructs caught this round introducing `${push_shas[-1]}` (negative subscripts are 4.3+) in the same commit that was removing the 4.0 dependency; it is index arithmetic now. (3) shellcheck IS PINNED, at 0.11.0 with a published sha256, out of the apt list and into its own step beside actionlint's. R311y417 assessed this exposure as "latent, not live" on the measurement that 0.8.0 / 0.9.0 / 0.10.0 agreed on this tree -- true when Layer 0 linted only the `run:` blocks inside .github/workflows/, and no longer true once R311y419 put scripts/*.sh, scripts/lib/*.sh and .githooks/* in scope. On THAT surface the versions disagree: 0.11.0 finds 5 SC2086 (unquoted `return $fail`) that 0.8.0 misses, all fixed here, plus SC2329, a check 0.8.0 does not have. 0.11.0 rather than the image's 0.8.0-2 because pinning to the floating value would freeze a 2021 release to avoid triaging its successors. SC2329 fires on 119 functions in run-ci.sh because every lane is reached through `run_layer <name> <fn>` invoking `"$@"`, which no static analysis can follow; that is the design, so it carries a FILE-scoped disable and stays live for the other 17 files. (4) THE PIN GATE NOW FIRES IN THE HOOKS, and earlier than the two that preceded it. R311y419 built scripts/verify-mnemosyne-pin.sh but ran it from the installer's tail, and hooks never install -- so it could not fire locally. It does not need to install: the hooks already require mnemosyne-cli on PATH and `describe-schema` is a pure report of the binary's own constant. wz_local_cli_pin_gate asks it directly, from pre-commit against the index ceiling and from pre-push against the pushed tip's. What it catches that the other two cannot is the ORDERING: wz_schema_pin_gate compares the STORE to the ceiling and so fires only once a migration has happened, and the co-change gate only proves two constants moved together; this one fires on the condition that CAUSES the migration, before the next mutate. That is exactly why R311y401, y406 and y416 were each discovered on hosted CI after the store had already been committed and pushed. Both directions block: ahead of the pin migrates the store past the reader CI installs, behind it cannot open a store the pin permits. (5) C4c / C4d / C1bf GATE HOSTED, closing the R311y332 gap R311y419 named and left open; hosted lanes 76 -> 79 of 107. Hardened first, and the hardening found a real hole: all three matrices read the subset SSOT through a PROCESS SUBSTITUTION, whose exit status the reading `while` loop cannot see, so an empty producer would have run zero iterations and returned 0 -- a matrix gate reporting success over an empty matrix. The floor was applied to C1j too, which has been HOSTED since R311y318 carrying the identical hole; closing it only for the lanes being moved would have knowingly left the worse one open. The A4 roll-up names them together, but mapping each atom's witnesses to the lanes that carry them shows two different failures. router-multicast-faces (5 witnesses) and transport-multicast (7) have EVERY witness in Layer M, which was opt-in and therefore ran on NO default path at all -- not hosted, not even the pre-push sweep. transport-link-vsock has ONE witness, and its lane (Z) IS hosted; the test echo-skips because the runner lacks the vsock_loopback kernel module and a vsock-enabled zenohd. codec-join, separately flagged as "promoted by a test hosted CI never runs", had all its `full` claims in Layer M too. LAYER M IS NOW HOSTED, on the interop job, with WZ_M_REQUIRE=1. That job already builds the zenoh-pico CLI these witnesses need, so a separate runner would pay that build again to gain nothing. WZ_M_REQUIRE makes every SKIP path fatal -- the opt-in guard itself and the pico-CLI prereq -- on the same rule as WZ_Z_REQUIRE: the job guarantees the CLI, so a SKIP would be a provisioning regression wearing a green badge and would silently restore the exact state this round closes. THE OPT-IN RATIONALE WAS RE-READ, NOT INHERITED. run-ci.sh kept the lane opt-in because multicast is "environment-dependent: a CI CONTAINER without a multicast route on the default interface drops the IGMP join". That is a claim about containers; GitHub's hosted runners are full VMs with a default route. The tests also use 224.0.0.224 -- the link-local control block -- joined with INADDR_ANY and set_multicast_loop_v4(true), so both ends are the same host and the datagram never leaves it. Measured locally: 5/5 green, 0 skips, 15-26s. None of that PROVES the runner can join, so the lane now prints a multicast preflight (routes, links, a real IGMP join attempt) before its first test; a failure is therefore readable as environment-versus-code in ONE run instead of an unexplained red. VSOCK GETS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A GUESSED GATE. Its two blockers differ in kind: the zenohd-vsock oracle is a known cached recipe (ZENOHD_VSOCK=1, exactly like the unixpipe variant already provisioned), but whether this runner image can load vsock_loopback is an unknown no local measurement can settle. Shipping a required lane on that guess would ship a probably-red gate; shipping one that skips green would be the hollow gate this repo keeps closing. So the interop job gains a probe step that ALWAYS exits 0, carries no proof, and reports uname / modprobe / lsmod / an AF_VSOCK bind attempt -- and the next round spends the oracle build only if the capability is real. The bookkeeping stays honest meanwhile: A4 still lists vsock under HOST_GATED_CI_TARGETS, still counts it as having no hosted witness, and assert_host_gated_ci_targets() falsifies that declaration in both directions. Writing the probe caught its own defect: `bind((CID, 0))` returns EACCES because port 0 on AF_VSOCK is a PRIVILEGED-port request, not "any port" -- it failed on the author's box, where the real vsock interop passes, so the probe would have reported a kernel problem that is not there. VMADDR_PORT_ANY (0xFFFFFFFF) is the sentinel. Result: PROVEN-WITH-NO-HOSTED-WITNESS 3 -> 1, PROMOTED-BY-AN-UNRUN-TEST 1 -> 0, hosted-executed proven 74 -> 77. No wire, atom, inventory or Cargo change. One commit: d42395c.

A CLAIM-WIRING ROUND AND A PRODUCT-CODE ROUND LOOK IDENTICAL FROM THE UNPROVEN LIST. R311y422's locator block was 6 atoms of pure wiring: every witness already existed and only the `wz-proves` line was missing. The scouting block has the same shape in A4's output and almost none of it is wiring -- one atom was wireable, one needed a new counter and log, and two need a CLI entrypoint that does not exist. Before estimating a block, trace one atom end to end: witness -> test -> lane -> hosted. The list tells you what is unproven, never what it costs.

A FLAG IS NOT A WITNESS. `--autoconnect` had been drivable for many rounds and logged "gossip-autoconnect enabled" -- a line that proves argument parsing. `summary.dialed` was equally useless because the static seed and reconcile bump it too. The fix was a counter with exactly one increment site plus a PAIRED assertion (1 on the gossip path, 0 on the static path), and the pair is the whole point: mirroring the increment makes the second assertion fail, which is what "discriminator" has to mean.

THE BLOCKER IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A MISSING TEST, and it is worth recording so the next attempt does not re-run these spikes: zenoh floods link-state on the ROUTER tier, so a wz PEER attached to zenohd sees `peak 2 node(s)` and never a dialable third party; a wz `--router-hat` node does receive the flood but its autoconnect matcher admits nobody by design (linkstate_forward.rs:232-233, mirroring zenoh). Either the demo needs a peer-tier gossip path that carries locators, or the proof needs a topology where the foreign side advertises a router the wz peer may dial.

NEXT, in cost order: (1) a demo entrypoint for ACTIVE multicast scouting -- one product-code slice that opens BOTH scouting-active and scouting-multicast, since the latter is FOUNDATIONAL and always-on under the former; zenohd answers on 224.0.0.224:7446 by default, Layer M is hosted, and the runner's IGMP join is measured, so only the entrypoint is missing. (2) scouting-autoconnect's precondition, which is a design question before it is a test. (3) The axis then has 36 unproven left, plus 37 `partial` to upgrade.

DO NOT wire layer3_scout / layer3_hello to scouting-active. They prove SCOUT/HELLO codec parity against pico's C source; the atom is the MODE ("indep of passive/static modes"). Containment would not refute it -- scouting-active is active, so containment applies, but it checks feature closure, not whether the test drives the mode. Same trap as locator-iface at R311y422.
