Round 311y423.decision_summary: R311y423 -- the four unproven scouting-* atoms, worked in order and reported by what each actually needs rather than as one task. ONE CLOSED, ONE'S WITNESS BUILT AND PROVEN, TWO BLOCKED BEHIND PRODUCT CODE -- and the blockers were established by running the real binaries, not inferred. (1) scouting-gossip CLOSED, by binding it to a witness that already existed and was already asserted. wz_router_hat_zenohd_interop's leg 1 asserts that wz DECODED at least one of zenohd's LinkStateList OAM floods -- `forwarder.ingested() > 0`, surfaced as the `learned mesh topology` shutdown line -- and that decode IS the atom (wz-routing-graph + linkstate_forward.rs, FOUNDATIONAL/always-on). The test's own comment already separates that assertion from the convergence tick it calls handshake-satisfiable, which is the R311y140 distinction; the claim binds to the decode, not to the link-up. zenohd->wz only: wz's own flood reaching zenohd is not asserted there, so no reverse claim was made. A4: proven 84 -> 85, unproven 39 -> 38, both populations still identical. (2) scouting-autoconnect's WITNESS did not exist and now does. The demo has driven `--autoconnect` since it was added, but the only log on that path says "gossip-autoconnect enabled" -- which proves the FLAG was parsed, not that anything was dialed -- and `summary.dialed` counts the static `--connect` seed and reconcile adds too, so asserting on either would credit the atom to a node autoconnect never moved. That is the hollow-witness shape R311y140 recorded. So `AcceptLoopSummary` gains `gossip_dialed`, incremented in exactly one place -- the `Step::Dial` arm, reachable only through a DialIntent the forwarder emits after the autoconnect policy admits a peer discovered in a link-state flood -- and the demo latches a shutdown line when it is > 0. The counter's DISCRIMINATION is proven rather than asserted: the existing autoconnect unit test now requires gossip_dialed == 1 and the existing static-dial test requires gossip_dialed == 0, and mirroring the increment at the static site makes that second assertion fail, verified. (3) scouting-autoconnect's cross-impl PROOF is blocked on a topology fact, measured twice with real binaries. A wz peer attached to a zenohd router learns `peak 2 node(s)` -- itself and that router -- with one zenohd and also with two linked zenohds. zenoh's link-state flood is ROUTER-TIER, so a peer-tier attachment never receives a dialable third party; and a wz node attached as `--router-hat` WOULD receive it, but linkstate_forward.rs:233 states the autoconnect matcher for a ROUTER admits nobody, mirroring zenoh. So the precondition the proof needs does not exist in the demo's current mode set. (4) scouting-active and scouting-multicast are blocked earlier still: the demo has NO entrypoint for active multicast scouting at all (args.rs:157 mentions it only in prose). zenohd answers scouts on 224.0.0.224:7446 by default and R311y421 both hosted Layer M and MEASURED the runner's IGMP join, so the execution environment is ready -- what is missing is one product-code entrypoint, after which a single test witnesses both (scouting-multicast is FOUNDATIONAL, "always-on under scouting-active"). NOT WIRED, deliberately: layer3_scout.rs and layer3_hello.rs prove SCOUT/HELLO codec parity against pico's C source, and scouting-active's F names that codec pair -- but a codec-parity test proves the BYTES match, not that wz actively scouts, and the atom's own note calls it a MODE ("indep of passive/static modes"). Claiming it there would be the same over-claim R311y422 caught with locator-iface, and containment would not have refuted it. Two commits: 843c0a8, 223c128.

Round 311y427.decision_summary: R311y427 -- the routing and adminspace groups hosted, which effectively closes the sole-runner class: 2 lanes and 2 selectors remain, from 21 and 44 when R311y425 first swept. AND IT CORRECTS R311y426, whose placement conclusion the very next measurement falsified. That round wrote that routing and adminspace "need their own runner", projecting them at the 4.3x hosted-to-local-median ratio R311y419 measured, which put feature-gates over its 45-minute ceiling. Hosted run 30267052174 then timed the eleven lanes R311y425 had added: 138s hosted against a 64s local median -- 2.2x, not 4.3x -- and the job as a whole moved only 14m37s -> 16m43s. The explanation is structural rather than noise: a lane APPENDED to a job that has already built the workspace reuses those artefacts, while the lanes the 4.3x came from did not. Recomputed at 2.2x these eight cost about 5.8 min (routing) and 4.0 (adminspace), landing the job near 26 min inside its existing ceiling. So no new runner, no budget change, and R311y426's "they need their own runner" is retracted here rather than inherited. That is the THIRD firing of the borrowed-ratio lesson in this arc and the first in the OVER-estimating direction; the durable form is that a borrowed ratio sizes a timeout and does not decide a placement. HARDENED FIRST, per the rule this arc has followed since R311y419: 42 filtered runs across the six pure-cargo lanes were all bare, and `cargo test <filter>` exits 0 on an empty selection, so each was one rename or cfg-slip from passing over nothing. All are now `_runci_guarded_test` at counts measured on this tree. Two things surfaced that guessing would have gotten wrong. C1ax ran four namespace e2e targets in ONE invocation, which prints four summaries of which two read `1 passed` -- an exact count would have matched the wrong line -- and measuring the targets individually showed the combined run's summary ORDER is not the target order (namespace_e2e is 4, namespace_query_e2e is 1, not the reverse the combined output suggests). Those four are now one guarded run per target. And a falsification came back GREEN: dropping `--features adminspace-core` from C1am's `--lib zid_hex` run left all 3 tests running, because that feature is not load-bearing for that filter. The guard was fine; the PERTURBATION was invalid, and the round re-falsified against `compiled_plugins`, where the feature genuinely gates, plus a count perturbation. RESULT: hosted lanes 93 -> 99, local-only 14 -> 8, sole-runner lanes 8 -> 2, orphan selectors 22 -> 2. The remaining two are E7b and E7c, `--ignored` integration tests in the interop genre that need foreign-binary provisioning, so they belong with the jobs that provide it rather than on feature-gates. One commit: 724be3a.

carry_forward_bullets: R311y428 built the entrypoint R311y423 named as the cheapest next item and closed BOTH atoms it was supposed to open: scouting-active and scouting-multicast are proven cross-impl against zenohd, A4 unproven 38 -> 36, and the leg runs on hosted CI (Layer M) rather than only locally.

THE BLOCKER WAS BIGGER THAN THE CARRY SAID, and the carry was not wrong so much as looking at the wrong layer. R311y423 recorded "the demo has NO entrypoint for active multicast scouting" -- true, and it read as "add a flag". The flag was the smallest part: wz/scouting-active was a declaration-only "= []" key, so NO facade consumer could reach the scouting FSM at all, and ScoutParams was unnameable through the facade, so the glue's own public constructor could not be CALLED from a facade consumer even with the feature on. Neither gap was visible from the demo's argv, and neither would have been found by grepping for the flag. When a carry says "only X is missing", check that X's dependencies are actually reachable from where X has to live.

RUNNING THE BINARY IS WHAT FOUND THE REAL DEFECT. The scouting witness lines went to a logger that was not yet initialised: the demo discovered the right locator, dialed it, and Established, while printing NOTHING about scouting. A test written against that binary would have asserted on a line it could never print, and it would have been a hollow proof of exactly the R311y140 shape -- except invisible, because every OTHER assertion would have passed. The lesson is narrow and repeatable: when a round's whole value is a witness LINE, run the binary and read the line before writing the assertion.

ASSERT ON SOMETHING THE SUBJECT WAS NEVER TOLD. This leg's discriminator is that zenohd binds tcp/127.0.0.1:0, the KERNEL picks the port, and the demo's argv carries no address at all -- so a log line naming that exact port can only have come from decoding zenohd's Hello. That is stronger than any assertion over values both sides knew in advance, and it is available whenever a test can let the foreign side CHOOSE something.

NEXT, in cost order. (1) scouting-autoconnect, the last unproven scouting atom, is a DESIGN question before it is a test: R311y423 measured that a wz peer attached to zenohd sees only "peak 2 node(s)" because zenoh floods link-state on the ROUTER tier, and that a wz --router-hat does receive the flood but its autoconnect matcher admits nobody (linkstate_forward.rs:232-233, mirroring zenoh). Either the demo needs a peer-tier gossip path carrying locators, or the proof needs a topology where the foreign side advertises a router the wz peer may dial. Nothing in this round touched that. (2) The axis has 36 unproven left plus 37 partial to upgrade.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, so a later round does not read these as oversights. --scout composes with --reconnect (the discovered locator becomes the reconnect target, since --scout only fills in what --connect would have named) but that combination has NO test; it is reachable and plausible, not proven. The scout does not RE-scout on reconnect, which matches pico's re-open-to-the-configured-endpoint shape rather than zenoh's continuously-scouting client. And the group address stays a constant rather than a CLI knob: an address the peers do not share discovers nothing, and zenoh exposes the override in its config file, not its scouting API.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: scout_for_peer_locator -- join 224.0.0.224:7446, emit a Scout, return the first locator a peer's Hello advertises, with the constants it needs (SCOUT_GROUP / SCOUT_PORT / SCOUT_WHAT=0x03 ROUTER|PEER / SCOUT_CYCLE_MS / SCOUT_TICK_MS). It REPEATS the cycle within the budget because drive_scouting_until_resolved is one cycle by construction (pico's __z_scout_loop shape, vendor/zenoh-pico/src/session/scout.c:57) and a single Scout races a responder still joining the group. Repetition is zenoh's own shape (Runtime::scout loops the send with a growing delay while receiving, zenoh net/runtime/orchestrator.rs:848-877); the exponential backoff deliberately is NOT mirrored, since that loop is an unbounded background task and this is a bounded startup budget.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: the witness log -- "scouted peer locator <loc> (scout_emit=N, record_hello=N)". The locator has exactly one producer, ScoutOutcome::Discovered, reachable only through record_hello_and_emit decoding a peer Hello; the FSM's own dispatch counters ride the same line so the claim binds to scouting.scxml's actions.

Round 311y428.decision_summary: R311y428 -- the product-code slice R311y423 named as next, and it opened BOTH atoms it was supposed to: scouting-active and scouting-multicast now have a cross-impl proof against zenohd, executed by hosted CI. THE MISSING PIECE WAS NOT THE FLAG. R311y423 recorded the blocker as "the demo has NO entrypoint for active multicast scouting", which reads as one CLI flag; the flag was the smallest of three gaps. The wz facade's scouting-active was a declaration-only "= []" key, so a consumer enabling it got the marker and NONE of the scouting code -- the multicast FSM was unreachable through the facade entirely, and the only way in was a direct wz-runtime-tokio dep that no facade consumer has. Second, ScoutParams was a PRIVATE use in scouting_glue, so the module's own public constructor ScoutingActions::new could not be CALLED through the facade -- its parameter type was unnameable there; the in-tree tests never hit it because they carry a wz-session-core dev-dep the facade's consumers lack. Both are now forwarded (AP-only, mirroring session-extauth: wz-runtime-coop has no scouting-active key, and inventing one would claim an MCU active-scouting path that does not exist). THE ENTRYPOINT IS A LOCATOR SOURCE, NOT A NODE KIND. --scout resolves the Initiator's connect locator by active multicast scouting before the role exists -- the active-mode twin of the static synth_static_locators bypass (docs/scouting-fsm.md 2.4.3) -- so everything downstream of the resolved string is the ordinary one-shot Initiator and needed no change; --router / --peer / --router-hat / --storage-host are separate node KINDS and this is deliberately not one. It repeats the scout cycle within a budget because drive_scouting_until_resolved is one cycle by construction (zenoh-pico's __z_scout_loop shape, scout.c:57) and a single datagram races a responder still joining the group; repetition is zenoh's own shape (Runtime::scout loops the send while receiving, orchestrator.rs:848-877), while its exponential backoff is deliberately NOT mirrored -- that loop is an unbounded background task, this is a bounded startup budget. MEASURED BEFORE BUILT: a hand-built wz-shaped SCOUT to 224.0.0.224:7446 returned a real zenohd HELLO (hdr 0x22, one locator "tcp/127.0.0.1:17447") that was DIALABLE, which is why the slice composes scout -> session-open instead of stopping at discovery. RUNNING IT FOUND THE DEFECT THAT MATTERED: with env_logger::init still downstream of the resolution, a real --scout run discovered and dialed the right locator while printing NO scouting line at all -- a test written against that binary would have asserted on a line it could never print, and every other assertion would still have passed. The init and banner moved up. THE ASSERTION IS SOMETHING THE DEMO WAS NEVER TOLD: zenohd binds tcp/127.0.0.1:0, the kernel picks the port, the demo's argv carries no address, so a log line naming that exact port can only have come from decoding zenohd's Hello. Three REDs prove the leg discriminates -- a zenohd with --no-multicast-scouting fails the readiness gate; a dial not derived from the scout fails the Established assertion; a witness locator not derived from the decode fails the port equality -- and a no-responder negative control emits 3 Scouts, records 0 Hellos, prints no witness and exits 1. carry_forward_bullets: R311y429 adopted mnemosyne's Round-783 citation gate and moved the pin to b867bfe2 (R786) in one commit. The gate is now ON for the author-written Rust: `crates`, `deploy`, `xtask` are scanned (790 files), `vendor` and `out` are declared excluded, and any NEW Rust tree that is neither will FAIL validate-workspace until someone says which it is. That is the intended behaviour, not a bug to work around -- if a new crate or demo dir reds the hook, add it to `paths` (or exclude it with a reason).

THE PIN CLASS HAS A SECOND SHAPE NOW, and it is the inverse of the first. Four prior firings were "the store drifted AHEAD of the pinned reader, discovered on hosted CI". This one was "the local reader gained a VALIDATOR the pin lacks, so the local hook reds while hosted CI is green". Same root (PATH binary != pin), opposite symptom. When validate-workspace fails locally, the first question is WHICH BINARY, not what the round changed: `mnemosyne-cli --version` against MNEMOSYNE_REV.

THE LESSON THIS ROUND COST THE MOST TO LEARN, and it is not about scouting: a MEASUREMENT and its EXPLANATION are two claims, and only the first was verified. R311y423 measured `peak 2 node(s)` correctly and then attached a causal story about zenoh ("floods link-state on the ROUTER tier, so a peer never receives a dialable third party") that was never checked against zenoh's source. The story was wrong, it was carried verbatim through y424, y428 and y429, and it shut the atom for seven rounds. When a carry says "blocked by <fact about a foreign system>", the fact is the thing to re-read first — the blocker, not the workaround.

WHAT THE FACT ACTUALLY IS, worth keeping because it governs every future wz-peer fixture: zenoh's `routing.peer.mode` is SUBSYSTEM-WIDE. `hat/mod.rs:275-281` picks `linkstate_peer::HatCode` for "linkstate" and `p2p_peer::HatCode` otherwise, and `DEFAULT_CONFIG.json5:240-241` says the option "needs to be set to the same value in all peers and routers of the subsystem". wz's ingest mirrors the FULL-linkstate path, so a wz peer belongs in a `linkstate` subsystem and EVERY zenohd in a wz peer fixture needs `--cfg routing/peer/mode:"linkstate"` — the router too, not just the peer. A default zenohd in that fixture is a misconfigured subsystem by zenoh's own rule, and its symptoms will look like wz bugs.

A NAMED, NOT-INVENTED GAP: wz implements only ONE of zenoh's two peer routing modes. `p2p_peer` (zenoh's DEFAULT `routing.peer.mode = "peer_to_peer"`) ingests via `process_linkstates_peer_to_peer` (network.rs:559-614) — no edge rebuild, no reachability prune — while wz's `LinkstateNetwork` always runs the full-linkstate path. So wz cannot join a DEFAULT-configured zenoh peer subsystem as a peer. This is a real capability gap, distinct from `scouting-autoconnect` (which is the POLICY, and is now proven), and it is nobody's atom yet. Naming it is the point; sizing it is a later round.

A DIVERGENCE LEFT IN PLACE DELIBERATELY: the demo hardcodes `AutoConnectStrategy::GreaterZid` (wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs) while zenoh's default is `always` (DEFAULT_CONFIG.json5 `autoconnect_strategy`, `defaults.rs` `Unique(Always)`), and there is no flag to reach the default. wz's own `autoconnect.rs` doc already records Always as zenoh's default, so this is a demo-surface expressiveness gap, not a policy bug — but it is why this round's test has to pin three zids, and any future autoconnect fixture will pay the same tax until a `--autoconnect-strategy` flag exists.

THE ZENOHD-SIDE ERROR is unexplained and should not be forgotten: `[Peers Network] Received LinkState from 2 with unknown link mapping 2` fires once on the router when wz floods, meaning one psid in wz's advertised links had no zid mapping on that link yet and zenohd dropped that edge (network.rs:527-539). Non-fatal today. It is a wz->zenohd flood-hygiene question, and the honest next step is to reproduce it minimally before theorising.

Round 311y430.decision_summary: R311y430 -- scouting-autoconnect, the last unproven scouting atom, is CLOSED cross-impl, and it needed NO product code: the blocker seven rounds of carries repeated was a mis-diagnosis of its own measurement. R311y423 measured a wz peer beside a zenohd seeing only "peak 2 node(s)" -- correct -- and then attached a causal story that was never checked: "zenoh floods link-state on the ROUTER tier, so a wz PEER attachment never receives a dialable third party". That is a claim about zenoh, and it is false. zenoh routing.peer.mode is SUBSYSTEM-WIDE, not per-node: hat/mod.rs:275-281 selects linkstate_peer::HatCode for "linkstate" and p2p_peer::HatCode otherwise, and DEFAULT_CONFIG.json5:240-241 states the option "needs to be set to the same value in all peers and routers of the subsystem". wz LinkstateNetwork ingest mirrors the FULL-linkstate path, so wz IS a linkstate-mode peer; y423 spike left its zenohd at the "peer_to_peer" default, which zenoh own rule forbids mixing. "peak 2 node(s)" was the documented consequence of a NON-UNIFORM subsystem, not a wall in the demo mode set -- so the FIXTURE was what had to change. THE PROOF is a three-node topology: a zenohd ROUTER, a THIRD-PARTY zenohd PEER listening beside it, and a wz --peer --autoconnect whose argv names ONLY the router; wz learns the third party listen port from the router LinkStateList and DIALS it, giving dialed 2 / accepted 0 and one gossip dial, with peak 3 node(s) where y423 saw 2. THE ASSERTION IS A PORT THE DEMO WAS NEVER TOLD, and it discriminates the DIRECTION of the dial rather than the existence of a mesh: with --autoconnect removed the mesh still forms, because the foreign peer own autoconnect dials wz instead, but the face then sits on a kernel-chosen SOURCE port and the leg REDS. Both REDs were planted and run, not argued -- restoring the "peer_to_peer" fixture also REDS the positive leg, at the 20s deadline. Join order is NOT a precondition, measured both ways (network.rs:860-864: the whatami==Router narrowing on the add_link delta applies only when NOT full_linkstate), so the test carries no inter-node gate. A4: proven 87 -> 88, unproven 36 -> 35, both populations identical; Layer Z, already hosted under WZ_Z_REQUIRE, runs the three legs. TWO THINGS NAMED AND NOT FIXED: wz implements only ONE of zenoh two peer routing modes (p2p_peer, zenoh DEFAULT, ingests via process_linkstates_peer_to_peer with no edge rebuild and no prune -- wz always runs the full path), and the demo hardcodes AutoConnectStrategy::GreaterZid where zenoh defaults to always, which is why this fixture must pin three zids.

carry_forward_bullets: ALL THREE ITEMS R311y430 LEFT OPEN ARE CLOSED, and none of them turned out to be what its carry said. The "unexplained" router error was a real wz divergence with a one-line cause; the strategy divergence was a missing flag; and the "wz implements only one of zenoh's two peer modes" gap was closable at the DISCOVERY plane without touching the data plane.

A DIVERGENCE WITH A WRITTEN RATIONALE IS STILL A CLAIM. `propagate`'s source-face exclusion carried a confident paragraph explaining why the echo was redundant. It was wrong, it had been wrong since the function was written, and no test covered it — the only thing that ever objected was a foreign implementation's ERROR log. When a comment says "a DELIBERATE divergence", treat the paragraph as the least-tested thing in the file. Same disease as R311y430's blocker prose, one layer down.

PSID SPACE IS PER-SENDER. This is the invariant behind both halves of the fix and it is easy to lose: a link-state's `links` array carries the SENDER's psids, so advertising a node to a peer is not the same as that peer being able to resolve it. Any change that omits a node from a flood must ask "does the receiver still have a mapping for every psid I am about to reference".

WHAT `--peer-mode peer-to-peer` DOES AND DOES NOT CLAIM. It switches the DISCOVERY plane — ingest, re-flood shape, and the add_link introduction — so a wz peer joins a stock zenoh subsystem, learns third parties and gossip-autoconnects there. It does NOT claim the DATA plane: wz routes along the linkstate spanning tree, and a gossip mesh has no edges to build one from (`peak 3 node(s)`, `0 graph edge(s)` in the proving run). zenoh's `p2p_peer` hat routes pubsub/queries by direct faces instead, and wz has no equivalent. That hat is the remaining half and is nobody's atom yet — name it before building it.

THE DEFAULT STAYS `linkstate` even though zenoh's is `peer_to_peer`, deliberately: wz's data plane implements linkstate, so defaulting to the other mode would ship a node whose discovery and routing disagree. Revisit only when the p2p data plane exists.

FLAKE-HUNTING RULE THIS ROUND PAID FOR: settle on the event you ASSERT, not on the event that motivates it. The neuter leg asserted `accepted 1` (a link the foreign peer opens after a 0-100ms backoff) while waiting on the flood, and passed three times in isolation before failing under sibling load. Isolation-green is not green.

Round 311y431.decision_summary: R311y431 -- the three items R311y430 left open, all closed, and not one of them was what its carry said. (1) THE UNEXPLAINED ROUTER ERROR was a real wz divergence with a one-line cause. zenoh propagate_link_states withholds only the UPDATED half from the source link (network.rs:661); NEW nodes ride back out on it. wz dropped the whole source face, on a written rationale -- "every node it would echo back was advertised BY that source, so the echo is redundant" -- that is false, because PSID SPACE IS PER-SENDER: the source knows that node under ITS numbering and nothing about ours, so our next self-entry naming that psid in links is unresolvable and zenohd rejects the edge. Read off the wire with zenohd tracing, and established as OURS rather than upstream by a pure-zenoh three-node control that logs the error ZERO times. (2) THE STRATEGY DIVERGENCE was a missing flag: --autoconnect-strategy now exists and DEFAULTS to always, which is zenoh default and was previously unreachable since the demo hardcoded GreaterZid; the opt-in carries the strategy inside an Option so "off, but with a strategy" is unrepresentable. (3) THE PEER-MODE GAP is closed at the DISCOVERY plane. LinkstateNetwork gains zenoh full_linkstate flag plus process_linkstates_peer_to_peer -- no edge rebuild, no reachability prune -- because running a gossip flood through the linkstate ingest makes every links-less entry unreachable and the trailing GC deletes the node the flood just introduced. That is literally observable as "pruning detached node" in the wrong mode. A second, INDEPENDENT fix was needed and only running found it: in gossip mode the add_link 2-entry delta must be unconditional (zenoh own condition), since the gossip re-flood relays direct neighbours only and would otherwise never introduce the freshly-dialed peer. wz now gossip-autoconnects inside a STOCK zenoh subsystem -- no routing/peer/mode on either zenohd -- with the router logging no error. NOT CLAIMED, and named rather than blurred: the p2p_peer DATA plane. wz routes along the linkstate spanning tree and a gossip mesh has no edges to build one from, so --peer-mode peer-to-peer switches discovery only; the default stays linkstate because that is the mode wz whole stack implements. The interop file goes 3 legs to 7 (two new PAIRS plus the router-log regressions), and a REAL FLAKE was root-caused rather than retried: a leg that asserted a link the foreign peer opens after its 0-100ms backoff was settling on the flood instead, green in isolation and red under sibling load. Layer Z green, A4 unchanged at 88/37/35.
verification_bullets: THE DEFECT WAS READ OFF THE WIRE, not inferred. With zenohd tracing `zenoh::net::protocol::network`, the router logged wz sending `[LinkState { psid: 0, sn: 3, zid: None, links: [1, 2] }]` — a links-only self entry naming psid 2 — while the mappings it had ever received from wz were psid 0 and psid 1 only. Hence `ERROR ... Received LinkState from 2 with unknown link mapping 2` (zenoh `network.rs:527-539`).

IT IS wz's BUG AND NOT UPSTREAM BEHAVIOUR, established by a PURE-ZENOH control rather than by reading: the identical three-node linkstate topology with a zenohd peer in wz's place logs `unknown link mapping` ZERO times across all three processes. Its trace shows why — the zenoh peer sends `[psid 2, sn 2, zid Some(1), links [1]]` (the new node, WITH its zid) before the links-only self entry that references psid 2.

AFTER the `propagate` fix, wz's wire matches that shape: the router now receives `[LinkState { psid: 2, sn: 2, zid: Some(1), whatami: Peer, links: [1] }]` first and the links-only self entry second, and logs no error.

UNIT RED for the propagate fix: the new `propagate_sends_new_nodes_back_to_the_source_face` fails with the old whole-source-face exclusion (`assertion left == right failed: the NEW node must ride back out on the source face`) and passes with it. The same test also pins the per-node exclusion (the other face gets the updated half only, links-only) so the fix cannot be over-applied.

CROSS-IMPL RED for the propagate fix: restoring the old exclusion makes leg 1 fail on the router-log assertion ALONE (`wz-integration-tests/.../wz_gossip_autoconnect_zenohd_interop.rs:352`) — every other assertion in that leg still passes, so the assertion is bound to this fix and nothing else.

THE GOSSIP-MODE HALF NEEDED A SECOND FIX, found by running rather than by reasoning: with `--peer-mode peer-to-peer` the router STILL logged one `unknown link mapping`, because the gossip re-flood relays direct neighbours only, so the newly-dialed peer was never introduced by that path either. Making `flood_link_added`'s 2-entry delta unconditional in gossip mode (zenoh's own condition) drops it to zero, verified against a stock zenohd.

THE MODE SWITCH, proven as a PAIR against a STOCK zenoh subsystem (no `routing/peer/mode` on either zenohd, so both run zenoh's `peer_to_peer` default). `--peer-mode peer-to-peer`: `discovered peer 01 reachable at ["tcp/127.0.0.1:17902"]`, `face 1 UP (peer 127.0.0.1:17902, zid 01)`, `dialed 2, accepted 0`, `autoconnected to gossip-discovered peer(s) (1 dial(s))`, `peak 3 node(s)`. `--peer-mode linkstate`, same fixture: `pruning detached node Zid(01)`, `peak 2 node(s)`, `dialed 1`, no gossip line — the reachability GC deleting the announcement, observed directly.

UNIT TWIN for the mode switch: `gossip_ingest_keeps_a_links_less_node_the_linkstate_ingest_prunes` feeds ONE builder-produced gossip announcement to two receivers differing only in the flag; RED-checked by neutering `set_full_linkstate` to ignore its argument, which fails it. A second test pins `gossip_reflood_admits` (direct neighbours only until multihop).

THE STRATEGY PAIR, on a fixture where wz's zid is the LOWER so the two values must disagree: `always` reports `1 dial(s)` and `dialed 2, accepted 0`; `greater-zid` reports no gossip line and `dialed 1, accepted 0`. Same topology, same discovered peer, one flag apart.

carry_forward_bullets: A GATE LIST RECITED IS NOT A GATE SET ENUMERATED. R311y431's verification named clippy on three crates as "the FULL Layer Z feature set" and it was not the full CRATE set -- the one crate it had just written a file into was missing. The rule that survives: after editing a file, the crate that OWNS that file is in the gate set, and no amount of feature-set thoroughness elsewhere substitutes. Same disease as the negative-claim lesson, applied to gates instead of claims.

A COUNT PIN INVALIDATES IN CLUSTERS, and the guard's early return hides the rest. `_runci_guarded_test` returns on the first mismatch, so hosted CI reported ONE stale count out of two that the same new test had broken. When a pinned count moves, re-measure every OTHER pin that shares the filter before assuming CI showed you the whole blast radius.

A DRIFT THAT REPORTS AS AN ABSENCE GETS DIAGNOSED AS ONE. The stale MCP server surfaced to the client as `Connection closed`, which reads identically to "no server configured", so two rounds of sessions treated a broken pin as a missing feature. When a capability is reported unavailable, drive the underlying tool by hand ONCE before accepting the absence -- the real diagnostic was one pipe away the whole time.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT CAUSED IT IS STILL THERE, deliberately. `mnemosyne-mcp` remains outside the CI installer because CI never speaks MCP, so nothing in a hosted run will ever notice the two binaries diverging again. The mitigation is entirely documentary -- CLAUDE.md step 1 plus the new script -- and that is weaker than a gate. If this recurs, the honest next step is a local hook check that the PATH server answers `initialize`, not more prose.

DO NOT STRENGTHEN THE NEW SCRIPT INTO A VERSION-STRING MATCH. It is the obvious "improvement" and scripts/verify-mnemosyne-pin.sh:46-55 already argues it out for the CLI: `--version` embeds `git describe`, so it is a bare short hash only while no tag is reachable upstream and becomes `unknown` with no .git. The handshake grades the property actually wanted -- can this server serve THIS workspace -- and does not depend on another project's tagging policy.

THE HOSTED VERDICT IS STILL OPEN. This round fixed the two lanes that failed and re-ran exactly those two locally; it did not re-run Layer Z, and it cannot pronounce on the run as a whole until a push produces one. Treat `main` as red until a hosted run says otherwise.

Round 311y432.decision_summary: R311y432 -- main was RED, and the round that reddened it had recited a gate list that looked exhaustive. Both failures on run 30324520884 (12/14) came from R311y431 and both sat OUTSIDE that list. (1) Layer C2 clippy: `//!   4/5.` in the scouting-autoconnect interop file is not an ordered-list marker, so `clippy::doc_lazy_continuation` read it as a lazy continuation of item 3 and `-D warnings` refused the crate. y431 ran clippy on wz-routing-graph, wz-runtime-tokio and wz-ap-demo -- and named that as the FULL Layer Z feature set -- but never on wz-integration-tests, the crate whose file it had just written. A COUNT IS A CITATION: adding a test invalidates it, and the invalidation is not local to the one line CI happened to reach. So two rounds of sessions ran with the Mnemosyne concept resources unreachable and no session diagnosed it; this one did only because the kickoff reported the absence instead of routing around it. Closed by scripts/install-mnemosyne-mcp.sh, which READS the rev through scripts/lib/schema-pin-gate.sh rather than carrying a second copy of the hash, and proves the install with a real `initialize` handshake against this workspace. carry_forward_bullets: A GREEN CROSS-IMPL LEG CAN WITNESS THE WRONG LAYER. The first hand-driven run of this slice passed with a 20-byte payload and proved nothing about lz4: keep-only-if-smaller had cleared the COMPRESSION bit, so the batch went out RAW and zenohd routed it exactly as an un-negotiated one. The negotiation flag was true the whole time, which is what made it convincing. For any atom whose wire form is CONDITIONAL on the data (compression, batching, fragmentation), the fixture has to be sized so the condition provably holds, and the sizing belongs in the test's prose where the next reader will see it.

A FAILURE THAT LOOKS LIKE YOUR SUBJECT NEEDS A CONTROL BEFORE IT NEEDS A DIAGNOSIS. The 4121-byte payload not arriving read as "compression breaks on large batches" and would have become a carried blocker. One run without --compression killed that reading in seconds. Same shape as R311y430's mis-diagnosis and R311y423's blocker: the measurement was right, the explanation was an unchecked claim.

THE DEFAULT-FEATURES WORKSPACE CLIPPY IS BLIND TO EVERY MODE ATOM'S DEMO ARM, and this round proved it rather than inferring it (C2 exit=0 with a planted useless_format in both witness blocks). transport-lowlatency had carried that hole since R311y372. Round 311y434.decision_summary: R311y434 -- wz composed two transport modes in an order zenoh does not, and a test was holding the divergence in place. R311y433 disclosed it as a carry: wz wraps lz4 compression OUTSIDE the lowlatency lean encode, so a session that negotiated both emitted a compressed lean wire. zenoh never produces that. Its establishment sets is_lowlatency on the transport config and is_compression on the link BatchConfig independently, so both flags CAN be true -- upstream config makes lowlatency exclusive with qos, not with compression -- but the lean transport serializes straight to the link behind a 4-byte length prefix and never touches WBatch or BatchHeader, and its lean rx never decompresses. Upstream the negotiated wrap is simply INERT on a lean link. So this was not a superset: superset means wz can do MORE, and a wire no zenoh peer can read is less. THE FIX IS A DATA-PATH CORRECTION, NOT A HANDSHAKE ONE, which is the whole design question this round had to settle. wz keeps offering and merging the 0x6 ext exactly as zenoh does, so Init/Open stays byte-identical for the same config; only the wrap is suppressed. That split now has a name in the code: is_compression reports the NEGOTIATED capability, compresses_batches reports whether the wrap is ACTIVE, and the bug was reachable precisely because one flag was answering both questions. Both the TX wrap and the RX un-wrap consult the single predicate, because a hand-maintained pair of conditions is exactly how a build ends up wrapping what it will not un-wrap, and that failure is silent on the wire. THE TEST THAT HAD TO BE REWRITTEN IS THE LESSON. transport_compose_e2e was written to answer a review saying the three modes were designed to compose and verified by a clippy pass; it did capture a real three-layer wire and assert it. It was still wrong, because the composition was never read against the reference impl -- each single-mode leg matched zenoh, the composed one matched only wz. It is now an option-atom PAIR: with lowlatency the wire leads with the bare lean Push and compresses_batches is false while is_compression stays true; dropping ONLY the lowlatency offer brings the BatchHeader back, which is the leg that catches an over-broad suppression. Both REDs were measured separately, and the byte assertion had to be provoked on its own because the invariant assertion panics first and would have left the bytes unexercised. WHAT THIS ROUND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM: a cross-impl witness for the composed session. No leg dials zenohd with both modes, because the demo cannot stage both offers -- session_open has one entrypoint per MODE. R311y433 guarded that combination for a reason that this fix makes false, so the guard survives with its justification replaced by the real one, a local API limit, and widening session_open to an offer SET is named as the next slice rather than smuggled into a bug fix.

carry_forward_bullets: ONE THRESHOLD ACROSS THIRTEEN SUBJECTS IS TWO BUGS, NOT A COMPROMISE. The global 1024B was simultaneously too low to catch a regression in a 74KB codec and too high for a near-zero one, and the second half is what produced the SOFT-SKIP list: five of thirteen lanes exempted, judging nothing, and the list only ever grew. A per-subject pin fixes both at once and deletes the exemption mechanism rather than curating it. Look for the same shape wherever one constant grades a population whose real values span orders of magnitude.

A PINNED NEAR-ZERO BEATS AN EXEMPTION. codec-fragment measures 0 and codec-scout/hello measure -144; exempting them said "we do not judge this", while pinning them at -256 says "this is what it is, tell me when it changes". The pinned form also catches a RISE, which the exemption could not -- if a near-zero codec suddenly elides 8KB, something was re-pulled that was not before, and that is worth seeing.

THE FLOOR-MISSING BRANCH IS THE ONE TO KEEP HONEST. Codec features are auto-enumerated from preset-ap-client, so the table can silently fall behind the catalog. Making an unpinned codec FAIL is what stops the table from decaying into a partial gate the way the SOFT-SKIP list did. If a future round finds this branch annoying, that is the branch working.

When that refactor lands it must re-pin `[codec-close]` with both numbers in its ledger entry, which is precisely the deliberate re-pin this gate is designed to force.

Round 311y436.decision_summary: R311y436 -- Layer F graded thirteen codecs with one number, and that number was wrong in both directions at once. The 1024-byte global threshold was TOO LOW to catch a regression in a large codec (codec-response elides 74472 bytes; it could have lost 98.6 percent of that and still cleared the bar) and TOO HIGH for the small ones, which is what produced the hand-maintained SOFT-SKIP list: codec-scout, codec-hello, codec-join, codec-fragment and codec-keep-alive were exempt, judging nothing, and the list only ever grew. Five of thirteen lanes graded nothing. R311y435 established where that ends -- a gate whose exemptions absorb its own subject matter reports green forever -- and this round applies the same lesson one level up. THE GLOBAL THRESHOLD IS DELETED, replaced by CODEC_DELTA_FLOOR: a pinned minimum elision delta per codec, measured at 49f2ea9 and carried with a margin far above the observed run-to-run noise of plus-or-minus 32 bytes. Every lane is judged now, and the exemption MECHANISM is gone rather than curated: a near-zero codec is pinned AT near-zero, which is strictly more informative than exempting it because a jump upward becomes visible too. Two branches make the table honest. An unpinned codec FAILS (FLOOR MISSING) instead of passing silently -- codec features are auto-enumerated from preset-ap-client, so without that branch the table would quietly fall behind the catalog exactly as the SOFT-SKIP list did. And a floor that the build cannot meet FAILS with both legitimate causes named: a consumer re-pulling the codec, which is the catalog-truthfulness defect this gate exists to catch, or a refactor consolidating the paths the codec used to own, which is legitimate but must be re-pinned deliberately with before/after numbers in the ledger -- never by lowering the constant alone, the same rule MNEMOSYNE_MAX_SCHEMA carries and for the same reason. The first is a live divergence, the third is latent. The Z-flag fix belongs in sources/codecs/*.scxml, not in out/ -- that tree is generated.

TWO FINDINGS ARE DEFECTS RATHER THAN RESIDUALS AND DESERVE THEIR OWN ROUNDS. access-acl is fail-OPEN where zenoh is fail-CLOSED on an unresolvable keyexpr (interceptor/access_control.rs:104-106 vs zenoh's :390-492), so an undeclared expr-id bypasses the ACL. session-extshm offers a UNIT ext at establishment id 0x2 where zenoh declares ZBuf, and its code comment has the failure mode backwards -- an SHM-DISABLED zenoh skips it harmlessly, an SHM-ENABLED one misparses. No cross-impl leg covers either.

transport-qos IS THE LARGEST SINGLE RESIDUAL FOUND AND ITS REASON HAD DISCLOSED NONE OF IT. The wire layer is bit-exact, but wz writes synchronously on the calling thread, so there are no per-priority TX queues and therefore no temporal priority at all -- a Background message enqueued first leaves before a RealTime one. zenoh keeps an independent StageIn/StageOut per priority and drains them in ascending order (common/pipeline.rs:666-765, 899-914). Queue-depth config and per-priority congestion drop-vs-block are absent with it.

The advanced-pubsub plane had NO foreign counterparty of any kind before this round -- every test was wz to wz, and a wz to wz pair agrees on a wrong dialect because the same wrong spelling sits on both ends. The oracle could not be zenohd (a router holds no AdvancedCache) or zenoh-pico (no advanced-pubsub plane at all), so it is upstream's own zenoh-ext example applications, now provisioned by build-zenohd.sh and given their own A4 proof class rather than being mislabelled as zenohd. THE MEASUREMENT CORRECTED THE STORY THE LEDGER WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE TOLD: the two defects COMPOUND rather than add, because under ampersand the whole selector reads to zenoh as one _max value that swallows the _anyke token too, so reverting the separator alone yields zero recovered samples and not the uncapped five that treating them as independent predicts. A control leg also caught one of the proof legs asserting vacuously, counting reply refusals on a stream that never carries them. A prior in-round measurement was retracted after the binary was found to predate the flag it was supposed to exercise. A4 proven 90 to 94, unproven 33 to 29; A3 correctly unchanged at 89.

Every finding below was re-verified against source or by measurement before being acted on.

THE TIMING BLOCKER WAS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. The reviewer instrumented the budget between the pre-join boundary read and the oracle's next publish: 513-515 ms over ten runs, and a sawtooth in the oracle's own session-open delay, so a slower runner can drive it toward zero. Injected-delay sweep: 0/200/400 ms pass, 600/800/1000 ms fail, with a message that reads like a dialect regression. That is a PERSISTENT red on an unlucky machine, not a flake. The bracketed assertion widens the tolerance from ~0.5 s to the run's whole publish span (pa-pb, about 4 s here) while staying discriminating -- re-measured: 2 red / 2 green on the pre-fix wire, 4 green after, and 3 consecutive clean repeats.

A COUNT PIN WAS INVALIDATED AND THE FIX WAS TO MOVE THE CODE, NOT RAISE THE PIN. carry_forward_bullets: R311y443 = the first foreign witness for ext-pubsub-advanced-recovery, obtained by INDUCING the loss the path needs. A4 proven 94 -> 95, unproven 29 -> 28. The vehicle is R311y438's counting relay taught to DROP: it already forwarded verbatim while counting, and one more branch turns it into a deterministic fault injector.

THE LESSON WORTH KEEPING IS ABOUT WHAT A RELAY CAN DROP. The obvious fault -- "drop the Nth data push" -- is unwritable, because there is no transport MID for a data push: application messages ride inside T_MID_FRAME together with every Declare, Request and Response. Matching the PAYLOAD instead is not a shortcut around that; it is strictly better for a test, because the fault becomes deterministic AND named, so the assertion can say which sample was removed and the control twin can say the same one is missing. Any future loss-recovery leg should reach for the same shape.

THE SECOND LESSON IS THE LANE. Layer E's catch-all sweep skips by test-fn NAME substring (zenoh_ext), and it runs a wz-ap-demo built WITHOUT --features advanced. NEW bind_multicast_tx_v4 is the send-only half, the wz counterpart of zenoh's separate ucast_sock (multicast.rs:264-290): ephemeral bind plus the egress pin, no join and deliberately no IP_MULTICAST_LOOP. wz already had zenoh's two-socket split at a higher level -- router egress spawns an ephemeral sender while ingress joins -- what it lacked was the pin on either.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/multicast_glue.rs: spawn_router_mcast_egress and spawn_router_mcast_ingress take Option<String> (owned, it crosses into the spawned task); egress moves off its inline bare bind onto bind_multicast_tx_v4, so a narrowed egress fails LOUDLY rather than sending out an interface the deploy did not name.

crates/wz-ap-demo: NEW --multicast-locator udp/GROUP:PORT#iface=NAME, parsed by the SHARED wz_session_core::locator parser (already re-exported at wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs:183, so no new facade surface). Spelled as a LOCATOR on purpose: this atom is about honouring a locator tail, so a honor reachable only through a Rust parameter would leave its semantic unclosed. A malformed value, a non-udp proto or an IPv6 group is a HARD ERROR. The router's egress and ingress now share ONE resolved group where they were two independent const pairs that happened to agree. The SCOUT group stays unnarrowed -- a discovery beacon must reach every interface a peer could answer on, and zenoh scopes UDP_MULTICAST_IFACE to a group locator too.

crates/wz-ap-demo/Cargo.toml: NEW locator-iface feature key, not in default. Needed for the proof to count at all, not merely to build it: the A4 gate requires every active atom a proof CLAIMS to sit inside the feature closure of a crate the proof builds, and locator-iface was in NEITHER the wz-integration-tests nor the wz-ap-demo closure.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml: transport-multicast now pulls link-interfaces. It was the sole multicast entry point that did not (scouting-active reaches it via transport-link-udp), so the resolver was unreachable from a multicast-only build. Same shape as transport-link-tcp / -udp / -ws.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_quic_acceptor_iface_zenohd_interop.rs: NEW cross-impl A/B on ONE real zenohd dial. Same binary, same dial, same cert; one token differs. #iface=lo establishes, #iface=<a non-lo NIC> does not, because SO_BINDTODEVICE delivers only packets that ARRIVED on the named device and a datagram to 127.0.0.1 arrives on lo. Both arms assert the (quic) listen tag, so arm B is a DELIVERY negative and not a bind failure -- bind(127.0.0.1) succeeds with a foreign device bound. A SEPARATE FILE because the sibling quic acceptor leg is count-guarded at 1 passed. No pico hop: pico has no quic at all, and the Established-vs-not pair IS the discriminator.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/quic_e2e.rs: NEW wz<->wz DELIVERY A/B, the same discriminator inside the crate that owns the code. Delivery-based on purpose: an implementation that device-binds a socket, drops it, and still calls the convenience constructor passes both a "binding to lo works" test and an "absent device gives ENODEV" test.
crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/multicast_pubsub_loopback.rs: NEW multicast pin A/B on real sockets, receiver joined on lo against egress pinned elsewhere, on a DEDICATED 239.0.0.0/8 group.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/link_interfaces.rs tests: the selector policy (address literal, name, absent name refuses) plus a carrier cross-check that compares the IFF_RUNNING verdict against sysfs for EVERY host interface -- an independent source, and the right one, since sysfs's flags file omits IFF_RUNNING while getifaddrs reports it.

Round 311y454.decision_summary: R311y454 -- the locator-iface atom CLOSES, and both grading axes move in one round for the first time in five: A3 REMAINING WORK 87 to 86 EXACT and A4 unproven 22 to 21. All three named residuals fall. The QUIC and quic-datagram LISTEN halves now honour the iface tail through one shared seam that pre-binds the UDP socket, applies SO_BINDTODEVICE and hands it to quinn Endpoint::new rather than the convenience constructor that owns its own socket -- the identical route zenoh takes, and the exact mirror of wz s own dial arm. The UDP multicast semantic, previously absent entirely, pins BOTH directions: imr_interface on the join and IP_MULTICAST_IF on egress, the pair zenoh splits across two sockets and wz already split at a higher level without pinning either. The honor is reachable as a LOCATOR, not as a bespoke flag, because this atom is about honouring a locator tail and a knob would have left its semantic unclosed. THREE THINGS THIS ROUND GOT WRONG AND CORRECTED BEFORE SHIPPING, each by measurement rather than argument. First, the planned deliberate divergence was not one: zenoh is ALSO hard-error for a not-found, down or carrier-less interface, and its silent fallback fires in exactly one narrower case, so the broad claim would have been a false ledger statement. Second, my own four-case multicast measurement said a pico-driven A/B would discriminate; it will not, because my probe had one joining socket while the real interop topology requires both stacks to co-bind, and IP_MULTICAST_ALL then makes the per-socket pin invisible -- reproduced independently before accepting the refutation, so the multicast half is recorded as not foreign-observable on a single host and the A4 witness is the QUIC A/B alone. Third, the resulting multicast test was FLAKY, passing alone and failing in its file s concurrent run, and the cause was the same mechanism at a different scale: the leaking membership is per group and device, not per port, so a unique port was never enough and a dedicated group was. Fixed, re-damaged to confirm it still discriminates, run clean three times. The proof is an A/B on ONE real zenohd dial differing in a single token, with both arms asserting the listen tag so the negative is a DELIVERY failure and not a bind failure, plus a delivery-based wz-internal twin that exists specifically to catch an implementation that device-binds a socket and then drops it -- a bug that would pass both an it-works-on-lo test and an absent-device-gives-ENODEV test. Two syscall facts were measured because the documentation answers neither: SO_BINDTODEVICE works unprivileged, which means the pre-existing dial-side honor has always actually worked and nobody had checked, and an absent device returns ENODEV. A FOURTH upstream honor site was found and deliberately NOT claimed: iface also filters which addresses a wildcard listener advertises, and wz has no wildcard expansion at all, so that residual belongs to the absent locator-advertisement capability and COMPLETE is scoped in writing to the socket-bind semantic. Closed as a side effect: Layer C1bd, the atom s own lane since R311y236, both ran nowhere hosted and only clippy-compiled the honor path -- it is now registered in ci.yml and executes it.
verification_bullets: BOTH AXES MOVED, WHICH THE LAST FOUR ROUNDS DID NOT MANAGE TOGETHER. A3 REMAINING WORK 87 to 86 EXACT (COMPLETE 50 to 51, PARTIAL 81 to 80, UNAUDITED still 0 of 130) and locator-iface is gone from the remaining-work list. A4 unproven 22 to 21 and partial 39 to 40 on BOTH populations, all-lanes and hosted-CI-executed; corpus 121 files / 255 tests to 122 / 256. The A3 move needed the inventory tag AND invariant #6, which requires a test naming the atom's OWN gated code -- the atom's gated symbol is multicast_iface_selector_v4, so the three selector policy tests are what makes COMPLETE admissible rather than merely asserted.

EVERY NEW ASSERTION WAS DAMAGE-TESTED, FIVE FOR FIVE, EACH REDDING ONLY ITS OWN TEST AND EACH PROVING ITS REBUILD: building the device-bound socket and then DROPPING it (quinn's convenience constructor still called -- the bind-then-drop bug) reds only the quic listen A/B while its sibling e2e passes; the join falling back to INADDR_ANY reds only the multicast A/B while the four other multicast tests pass; the egress IP_MULTICAST_IF pin going no-op likewise; the IFF_RUNNING rejection never firing reds only the sysfs carrier cross-check; an absent interface reporting Undetermined instead of NotFound reds only the policy-boundary test. None escaped into a compile error: each damage kept its variable used deliberately.

THE CROSS-IMPL DAMAGE NEEDED AN EXPLICIT DEMO REBUILD, AND SAYING SO MATTERS. The fixture launches the wz-ap-demo BINARY, a separate artifact from the crate cargo test rebuilds, so damaging the library and re-running the test would have exercised a stale binary and read exactly like damage-not-caught. With cargo build -p wz-ap-demo forced, arm B reported STILL completed the handshake and redded.

THE MULTICAST A/B WAS FLAKY AND WAS ROOT-CAUSED, NOT REVERTED. It passed alone and FAILED inside its file's concurrent run. Cause, measured: IP_MULTICAST_ALL defaults to 1 and the leaking membership is per (group, device) -- the PORT only decides which socket receives what the membership already admitted. A sibling test joining 224.0.0.224 with INADDR_ANY installs a host membership on the default-route device, and arm B, whose egress is pinned to that device, then receives its own datagram on a port nothing else binds. Fixed with a DEDICATED 239.0.0.0/8 group, then re-damaged to confirm the fixed test still discriminates, then run three times clean. My own earlier reasoning that a unique PORT sufficed was wrong.

THE PRE-CODE DESIGN PANEL REFUTED MY OWN MEASUREMENT, WHICH IS THE ROUND'S SHARPEST FINDING. I had measured a four-case multicast matrix and concluded a pico-driven join/egress A/B would work. It does not: my probe had exactly ONE joining socket, while the real pico interop topology requires BOTH stacks to wildcard-bind with SO_REUSEADDR/SO_REUSEPORT to co-exist on one host, and that co-bind is precisely what makes the pin invisible. Reproduced independently before accepting it: with a peer co-joined on a real NIC, a lo-joined socket still receives that NIC's traffic. So the multicast half is recorded as NOT foreign-observable on a single host, and the A4 witness is the QUIC listen A/B alone.

THE PANEL ALSO REFUTED THE ROUND'S PLANNED DIVERGENCE. I had intended to record a deliberate hard-error divergence against zenoh's silent fallback. zenoh is ALSO hard-error for not-found / not-up / not-running: get_unicast_addresses_of_interface bails on all three (zenoh-util/src/net/mod.rs:233-247) and zenoh-link-udp propagates with ? (multicast.rs:229). The fallback fires in ONE case only -- an interface up and running but carrying no address of the group's family. Verified by direct read before narrowing the claim; recording the broad version would have been a false statement in the ledger.

TWO SYSCALL FACTS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, BECAUSE THE DOCUMENTATION DOES NOT ANSWER EITHER. SO_BINDTODEVICE succeeds UNPRIVILEGED (euid 1000, on lo and on a real NIC) -- which also means the pre-existing dial-side honor has always actually worked, something the project had never checked. An absent device name returns ENODEV(19); man 7 socket documents the delivery semantic but not that errno, so the negative arm could not have been designed on the page alone.

A FOURTH UPSTREAM HONOR SITE WAS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED. get_locators() reads BIND_INTERFACE to filter which local addresses a WILDCARD-bound listener ADVERTISES (zenoh-link-commons/src/listener.rs:115-144). wz has no counterpart because wz has no wildcard-to-concrete locator expansion at all -- one is_unspecified use in the entire runtime, and get_locators appears only in comments citing zenoh. The residual therefore belongs to the absent locator-advertisement capability, not to this atom, and COMPLETE is scoped to the socket-bind semantic in the inventory reason.

scripts/run-ci.sh (Layer C0): NEW skip-token naming gate. For every fixture under crates/wz-integration-tests/tests whose BASENAME carries a Layer E skip token, every #[test] / #[tokio::test] fn must carry at least ONE token from the set. Round 311y455.decision_summary: R311y455 -- a HOSTED RED inherited from R311y453 is diagnosed and fixed, and the hazard that caused it is finally gated. R311y453 added a subject-scoping cross-impl fixture whose FILE name carried the wz_peer family token but whose two test FUNCTIONS did not. libtest --skip matches the TEST name, which for an integration test is the function name, so Layer E s default sweep did not exclude them: it ran both against the DEFAULT demo binary, the demo refused --peer for want of the routing-peer feature, and the hosted run for 2ab214a4 went red at Layer E. The fixture itself is sound -- Layer E6, which owns the routing-peer build, runs it two passed -- so what failed was routing, not the proof. Both functions now carry the token, and Layer E selects zero of them while E6 still selects both, each measured rather than assumed. THE PART WORTH KEEPING IS THE GATE. run-ci.sh had ALREADY written this hazard down, at the E4i lane in R311y449, in as many words: the token is a naming obligation that no gate enforces. Six rounds later R311y453 walked into it. A documented-but-ungated hazard is one that recurs, so Layer C0 now enforces the obligation: any fixture under wz-integration-tests whose basename declares an excluded family must have every test function carry at least one skip token. The gate was falsified before being trusted, in both directions and including its own self-check, and it was CALIBRATED after a first draft flagged twenty-nine sites of which twenty-eight were not hazards -- it had demanded every token the filename carries, where any one token suffices, and it had scanned crates Layer E never runs. That miscalibration is recorded rather than quietly corrected, because a gate that fails the build on non-hazards is worse than no gate at all. A second lesson lands beside it: R311y453 was pushed and recorded as shipped with its hosted verdict unread, and the red sat there until R311y454s push happened to list the prior run next to it. The carried note said to read the verdict; it was still not read.

carry_forward_bullets: A SIGNATURE CHANGE NEEDS --all-targets, NOT A FEATURE-NARROW cargo check. R311y454 threaded one parameter through four functions and verified each with a narrow `cargo check`; the crate's OWN test targets call two of those functions and were never compiled. The cheap habit that prevents it: after any signature change, `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` on every touched crate before the round claims to be done.

A LANE REGISTERED IN A FAIL-FAST JOB IS NOT YET A LANE THAT RAN. Steps in the feature-gate NEG lanes job stop at the first failure, so ten lanes after C1bf were skipped. When a round adds a hosted lane, the verdict to read is that STEP's conclusion -- success / failure / SKIPPED -- and not merely that the lane appears in ci.yml.
STILL OPEN: R311y454's Layer C1bd has never actually executed on hosted CI. The next green run is its first, and that step's conclusion is what settles it.

NEXT: access-acl, and the design read is already done. Its fail-OPEN arm at interceptor/access_control.rs:102-106 is NOT a data-plane bypass -- both the forward path (linkstate_forward.rs:1547-1549) and the local-delivery path (:2656-2659) drop an unresolvable keyexpr anyway, so the comment claiming routing handles it is TRUE for those paths. But the naive fix is a REGRESSION: acl_action governs NetworkMessage::Response(_) wholesale and the keyexpr-None arm is what admits ResponseFinal, so flipping admit to deny would deny every query end-marker. zenoh does not rely on that path at all -- it puts ResponseFinal in an explicitly unfiltered arm beside Interest and OAM (net/routing/interceptor/access_control.rs:614-617 and :921-924). So the fix is TWO parts in order: make ResponseFinal an unfiltered kind in acl_action, THEN deny on an unresolvable keyexpr, matching the 22 of 22 zenoh arms that all `return false`. Also established: zenoh DOES govern UndeclareSubscriber (:468-484, with a deliberate ingress asymmetry keyed on ext_wire_expr) and DOES govern token-carrying Interest (:557-591), so those inventory residuals are real -- the `Interest(_)` unfiltered arm is a catch-all that sits AFTER the guarded ones.

Round 311y456.decision_summary: R311y456 -- R311y454 broke two hosted lanes and this fixes them, with the honest cause named: one error in two places, error E0061, six arguments where seven are needed, in the wz-ap-demo bin TEST target. carry_forward_bullets: R311y456's carry NAMED THE WRONG MECHANISM AND MUST NOT BE FOLLOWED. It said the naive fix is a regression because acl_action governs NetworkMessage::Response wholesale and the keyexpr-None arm is what admits ResponseFinal, so the fix had to be TWO parts in order. That is false: ResponseFinal is its own NetworkMessage variant, not a Response body, so it exits at `_ => None` and never reaches the keyexpr branch. The fix is ONE part. I took the claim from the comment at access_control.rs:73-75 instead of from the enum -- a comment I had written -- and the comment is now corrected and pinned by a test. The real trap was elsewhere and the residual did not name it: the EMPTY wireexpr of a synthesized timeout Err also lands on that branch. It is denied, and denying it is what zenoh does.

A RESIDUAL'S CONSEQUENCE CLAUSE IS A SEPARATE CLAIM FROM ITS DEFECT CLAUSE, AND CAN BE FALSE WHILE THE DEFECT IS REAL. Here the defect (wz admits where zenoh denies) was true and the consequence (a peer bypasses the ACL) was not, because five routing sites already dropped every governed kind carrying an unresolvable alias. The atom still deserved the fix -- the enforcer's own contract was wrong, and the next governed kind that routing does not pre-drop would have bypassed in silence -- but the round is smaller than the residual advertised. Grade the consequence too, not just the defect.

STILL OPEN ON access-acl, all vs zenoh 1.5.0 and each with its upstream site: UndeclareSubscriber is ungoverned in wz while zenoh governs it with a deliberate ingress asymmetry keyed on ext_wire_expr (access_control.rs:468-485); token-carrying Interest is ungoverned while zenoh governs it (:557-591), the unfiltered Interest(_) arm being a catch-all that sits AFTER the guarded ones; the three liveliness actions are absent; Subject still lacks cert_common_name and username (authorization.rs:40-45) though link_protocols and interfaces landed in R311y453; and enforcement needs a routing build while zenoh applies it to a client transport too.

Round 311y459.decision_summary: R311y459 -- the foreign witness R311y458 was missing: real zenoh-pico CLIs now drive a DeclareToken, its UndeclareToken and a token-carrying CURRENT Interest at a wz peer running --acl-deny, and all three are denied on the denied keyexpr while all three are admitted on the allowed one. y458 shipped five new governed arms with nothing but wz's own fixtures behind them; this closes that. The count is the discriminator and so the emitter was read first: pico carries the keyexpr on BOTH halves of a token's life, the undeclare putting it in the optional ext_wire_expr, so a denied token costs TWO drops -- and one drop rather than two would have meant the ingress asymmetry admitted the undeclare instead of judging it. That the second drop really is the undeclare was settled by moving the CLI hold from one second to three and watching the gap follow, not by assuming. The liveliness get sends exactly one message, so its drop is attributable to the Interest arm alone. Every allowed message runs FIRST and must leave the drop counter at zero, which rules out the ACL dropping the whole liveliness plane -- something a per-message positive control cannot distinguish. The A4 headline does not move and that is worth stating plainly: access-acl was already proven by the data-plane leg, so the gate is structurally unable to show that the CONTENT of the proof grew.
verification_bullets: RED PROVED AGAINST THE y458 CODE, WITH THE REBUILD VISIBLE. Removing the DeclareToken and UndeclareToken arms and making the Interest arm ungoverned -- i.e. restoring the pre-y458 state -- makes the leg FAIL at its first liveliness barrier: "wz peer never reached 'interceptor dropped (2 message(s))' for the DENIED secret/alive token within 15s". WHAT EACH pico CLI EMITS WAS READ BEFORE THE COUNTS WERE TRUSTED, not inferred from them. z_liveliness declares a token and, after -t seconds, undeclares it, and BOTH messages carry the keyexpr -- _z_liveliness_send_declare_token builds a DeclToken with an inline wireexpr, _z_liveliness_send_undeclare_token builds an UndeclToken via _z_make_undecl_token(id, &wireexpr), i.e. the OPTIONAL ext (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/net/liveliness.c:32-50). z_get_liveliness sends EXACTLY ONE message, an Interest with KEYEXPRS|TOKENS|RESTRICTED|CURRENT and no subscriber declaration (:314-362).

THE "SECOND DROP IS THE UNDECLARE" CLAIM WAS SETTLED BY MOVING IT, NOT BY ASSUMING IT. With -t 1 the two drops are one second apart; re-running with -t 3 moved the gap to three seconds. So the second drop tracks the undeclare's timing and is not a retry or a teardown artefact. The test then uses -t 1 so the pair lands inside its barrier.

THE FOREIGN ENCODER EXERCISES THE ext_wire_expr PATH, WHICH NO wz FIXTURE PROVED. pico's UndeclareToken carries its keyexpr as the optional extension, so the drop of the DENIED undeclare goes through R311y458's resolve path for undeclares -- the branch that reads declare_ext_keyexpr rather than an inline wireexpr. Had pico omitted the extension, the ingress asymmetry would have ADMITTED it and the count would have been 1, not 2; the count is what distinguishes the two.

Round 311y461.decision_summary: R311y461 -- the round set out to write the missing foreign witness for liveliness-historical-samples and instead falsified the classification that made it look writable. Two blockers were cleared by direct read first: pico z_sub_liveliness differs on the wire by exactly the CURRENT bit, and pico feeds an interest_id-tagged DeclareToken to BOTH the pending-query and the subscriber path, so a wz CURRENT reply does reach a foreign liveliness subscriber. What actually blocks the witness is the precondition, and it is architectural. In the single-session acceptor topology the sample counts are flaky AND the arms overlap (history ON 1 1 1 1 2 1, OFF 1 0 1 1 1 1 over six runs each), because wz holds its token in a PER-SESSION observer declared at Established, so the token can never pre-exist the session that asks for it, while the same token also arrives by a proactive push and by pico replaying its own cache. In the routing-peer topology, the one where a token genuinely does pre-exist a later subscriber session, wz delivers NOTHING -- 0 of 5 on the CURRENT dump and 0 of 5 on the FUTURE push, with routing-token-tables compiled in and the rebuild visible in the binary size. So this atom needs CODE, not a witness, and the roadmap FOUNDATIONAL witness-only label for it is wrong. No test shipped: a leg on either topology would have been flaky. The shippable finding underneath is a composition gap -- routing-token-tables was the ONE §5.21 routing atom missing from preset-ap-full, with no rationale anywhere, so the AP-full artifact carried the whole liveliness family with the entire router token plane compiled out. Added, 136 to 137, and all eight presets still build under Layer C4 exact command.
verification_bullets: WHAT pico ACTUALLY EMITS, READ BEFORE ANY COUNT WAS TRUSTED: z_sub_liveliness differs on the wire by EXACTLY the CURRENT bit -- history=false sends Interest KEYEXPRS|TOKENS|RESTRICTED|FUTURE, history=true sends the same plus CURRENT (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/net/liveliness.c:196-205, the mode ternary). The -h flag is what sets it (examples/unix/c11/z_sub_liveliness.c:110-131). wz gates its replay on that same bit (LocalTokenRegistry::respond_to_interest returns early on !interest.c(), local_token.rs:322-330), so the flag pair IS the discriminator the atom needs.

A BLOCKER NAMED BY AN EXISTING TEST WAS REFUTED BY DIRECT READ, NOT ASSUMED AWAY. wz_e2e_liveliness_token_to_zget_liveliness.rs:12-22 says a liveliness subscriber cannot isolate the interest-response and that pico routes an interest_id-tagged declare to the pending-QUERY path. The dispatch is NOT exclusive: _z_liveliness_process_token_declare feeds the pending-query path under #if Z_FEATURE_QUERY when interest_id.has_value AND THEN unconditionally calls _z_liveliness_process_remote_token_declare, the subscriber path (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/session/liveliness.c:218-235). So a tagged wz reply DOES reach foreign subscriber callbacks; that is not what blocks the witness.

TOPOLOGY 1 (single-session acceptor: wz-e2e-liveliness-token --listen --token, whose feature set is liveliness-token ONLY, so nothing but respond_to_interest could answer) IS FLAKY AND THE ARMS OVERLAP. Six runs per arm, fresh port each, sample counts: history ON = 1 1 1 1 2 1; history OFF = 1 0 1 1 1 1. No stable separation exists, so no assertion can be written. ROOT CAUSE, and it is architectural: wz's token lives in a PER-SESSION observer (observer.rs:255 local_tokens, registered at session/liveliness.rs:162) and is declared after Established (runner-side, pre-drive), so it CANNOT pre-exist the session that asks for it -- which is precisely the atom's precondition. Two further confounds ride along: wz also delivers the token by a proactive push, and pico replays from its OWN _remote_tokens cache before sending the Interest (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/net/liveliness.c:133-163, 196-200).

TOPOLOGY 2 (wz routing peer + pico z_liveliness token holder + pico z_sub_liveliness subscriber) IS THE ONE WHERE THE TOKEN GENUINELY PRE-EXISTS THE SUBSCRIBER'S SESSION, AND wz DELIVERS NOTHING. Five runs per arm: history ON = 0 0 0 0 0, history OFF = 0 0 0 0 0. Not a fixture artefact -- the fixture was bisected: the peer logs face 0 UP and face 1 UP, pico A printed its own "Press CTRL-C to undeclare liveliness token" banner (so the token EXISTS before B is spawned, the same gate the R311y354 pair uses), and B printed "Declaring liveliness subscriber on group1/**". The FUTURE-push arm (subscriber first, token second) is ALSO 0, and it shares the is_client_face gate, so the whole client-token plane is inert against a real pico here.

THE SECOND TOPOLOGY WAS RE-MEASURED WITH THE FEATURE COMPILED IN, WITH THE REBUILD VISIBLE. routing-peer does NOT pull routing-token-tables (crates/wz/Cargo.toml:473 vs :857), so the first five runs had the plane compiled OUT. Rebuilding with routing-peer,adminspace-write,routing-token-tables moved the binary 29697104 -> 31301112 bytes, proving the feature added code, and the counts stayed 0 0 0 0 0. RUST_LOG=trace on the peer yields 180 lines with no token or interest entry, so no further localisation was possible from logs.

Layer C4 is cargo build -p wz --no-default-features --features <preset> (run-ci.sh:4650-4669); all EIGHT presets build clean after the edit: mcu-minimal, mcu-extended, ap-client, ap-router, ap-full, zenoh-cpp, cortex-m4-default, cortex-m0-minimal. carry_forward_bullets: THE PIN IS NOW TWO FILES THAT MUST MOVE TOGETHER. mnemosyne.toml [tool] pin and scripts/install-mnemosyne-cli.sh MNEMOSYNE_REV state one fact twice, deliberately: the installer constant is the SSOT (ci.yml + release.yml install it, install-mnemosyne-mcp.sh parses it out of HEAD) and the toml key is where every binary -- including the MCP server, which the installer's schema gate never sees -- actually reads it. Backwards, the old binary dies in TOML parse before it can explain itself, and MNEMOSYNE_PIN_SKIP=1 does not rescue that: the env var is read only after the config has parsed.

THE MCP IS THE BLIND SPOT THAT MADE THIS DANGEROUS, AND IT STILL IS. verify-mnemosyne-pin.sh interrogates the installed CLI only; nothing in the installer or the hooks ever asks the MCP binary anything. The only oracle that observes a startup CONFIG-parse failure is a real initialize handshake, which is exactly what scripts/install-mnemosyne-mcp.sh does -- so after ANY mnemosyne.toml schema-shaped change, run that script, not just validate-workspace.

So the key and the rev moved in ONE commit, with both binaries installed and verified first, and upstream own escape hatch does not cover it because MNEMOSYNE_PIN_SKIP is read only after the config parses. SECOND, its section 2 is wrong about this tree: it says we were lucky and skipped the R840 red window, but Round 311y453 records that gate firing here on a drifted 27396a99 and blocking every commit. Its section 5 question is answered NO by VCS -- vendor/ holds four entries, all mode 160000, and zero wz-authored files -- and its section 6 verdict that nothing is wrong with our configuration is confirmed. A LOG LINE CAN BE A NEEDLE CONTRACT CONSTRAINED FROM BOTH SIDES, and appending to it is not the safe default it looks like. Here `(peer

, zid )` was pinned by two barriers with DIFFERENT shapes -- one needing the closing paren as the zid's right delimiter, one needing peer and zid adjacent -- so every position inside the parens stranded at least one. The two-step measurement here is the proof that reasoning about it is not enough: the "obviously safe" middle position still broke one of four.

Upstream's recipe would have worked, but its example root (40-char) and the machine's existing roots (7-char) disagreed, and following either blindly could have produced a directory nothing looks in. `pinned_root` joins the pin VERBATIM -- so the rule is "the directory name IS the pin string", which neither the notice nor the machine state states outright. DO NOT SWAP `--force` FOR `--root` HERE, EVER. Three sites resolve mnemosyne-cli through `command -v` and two of them HARD-FAIL on absence (R311y418 turned that SKIP into a FAIL deliberately). The safe shape is ADD, never MOVE: shared slot by `cargo install` (which also keeps ~/.cargo/.crates.toml truthful for the full-SHA read), per-rev root by copy.

A PREFIX TEST BUILT FROM A VARIABLE IS A HOLLOW GATE WHEN THAT VARIABLE CAN BE EMPTY. `case "$X" in "$Y"*)` with an empty `$Y` is `case "$X" in *)` -- it passes everything. THE FIRST DESIGN WAS MEASURED WRONG, AND THAT MEASUREMENT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE. The obvious witness -- seed N versions of one key, count N replies at a foreign querier -- was built, run, and produced ONE reply. The cause is not in wz: pico's z_get passes empty selector parameters (examples/unix/c11/z_get.c), so Z_CONSOLIDATION_MODE_AUTO resolves to LATEST rather than NONE (src/net/primitives.c:567-571 -- the branch turns on a _time parameter being present), and pico then drops every non-newest same-key reply INSIDE THE QUERIER before the application callback (src/session/query.c:133-150). A reply count for one key is therefore not observable through that CLI at all. z_querier does accept a ?params selector but returned no replies in this harness; that is recorded as an open question rather than pursued.

SO THE OBSERVABLE BECAME THE GATE SKIP, WHICH IS THE SAME CAPABILITY THROUGH A SINGLE REPLY. zenoh implements History::All as the ABSENCE of the newer-wins guard (plugins/zenoh-plugin-storage-manager/src/storages_mgt/service.rs:319 runs it only for History::Latest; zenoh-backend-traits/src/lib.rs:161-165 defines the two modes), and wz mirrors that in StorageState::latest_mode / process_put. A put replayed after a NEWER delete is the one mutation whose outcome differs: accepted under All, Outdated under Latest. One reply either way, so the difference survives pico's consolidation.

DAMAGE-VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, WHICH NEITHER LEG COULD DO ALONE. Forcing latest_mode TRUE (the gate always runs) reds the All leg and leaves the Latest twin green; forcing it FALSE (the gate never runs) reds the Latest twin and leaves the All leg green. The pair therefore brackets the mechanism from both sides -- a build that ignored history() in either direction is caught. A third damage emptied the WIRE reply set (matching_versions returns nothing): the All leg reds, and the Latest twin PASSES, which is the honest limit of an absence assertion and exactly why the round does not rest on the twin.

THAT THIRD DAMAGE ALSO EXPOSED A REAL RACE IN THE HARNESS, WHICH WAS ROOT-CAUSED RATHER THAN RETIMED. The select! treated the drive future completing as a failure, but pico is a one-shot querier, so the session ending is the ORDINARY consequence of it exiting -- and on a leg whose answer is empty pico exits almost immediately, so the drive branch could win with the terminator ALREADY in the capture. The verdict now comes from pico's own terminator in the final capture and neither select! branch decides it. 5/5 green after the fix.
