changes_bullets: crates/wz-capi-pico/src/keyexpr.rs: the keyexpr-DECLARATION family, 9 exports -- z_declare_keyexpr, z_undeclare_keyexpr, z_keyexpr_loan/_loan_mut/_move/_take/_drop, z_internal_keyexpr_null/_check. z_declare_keyexpr allocates a wire alias id, announces it, and returns an owned keyexpr that OWNS its literal (upstream's z_put.c keeps the declared value past the argv-backed string it built it from, so a borrow would dangle). z_keyexpr_drop frees the local value ONLY and does not retract, which is pico's own split -- drop takes no session, and a drop that silently retracted would lose a live alias when a value went out of scope.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/abi.rs: z_owned_keyexpr_t / z_moved_keyexpr_t added at pico's measured 48 B, and z_loaned_keyexpr_t widened to {start, len, handle, mapping}. Both the view arm and the declared arm keep the LITERAL at slots 0/1, so keyexpr_str stays a single branchless read and the declaration is additive; the alternative (a handle at slot 0 for the owned form) would make slot 0 ambiguous and force every reader to carry a tag. _mapping == 0 is the not-declared discriminant, sound because 0 is RESERVED on the wire. A `borrowed()` constructor replaces six struct literals so the two new slots cannot be left un-zeroed at an inbound site -- a forgotten zero would be read as a live alias id.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/faces.rs: KexprEntry, the THIRD SSOT next to subscriptions and queryables. declare_keyexpr allocates a session-global id (pico's `_z_get_resource_id` model; safe because a mapping table is DIRECTIONAL, so one id may go to every peer), fans send_declare_keyexpr over live faces, and records the entry so face_up REPLAYS it -- ordered BEFORE the sub/qbl replays, because a peer must never see a declaration or Push referencing an alias it has not registered. undeclare_keyexpr drops the entry and emits send_undeclare_kexpr per face. publish_aliased_all fans publish_aliased_auto, treating UnknownMapping as the per-face transient publish_all treats TransportUnavailable (a face whose declare failed mid-teardown has no table entry, and the healthy peers should still get the sample). Id allocation REFUSES above u16::MAX instead of wrapping: the wire's ExprId is u16 in both zenoh and pico, and a reused id would silently re-point a peer's live alias at a different keyexpr.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/pubsub.rs: z_put reads the declaration off the loaned keyexpr and publishes ALIASED when present, literal otherwise -- the same discriminant pico's _z_write reads off its _z_declared_keyexpr_t.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-capi-pico/src/platform.rs (NEW): pico's PLATFORM surface -- z_malloc / z_free, z_sleep_{us,ms,s}, z_clock_now, z_clock_elapsed_{us,ms,s}, plus z_bytes_from_buf and z_bytes_from_static_buf. No zenoh semantics at all, and the single biggest link blocker in the corpus: z_malloc/z_free alone blocked NINE of the 32 upstream examples and z_sleep_s seven, more than any protocol-level export. z_malloc/z_free forward to libc because pico defines them as exactly malloc/free and a C program may mix them with plain free() on one pointer, while std::alloc::dealloc needs a Layout a bare void* cannot supply. z_clock_now is clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) through libc so the constant stays right per platform (1 on Linux, 6 on macOS). z_clock_elapsed_* reproduces pico's SIGNED difference and its clamp-to-zero rather than a Duration subtraction, which would panic exactly where pico returns 0 -- the C side may hand back a clock it advanced past now.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/platform.rs: z_bytes_from_buf invokes the caller's deleter immediately after copying, on EVERY path. pico ADOPTS the buffer, so the transfer is unconditional once the call is made; dropping the deleter would leak the caller's buffer, which is the one thing a program handing over ownership cannot check for itself.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/pubsub.rs: z_declare_background_subscriber -- a subscription with no owned handle, for programs that subscribe once and loop forever. One export, three examples (z_ping, z_pong, z_sub_thr). Identical to z_declare_subscriber except that the SubId is discarded: with nothing to undeclare with, retaining it would only invite a removal path pico does not have.

crates/wz-capi-pico/src/keyexpr.rs: z_view_keyexpr_from_str_unchecked. Returns void -- pico's signature, and the point of the unchecked variant. wz still refuses a NULL or non-UTF-8 name and leaves the view EMPTY, which is narrower than pico (it would store the bytes and misbehave later): with no error channel, an empty keyexpr surfaces at the next publish instead of as undefined behaviour inside the library.

Round 311y478.decision_summary: R311y478 -- the platform surface lands and the drop-in gains a full ROUND-TRIP witness: real-body upstream linkers go 3 to 7 and exports 159 to 172 of 726. The target was picked by measurement rather than guess: every real-body example still short of exports was compiled, its undefined-reference set collected, and symbols ranked by how many examples each blocks, then candidate bundles scored by how many they fully CLOSE. That ranking is what identified pico's PLATFORM surface -- z_malloc and z_free block nine examples each and z_sleep_s seven, more than any protocol-level export -- and it also showed why the block alone is not enough: platform plus helpers closes exactly one example, and it took z_declare_background_subscriber, one further export, to take it to four. z_malloc and z_free forward to libc because pico defines them as exactly malloc and free and a C program may mix them with plain free on one pointer; z_clock_now is clock_gettime on the monotonic clock through libc so the constant stays correct per platform; and z_clock_elapsed reproduces pico's signed difference with its clamp to zero rather than a Duration subtraction, which would panic exactly where pico returns zero. The new leg is upstream's own z_ping.c completing five round trips against a real zenoh-pico z_pong, and it is the widest witness in the file because every printed line needs a publish, a foreign process receiving and republishing, wz's background subscriber delivering the echo, and the platform clock, all correct at once. Its load_loop busy-waits on an atomic with no timeout of its own, so the harness gained wait_for_exit and the leg waits with a budget -- a lane that hangs tells CI less than one that reds. Damage-verified: neutering the background subscriber reds only leg 4, and it reds through the budget rather than hanging. Round 311y482.decision_summary: R311y482 -- the harness was DISCARDING THE EVIDENCE, and that is the defect this entry records; the flake it hid is still open. R311y481 reported a Layer E failure in pico_c_examples_on_wz_capi_dropin and said the failing test's NAME was unrecoverable because the lane runs --quiet. That was false: run-ci writes a full log and names it in its own final line, and lines 192-208 of that file carry the test name, the file:line and the panic text. Opening it produced the real finding. Every witness in that file is a C program's printf captured to a file, where libc is block-buffered and only flushes at exit -- and each leg is driven by a self-terminating `-n N` invocation. So on the PASS path exit-flush works, and on the FAIL path the process has by definition not reached its exit count, nothing flushes, and the capture handed to the panic is ZERO BYTES. Measured: an `-n 2` subscriber that has seen one event holds 0 bytes while running and 0 after a kill, against 148 bytes with `stdbuf -oL`. Every failure mode therefore produced a byte-identical empty capture, and the leg-5 panic message asserted one specific mode -- "produces the ALIVE line and nothing else" -- that the harness could not distinguish from any other. R311y480 had already scanned for this and cleared the file as a "deliberate exit-flush design"; that exemption is retracted, since it describes only the path where the output is not needed. A derived scan (C-program binding AND captured stdout) found seven such sites and now finds zero. The leg-5 token holder was worse than unbuffered -- its stdout went to Stdio::null(), throwing away upstream's "Undeclaring liveliness token..." line, which is the one observable that separates "wz never reached the retraction" from "wz retracted and the frame did not arrive". Both sides now capture and the panic reports both, enumerating the three legs they distinguish instead of asserting one. The fix is verified by the failure it produces: with the capi staticlib damaged the leg now prints alive=true and the captured ALIVE line. The flake itself is measured (7/1 file-parallel, 0/10 serial, 0/6 under CPU load) and NOT root-caused; the one hypothesis I formed by reading -- close() latching stop while the drive future sits in a tokio::select! with no outbound drain -- was refuted by a 200 ms pre-latch probe that changed the rate not at all.
verification_bullets: RETRACTION 1 -- R311y481's verification said "WHICH test failed is unknown because the lane runs --quiet, which prints no test names". FALSE, and the file was there the whole time. `crates/target/run-ci-logs/run-ci-20260731-184619-2689945.log` lines 192-208 carry the FAILED line, the `failures:` block, the test name, the file:line and the panic text. I had grepped only the background-task capture, not the log run-ci names in its own final line. The claim was retracted by opening the file.

RETRACTION 2 -- R311y480's verification said a scan for pico CLIs spawned without stdbuf "flagged two files; both are deliberate exit-flush designs". That exemption was WRONG, and it is why this stood. Exit-flush is a property of the PASS path: a failing leg has not reached its `-n` exit count, so nothing flushes. MEASURED: an `-n 2` z_sub_liveliness that has seen ONE event holds 0 bytes on its capture file while running, and 0 bytes after a kill (the buffer is lost outright). With `stdbuf -oL` the same state shows 148 bytes including the ALIVE line. The two files named in that bullet are exactly the two fixed here.

THE ENUMERATION IS DERIVED, NOT SAMPLED. A scan over every `Command::new` in the corpus that binds a C program (`zenoh_pico_cli_binary` / `dropin_binary`, plus the helper params that are C by contract) AND captures stdout via `Stdio::from` found SEVEN sites; the same scan now reports ZERO. The 134 raw `Command::new` hits are NOT all affected: wz and zenohd are Rust processes writing through unbuffered stderr, which is why the class is C-stdout specifically.

THE FIX IS VERIFIED BY THE FAILURE IT PRODUCES, not by a green run. With the capi staticlib damaged (TokenState::drop no longer retracting) the leg fails and now prints "subscriber saw the ALIVE line: true" plus the captured ALIVE line -- the exact discrimination the old empty capture could not make. NOTE the second trap this exposed: `cargo test -p wz-integration-tests` does NOT rebuild `libwz_capi_pico.so` (wz-capi-pico is not a dependency of that crate), so the first damage read GREEN until `cargo build -p wz-capi-pico` ran.

THE UNDERLYING FLAKE IS MEASURED BUT NOT ROOT-CAUSED, AND IS REPORTED THAT WAY. Rate: file-PARALLEL 7 pass / 1 fail; serial single-test 10 pass / 0 fail; CPU-loaded serial 6 / 0. So it is parallel-specific, not load-specific. The failing run's evidence says the subscriber saw ALIVE and never saw the retraction.

Round 311y487.decision_summary: R311y487 -- the R311y486 close-frame carry measured on the wire, and RETRACTED by the measurement. That carry recorded that wz-capi-pico z_close emits no Close frame "where pico sends a session Close", and it named the second half as newly cheap to fix. Only the first half was ever measured; the second was inferred from _z_unicast_send_close existing in the vendored pico tree, without checking that z_close reaches it. It does not -- the only caller is the lease task (_Z_CLOSE_EXPIRED). A new Layer E10 counts Close-opening batches through the harness own counting relay for three closers against one wz-ap-demo acceptor: the demo on SIGTERM as a positive control, a real zenoh-pico z_put, and the C ABI z_close. Over 20 runs the control emitted one Close every time, wz-capi-pico emitted none every time, and real zenoh-pico emitted one in 3 of 20 and none in the other 17. So a bare TCP FIN at close is INSIDE pico own behaviour envelope, the capi silence is fidelity rather than a gap, and the follow-up the carry proposed is withdrawn instead of built. The round also did not ship the assertion it was written to carry: capi > 0 == pico > 0 was the obvious gate and at 3/20 it is a 15%-red lane, which five green runs had already hidden before twenty were taken. What ships is the calibration as a hard gate (a zero is unreadable until the control reaches one), a delivery precondition on both zero legs so silence cannot be an unopened session, and a single stable assertion that the capi emits none -- pinning current behaviour rather than blessing it. Why pico sometimes speaks is measured but unexplained and is labelled so in the lane, the file, and this entry.
verification_bullets: THE MEASUREMENT, 20 runs of the same three legs: wz-ap-demo on SIGTERM emitted 1 Close in 20/20 (the control); real zenoh-pico z_put emitted 1 Close in 3/20 and none in the other 17; wz-capi-pico z_close emitted none in 20/20. Distribution recorded exactly: 17 runs '1/0/0' and 3 runs '1/1/0'.

THE CARRY IS RETRACTED BY IT. R311y486 recorded that the capi sends a bare FIN 'where pico sends a session Close'. The first half is confirmed; the second is false. A bare FIN at z_close is INSIDE real pico's own envelope, so the capi's silence is fidelity, not a gap, and no fix is warranted.

HOW THE WRONG CLAIM WAS REACHED, because the shape recurs: _z_unicast_send_close EXISTS in the pico tree and was read as proof that z_close reaches it. It does not -- its only caller is the lease task (lease.c, _Z_CLOSE_EXPIRED). The existence of an emitter is not evidence that a path calls it.

THE LEG MEASURES PICO'S REAL CLOSE PATH, established before trusting it: the z_put example ends z_drop(z_move(s)), and z_session_drop (api.c:946) calls z_close before dropping the rc. So leg 2 is a z_close measurement and not a process-exit measurement.

THE EQUALITY GATE WAS WRITTEN AND THEN NOT SHIPPED. 'capi > 0 == pico > 0' was the intended assertion; at 3/20 it is a 15%-red lane. It was caught by running the fixture 20 times rather than the 5 that had already passed, and the file records the number so the next author does not re-add it.

THE INSTRUMENT IS CALIBRATED AND THE CALIBRATION IS A HARD GATE. Leg 1 must count at least one Close or the test aborts before publishing any zero -- without it a broken relay, a wrong mid and a genuinely silent client are the same output.
BOTH ZERO LEGS PROVE THEY MEASURED A LIVE SESSION. require_delivery blocks on the acceptor logging SUBSCRIBER FIRED for that leg's own put, so 'sends no Close' cannot be a session that never opened.

An earlier attempt added a SECOND client to the same relay and still read 0 -- spawn_counting_relay accepts ONE connection, so the damage never reached the instrument; recorded because it looked like a null result.

THE 3/20 IS UNEXPLAINED AND IS LABELLED AS SUCH. A sub-second process should not reach a lease expiry, which is the only Close emitter reachable in pico's tree, so the cause is an open question rather than a known one. The lane prints it every run.

Round 311y488.decision_summary: R311y488 -- AP-full now carries the ADVANCED PUB/SUB plane, and a real zenoh-pico witnesses it in both directions. The round started from a measurement of how full "full" is: preset-ap-full is 137 of wz s 246 feature keys and omits 100, among them all 10 ext-pubsub-* atoms. Making it literally full is not a coherent target (a union of every non-platform non-runtime key does not build; no_std and http-send are mutually exclusive through sce-rust-runtime), so the target became the one whole PLANE the kitchen sink dropped, which builds clean on top of the preset. Two blockers stood in the way and both were BUILD facts that had been restated as implementation facts. On the pico side, Z_FEATURE_ADVANCED_PUBLICATION and _SUBSCRIPTION default to 0, so every advanced example in the vendored tree compiled to its own #else stub main -- and "zenoh-pico has no advanced-pubsub plane whatsoever" had entered a test module doc and the corpus KIND_CLASS note as if it described zenoh-pico. On the wz side, wz-ap-demo deliberately mirrors the library preset, so with the family omitted the AP-full binary logged INERT for --advanced-publish and declared no cache. Both are fixed and both fixes are asserted rather than assumed: the pico build script reads back the GENERATED config.h, and every leg checks the demo s own BUILD FEATURES line before any wire wait. What ships is Layer E11, hosted in the same commit, with two legs through an AP-full peer hub -- wz s cache answering a real z_advanced_sub s history GET, and wz s AdvancedSubscriber recovering a real z_advanced_pub s cache. Three things the round found by measuring rather than reading are recorded as prominently as the result. The first draft of leg 1 PASSED while proving nothing, because the demo s burst is triggered by session-Established and so every sample postdated pico; the fixture asserting its own precondition is what caught it. A publisher-detection leg was written, observed working, and REMOVED, because its ordering is a race the fixture cannot own. And session-extqos is closed as pico-unobservable: a real pico InitSyn carries one extension and no QoS one, and pico has no QoS knob to turn on.
verification_bullets: THE ROUND'S FIRST MEASUREMENT, and the one that set its target: preset-ap-full is 137 of wz's 246 feature keys. Crossed against A4's UNPROVEN 16 it leaves exactly 3 (session-extqos / session-extshm / transport-shm), but crossed against the FULL key list it omits 100 -- including all 10 ext-pubsub-*, all 8 adminspace-*, the storage-backend family, transport-multilink and transport-qos. "Make it actually full" is NOT the same target: a union of every non-platform, non-runtime key does not build (sce-rust-runtime compile_error, no_std x http-send are mutually exclusive), so the coherent target was the whole advanced plane, which builds clean on top of the preset.

THE PICO SIDE WAS COMPILED OUT, not absent. The generated config.h of our own CLI build carried Z_FEATURE_ADVANCED_PUBLICATION 0 and Z_FEATURE_ADVANCED_SUBSCRIPTION 0, so every advanced example in the tree was its own #else STUB main. With the flags at 1 both binaries reach "Opening session..." instead of "ERROR: Zenoh pico was compiled without ...", and the generated header reads 1.

THE WZ SIDE WAS INERT. The AP-full demo's own BUILD FEATURES line carried no `advanced` before the change and carries `advanced group` after. Damage-confirmed: removing `advanced` from the demo preset reds both legs in ~0.15s at the build assertion, naming the feature list, rather than timing out on a wire marker.

LEG 1, MEASURED: 5 samples published and "ADVANCED BURST COMPLETE" read BEFORE the pico process is spawned; a real z_advanced_sub then reports all 5, byte-exact, from its startup history GET. LEG 2, MEASURED: pico's cache filled to sample 4 before the wz subscriber's session exists; wz recovers 0..4 and then live 5+. Both legs and E9 green; all pico/zenohd lanes re-run after the foreign-oracle rebuild (E, E2, E5, E6, E6b, E6e, E6f, E6g, E6h, E7, E8, E8t, E9, E10, E11, M, Z) plus C4, Layer 0, fmt, clippy.

THE ORDERING TRAP, and why it is in the file's doc. The first draft was a two-process --listen fixture and it PASSED while proving nothing: the demo's advanced burst is triggered by a session reaching Established, so in that topology every sample POSTDATES pico and a live delivery is indistinguishable from a cache recovery. Measured directly -- 0 ADVANCED PUT lines at T+3s with no peer, 7 the instant a pico client attaches. What caught it was the fixture asserting its precondition instead of arranging it by sleep.

WHICH CODE THE LEGS BIND TO, by damage; two of four damages refuted what was expected. KE_ADV_PREFIX @adv -> @advX reds BOTH legs (the wire discriminator). ANYKE_PARAM _anyke -> _anykeX reds leg 2 ONLY -- so pico's responder applies the same intersect guard zenoh does, and wz's own replier does NOT (leg 1 stayed green while wz answered a token it no longer recognised). PARAM_LIST_SEPARATOR ; -> & reds NOTHING here, because neither leg passes --history-max so its selector carries ONE parameter and a list separator never appears.

A PUBLISHER-DETECTION LEG WAS WRITTEN AND REMOVED. A real pico DID report New alive token ('<ke>/@adv/pub/<zid>/0/_') against the --listen topology, repeatedly. It is not shipped because the fixture cannot own the ordering: pico's z_liveliness_subscriber_options_default sets history=false (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/api/liveliness.c:73), so it only sees a token declared AFTER its subscriber is installed, while wz declares the token the instant the session establishes. The ANYKE_PARAM damage exposed it -- that leg went red while still receiving all 5 samples live, i.e. the damage moved TIMING, not the token.

Round 311y489.decision_summary: R311y489 -- preset-ap-full now carries the ADMINSPACE plane, a real zenoh-pico witnesses it COMPOSED in both directions (Layer E12, hosted), and the demo's BUILD FEATURES self-report is made drift-proof by generation. Here it was sharper, because it was HALF present -- routing-peer has hard-pulled adminspace-core since the preset existed, so an AP-full node already answered @/<zid>/peer with its node record while every leg that makes that record worth querying (per-entity introspection, metrics, plugins, both permission gates, hot-reload, router linkstate) was compiled out. A node that answers its own identity and nothing else is not an admin space. What no lane could previously ask is COMPOSITION: every one of the eight atoms already had a pico witness (y270 core+introspection, y237 plugins, y275 metrics, y276 read gate, y51 write gate), but each builds its own narrow feature set into the ONE shared wz-ap-demo path and they actively assert the others are OFF -- y270's test ends by requiring /metrics ABSENT, which is what makes its own cfg-gate argument work and what makes it structurally unable to be the metrics witness. Six proofs of six parts and none of the whole. Layer E12 runs the whole plane on the AP-full binary in four legs: one z_get reads node record + introspection + metrics + plugins at once; --no-admin-read suppresses every one of them from the SAME build; a real z_put reconfigures the node and reads its own write back through a second z_get; and the same topology without --config-write-permit has pico observe ON THE WIRE that its un-permitted write did not land. The round also found and corrected two of its own errors rather than shipping them: the BUILD FEATURES line under-reported four declared features including adminspace-read, and the first draft of the plugins claim was graded full when it witnesses only one of that atom's three surfaces -- an over-claim that would have moved the A4 count on nothing.

THE GENERAL LESSON, worth more than the fix: a `static` is process-global, and cargo's unit of test parallelism is the BINARY. Any test-support exclusion built on a `static` covers one seventeenth of this crate's contention. A BARE TCP-ACCEPT BARRIER PROVES SOMETHING ACCEPTS, NOT THAT YOURS DOES. `wait_for_tcp_accept` can pass against whatever won a port race while your child is already dead, pushing the failure downstream into an unrelated assertion. Prefer `wait_for_tcp_accept_alive`, which Errs the instant the child you spawned exits. All six barriers in pico_c_examples_on_wz_capi_dropin were converted; other files still using the blind variant are worth the same sweep.

Round 311y490.decision_summary: R311y490 -- both R311y489 carries closed, each by measuring the thing rather than mitigating around it. The Layer E flake: PortReservation's exclusion was a `static` mutex, which is PROCESS-global, while cargo runs a crate's test BINARIES concurrently -- 17 were MEASURED alive at once in Layer E's --ignored sweep. Layer E wall time is unchanged (53/54/66s against a 58/68s baseline), so the serialisation costs nothing measurable. Independently, all six of that suite's readiness barriers move from wait_for_tcp_accept to the liveness-aware wait_for_tcp_accept_alive: a bare TCP connect proves only that SOMETHING accepts, so a child that lost the port race and died left the barrier PASSING against whatever won, and the failure resurfaced downstream as a foreign process exiting -1 with no diagnosis -- which is the exact shape observed. verification_bullets: THE MEASUREMENT THAT IDENTIFIED THE COMPETITOR: sampling live `target/debug/deps/` processes during Layer E's own `cargo test -p wz-integration-tests -- --ignored` invocation gives a peak of 17. PortReservation's mutex is a `static`, hence one per process, so sixteen siblings were never serialised against each other at all. This is what turns the doc's 'external process' framing from a remote hazard into the lane's own design.

THE RACE REPRODUCED: 17 concurrent processes running bind(0) -> close -> bind(port) lose the port 1 time in 6800 with a MINIMAL window (runs of 0, 1, 1 across 3x6800). With the fix's mechanism (an flock over the same window) the same reproducer loses 0, 0, 0.

A PREDICTION OF MINE WAS REFUTED MID-ROUND AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED. I expected a wider window (a 2 ms sleep standing in for fork+exec) to RAISE the loss rate; measured, it fell to 0/2040. The dominant term is the FREQUENCY of reserve calls, not the width of the window -- a tight loop keeps the processes phase-locked on the kernel's ephemeral cursor in a way a real lane does not. So the reproducers bracket the real-world rate, they do not measure it; what is established is the mechanism and that the fix removes it.

THE COST IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: Layer E wall time with the cross-process lock is 53s, 54s and 66s, against a 58s / 68s pre-change baseline. Reservations are held only from pick() to just past the readiness barrier, so serialising them across processes is not observable at lane scale.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-plugin-abi (NEW): the host<->plugin C ABI. `no_std`, zero dependencies, all `repr(C)` — the two sides are separate compilation units that need not share a rustc version, so a Rust-ABI type crossing this boundary is UB waiting for a toolchain bump. ENTRY_SYMBOL returns a descriptor and runs NO initialisation, so a host can interrogate compatibility without letting the plugin execute anything. `PluginEntry::compatibility` is the plugin-abi-compat atom: abi_major equality, abi_minor <= host (asymmetric on purpose — a host may know fields a plugin never fills, but a plugin expecting a newer host may reach for one that is not there), and vtable size+align, the check that catches a stale rebuild at an UNCHANGED declared ABI. crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/storage_service.rs: StorageService::rebind re-declares a storage's capture subscriber and answering queryable on another session, keeping the shared StorageState. declare_with_backend and rebind now build the pair through one private declare_handles, so the two cannot drift in what they declare. crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/storage_manager_service.rs: the manager holds each storage's StorageConfig beside its service (HostedEntry) and gains rebind_all(session, zid), which rebinds every hosted storage onto an accepted client session. Round 311y496.decision_summary: R311y496 -- preset-ap-full is made literally full, the omission class that produced it is gated, and the fifth missing family turned out to be hiding a functional defect rather than only a manifest gap. MEASUREMENT FIRST: of 213 inventory atoms, 164 were members and 49 were not; building the preset plus all 36 plausible candidates was clean under warnings = "deny", so "every atom this preset can carry" is a measured set, not a judged one. All 36 join (membership 200/213), and the 13 that stay out do so through a reasoned exclusion table whose categories are re-validated against the live inventory on every run. THE HEADLINE FAMILY IS STORAGE, and it is the sharpest instance yet of why membership is not bookkeeping. The preset's own header comment has claimed "all storage" since it was written while carrying four of seventeen atoms: the whole storage MANAGER (storage-mgr-*, seven atoms) and every backend implementation (filesystem / memory-volume / volume-trait / capability) were compiled out, while `--storage-host` remained reachable. So an AP-full node could report a live storage in its admin plane that its storage plane could not serve one foreign read from -- and that is exactly what a real zenoh-pico measured: a z_get on a mount a z_put had just written received only the terminating Final. THE DEFECT UNDERNEATH was a lifetime conflation the run-mode's own doc had NAMED as a "zombie storage" bound and accepted: a storage was created by add_storage(&session, ..) on whichever transient one-shot client carried the storage-add, so its capture subscriber and answering queryable died with that client. R311y496 splits the two lifetimes explicitly -- a storage's DATA is its StorageState over the volume-created backend, its two declaration handles are a BINDING TO ONE SESSION -- via StorageService::rebind and RuntimeStorageManager::rebind_all, which run_storage_host calls on every accepted client. Data outliving the PROCESS stays the volume's job, which is what --storage-host-dir asks for. FIFTH ROUND OF ONE SHAPE IS A MISSING GATE, not five mistakes (y461 routing-token-tables, y488 ext-pubsub-*, y489 adminspace-*, y491 the router-hat tier, y496 storage), so the round builds Layer A5: membership is DERIVED from cargo metadata + the Mnemosyne inventory, every omission must be on the exclusion table, and every exclusion must satisfy its category's predicate against the inventory -- out-of-scope requires an OUT-OF-SCOPE reason, unbuilt requires UNBUILT -- so the table cannot become the silencing mechanism it replaces. A5 also mechanises the wz-ap-demo manifest's own "held back" rule, which was prose; that list is now EMPTY, and storage-backend-filesystem leaving it is what makes --storage-host-dir more than an accepted flag. Layer E13 witnesses the plane on ONE AP-full binary with four legs driven entirely by foreign one-shots, including a durability PAIR (restart on the same dir must return the value; the same script without the flag must not). TWO SELF-CAUGHT ERRORS, both by gates rather than by review: the first version of E13 was FLAKY (leg 2, 3 failures in 8) because a log barrier that is not unique to its event matches the previous occurrence -- read_captured re-reads from offset 0, so wait_for_substring means "has this EVER appeared" -- root-caused to a counted barrier, then measured 12/12; and Layer A4 REFUSED two of this file's first-draft claims (storage-mgr-config, storage-backend-volume-trait) as foreign-NON-observable, which is correct and the claims are withdrawn rather than the exclusions widened. MEMBERSHIP IS A BUILD CLAIM: adding 36 atoms moves neither A3 nor A4 by itself.

DAMAGE, after the fix: wrapping the manager.rebind_all call in `if false` and rebuilding turns ALL FOUR E13 legs red (0 passed / 4 failed), including leg 3's pre-assert, which is what binds this file's legs to this round's change rather than to the storage subsystem in general. Restored: 4 passed.

THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS FILE WAS FLAKY AND WAS ROOT-CAUSED, NOT RETRIED. Leg 2 failed 3 runs in 8. The cause is that read_captured re-reads the capture from offset 0 on every poll (it must -- parent and child share one open file description, so a parent seek would rewind the child's write position), so wait_for_substring answers "has this EVER appeared". The barrier "client session ended" therefore matched the PREVIOUS client's line, and the host was killed while the sample it was to persist was still in flight -- surfacing two steps away as "the filesystem volume did not restore its mirror". Fixed by counting terminators. Measured after: 12 consecutive full runs of all four legs, 12 pass / 0 fail.

carry_forward_bullets: R311y497 = storage-mgr-dynamic-volume-loading BUILT, which discharges R311y256's own conditional deprecation ("if plugin-dynamic-loading is ever built, this returns with it") that R311y492 fired and R311y496 made Layer A5 print as OPEN on every run. Three parts, because one alone is inert: a repr(C) ABI crate (wz-volume-abi), a dlopen host that presents a loaded .so as an ORDINARY Volume so every storage-mgr-* feature composes over it for free (dynamic_volume), and a WIRE widening so a foreign client can name a volume at all — storage-add is now <name>[@<volume_id>]:<keyexpr>. preset-ap-full membership 200 -> 201 of 213; api-compat-c is now the ONLY item A5 prints as OPEN.

A GATE THAT PRINTS AN OPEN ITEM EVERY RUN IS WHY THIS ROUND HAPPENED. R311y256 deprecated this atom on a condition, the condition fired at y492, and nothing would have noticed — the same shape that kept the atom mislabelled for months — except that y496 refused to let the exclusion be silent. The lesson to keep is the mechanism, not the atom: when a status word carries a CONDITION, the condition needs a gate, because the word will outlive it.

WHAT MADE THE WIRE CHANGE POSSIBLE WAS ASKING WHICH FIELD THE DELIMITER LANDS ON. R311y496 deferred volume selection because it "needs a keyexpr-safe delimiter or a json5 body", and read that way it is a hard problem — every plausible delimiter is a legal keyexpr byte. It dissolves once the split is applied to the leading NAME field instead of to the payload as a whole: a storage name is a manager-unique identifier, not a keyexpr, so the keyexpr's grammar is simply not involved. The json5 body was never needed for this.

THE READ-MIRROR BOUND IS THE HONEST LIMIT ON EVERY CLAIM HERE, and it is shared with storage-backend-filesystem rather than specific to this atom: the in-tree StorageBackend::get returns a BORROWED value, so any backend whose real store is external must keep an in-memory mirror, and inside one process a read is therefore answered by the mirror. A read cannot distinguish a working volume from a broken one — only a value the PREVIOUS process wrote can, and it reaches a fresh host solely through store_entries. That is why the witness discriminates on a host RESTART and why the example volume is durable at all. A seam whose get returned owned data would remove the bound for both backends; that is a kernel-seam question, not a follow-up to this round.

RESIDUAL, and it is why the A3 tag is PARTIAL rather than COMPLETE: the operator seam loads ONE volume per host, where zenoh's config declares N volume plugins each with its own config object. N needs a pairing syntax, not a second Vec — pairing an i-th --storage-volume-config to an i-th --storage-volume by argv order is an interface that misfires silently, which is exactly the hazard the singular flag avoids. Per-storage volume config beyond the single configure() string is likewise not client-drivable.

THE DEFERRED §5.23 parse_storage_add_payload FOLLOW-UP NARROWS BUT DOES NOT CLOSE: volume selection is now on the wire, so what remains of it is strip_prefix and the complete flag, which stay host-side choices and are still not foreign-drivable.

NEXT, if the goal is A5 reporting zero OPEN items: api-compat-c, and it is not a membership line either. It is the zenoh-c C ABI drop-in — a sibling surface to api-compat-pico (proven at R311y479) but a different upstream ABI, so it is a build of comparable size to that one, not a flag. Nothing in this round moved it.

A LOG LINE IS AN INTERFACE, AND WHERE YOU ADD TO IT DECIDES WHO BREAKS. Appending a field to the host's storage spawn line looked safe and a comment said so: "the barrier substring is unchanged". It was unchanged relative to the storage NAME and inserted before the "— storage_manager Started" tail, which two older integration tests pin THROUGH. Moving the field to the END of the line makes every existing barrier a prefix by construction, which is strictly better than editing the two consumers — that would have fixed this instance and left the next inserter the same trap. The general rule: extend a log line at the END, and enumerate the pinners before believing any claim about which substring survived.

A GREEN SUBSET IS NOT A GREEN GATE, and this round is the demonstration. Every lane it touched deliberately was green, an interim read of the sweep said "21 lanes passed, 0 ERROR", and FOUR failures were still ahead of that point — including a BUILD ERROR in a feature combination the round never thought about (adminspace-config-hotreload WITHOUT the volume feature, where the new args struct's fields were dead). The verdict is the full run's exit code and nothing earlier.

LANE PLACEMENT IS A DESIGN DECISION AND WAS TREATED AS ONE: the atom's proof is split C1bv (no foreign binary, cannot SKIP anywhere) / E14 (pico job), instead of bundled the way C1bp is. C1bp did 86s of real work and then SKIP-passed the one leg that made it a cross-impl proof because it was wired into a job that provisions no pico CLI (R311y495 found that two rounds late). Applying that lesson costs one extra lane and removes the whole failure mode.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-volume-abi: NEW. The host<->volume C ABI contract, no_std, zero deps, everything repr(C) — linked INDEPENDENTLY by the loader and by every volume cdylib. It is NOT merged into wz-plugin-abi despite the shape similarity: a plugin is started and stopped while a volume creates stores that are put to, deleted from and enumerated, so one crate would make every plugin author link a storage vtable they never fill AND would tie the two ABI version numbers together, so a storage-side field append would invalidate every existing plugin .so for no reason. Two decisions differ deliberately from the plugin ABI. (1) TWO layout fingerprints, not one: this ABI passes a struct BY POINTER (StoredEntry), so that struct's layout is part of the contract and a volume rebuilt against a stale header would agree on the vtable and disagree on the record it is handed — the failure the version numbers cannot see. VolumeEntry::compatibility checks vtable size/align AND entry size/align, with a distinct verdict for each. (2) Enumeration is a host CALLBACK (EntrySink), not a returned array: an array would have to be allocated by one side and freed by the other, which is the classic C-ABI ownership bug this shape simply does not have. The entry symbol is wz_volume_entry, deliberately distinct from wz_plugin_entry, because one shared object may legitimately be both and a shared name would let the wrong loader resolve the wrong vtable while passing its own gate.

crates/wz-volume-example: NEW, cdylib-only so nothing can link it directly and skip the boundary; depends on wz-volume-abi and nothing else, which is itself the demonstration that the ABI crate suffices to author a volume. It is DURABLE (one file per key, hex-encoded because a key legally contains /, with a distinct r stem for the mount-root slot because that slot is the ABSENCE of a key rather than the empty key) and that is load-bearing rather than gratuitous: the host keeps a read mirror over every backend, so a volatile volume's proof could not separate "the host called through the vtable" from "the host answered itself". It exports two out-of-band counters that are deliberately NOT in the vtable, so a test can establish the calls landed without asking the mechanism under test to vouch for itself. A refused configure FAILS CLOSED (clears any root it held): a volume still writing to a root the operator has since replaced, because the replacement was rejected, persists data somewhere nobody named any more.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/dynamic_volume.rs: NEW. DynamicVolume::load does the dlopen + dlsym + ABI gate + metadata copy, and configure is a SEPARATE call so a host can interrogate what a .so claims to be before letting it act. DynamicVolume implements the ordinary wz-session-core Volume trait, so RuntimeStorageManager::register_volume takes it unchanged and every storage-mgr-* feature above it composes over a loaded volume for free — a dynamic volume with its own registry would have made all of that conditional. DynamicStore implements StorageBackend with an in-memory read mirror rebuilt from the volume's store_entries at create time, exactly as FilesystemStorage does and for the same reason (StorageBackend::get hands back a BORROWED value). LIFETIME: one Arc<Library> is shared by the volume and every store it creates, so the mapping outlives its last user by CONSTRUCTION — unlike crate::plugin, which leaks its registry because a plugin's effects can outlive every handle the host holds. Both Send impls are justified against the ABI's written threading contract rather than asserted.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/dynamic_volume.rs, three things a self-review of the finished module changed rather than documented. (1) load_mirror now CLEARS before rebuilding: its name and doc said replace and the body merged. Today that is a no-op — the only caller runs on a fresh empty store — so it is a latent trap removed, not a live bug fixed, and no test can reach it; stated that way rather than claimed as a fix. (2) put and delete now treat anything that is not one of the DOCUMENTED success codes as a failure, where they had only checked the ERR sentinel: an out-of-contract volume returning an unrecognised code was read as a successful write, which is how a value that was never written comes to be believed persisted. (3) a key or encoding schema carrying an interior NUL is now LOGGED at error before being dropped. The comment claimed "the caller logs it" and no caller did, so a key would have been silently written to the mount-root slot — the prose was wrong, and the behaviour was the thing worth fixing.

crates/wz-session-core/src/adminspace.rs: the storage-add wire payload becomes <name>[@<volume_id>]:<keyexpr> and AdminConfigWrite::AddStorage.volume_id becomes Option<String>. The Option is the load-bearing part: before it the wire always encoded mem and the host overrode it unconditionally, so no client could select a volume AND no host could tell "the client wants mem" from "the client did not say". R311y496 deferred this and recorded why — "it needs a keyexpr-safe delimiter or a json5 body". The delimiter is keyexpr-safe by CONSTRUCTION rather than by luck: it is applied only to the leading NAME field, which is a manager-unique identifier and not a keyexpr, so the keyexpr's grammar freedom (which @ is part of — every adminspace key begins @/) is untouched. Split on the LAST @ so a name containing one stays addressable; an empty volume is Malformed rather than a storage on a volume called "". to_storage_config resolves None to the new DEFAULT_STORAGE_VOLUME_ID, so a legacy payload produces the identical config it always did.

crates/wz-ap-demo: --storage-volume <path.so> + --storage-volume-config <text> on the --storage-host run-mode, loaded and configured BEFORE the listener binds so a client cannot race startup. The volume is registered under the id the .so ITSELF declares, never an operator-chosen name, or two libraries could be registered as one volume and a storage naming it would land on whichever loaded last. The pair is ONE struct argument (args::DynamicVolumeArgs) rather than two adjacent Option<String> parameters, which is the shape a caller transposes — and a transposed pair here would dlopen the config text and hand the volume its own path as a directory. run_storage_host now applies its own volume choice ONLY when the client named none; a client that NAMES a volume gets that volume or a VolumeNotFound it can see, never a silent substitution. The spawn log gains "on volume '<id>'" AFTER the existing barrier substring, so a witness can assert which volume the storage landed on without moving any existing wait.

crates/wz/Cargo.toml + wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml + wz-ap-demo/Cargo.toml: storage-mgr-dynamic-volume-loading stops being a no-op = [] facade and forwards to the real cfg site; preset-ap-full and the demo both gain it. The runtime feature forwards only the wz-session-core kernel SEAM, not the runtime storage-backend driver — like storage-backend-filesystem, because a loaded volume IMPLEMENTS the seam and never touches the StorageService.

Round 311y497.decision_summary: R311y497 -- storage-mgr-dynamic-volume-loading is BUILT, which discharges R311y256's own conditional deprecation, and preset-ap-full goes 200 -> 201 of 213 with api-compat-c left as the sole OPEN item Layer A5 prints. Three parts, because any one alone is inert: a repr(C) host<->volume ABI crate (wz-volume-abi) that is deliberately NOT merged into wz-plugin-abi and that gates TWO layout fingerprints rather than one, since unlike the plugin ABI it passes a struct BY POINTER; a dlopen host (dynamic_volume) that presents a loaded shared object as an ORDINARY Volume, so register_volume takes it unchanged and every storage-mgr-* feature composes over it for free, with one Arc<Library> shared with each store so the mapping outlives its last user by construction rather than by the leak-and-argue the plugin host needs; and a WIRE widening, storage-add becoming name-at-volume-colon-keyexpr with AddStorage.volume_id an Option, without which no foreign client can reach any volume but the host's own. R311y496 deferred that widening as needing a keyexpr-safe delimiter or a json5 body, and it dissolves once the split is applied to the leading NAME field instead of the whole payload: a storage name is not a keyexpr, so the keyexpr grammar is never involved. THE HONEST BOUND, which the witness is designed around rather than despite: the host keeps an in-memory read mirror over every backend because StorageBackend::get hands back a BORROWED value, so within one process a read cannot separate the volume working from the host answering itself -- only a value the PREVIOUS process wrote can, reaching a fresh host solely through store_entries, which is why leg 2 is a host RESTART and why the example volume is durable at all. Three damages bind three different claims: reverting the wire honouring reds all four legs, skipping register_volume reds legs 1-2 while the negative legs stay green by construction, and skipping the mirror rebuild reds EXACTLY leg 2. A green subset is not a green gate. RUNCI_EXIT=0 on the final tree, 120 lanes.
verification_bullets: DAMAGE, three of them, each binding a DIFFERENT claim, and the differences are the evidence. (A) Restore the pre-R311y497 behaviour — the host overrides the volume unconditionally — and ALL FOUR E14 legs go red (0 passed / 4 failed): legs 1 and 2 lose their "(volume 'wzvol_example')" barrier, and legs 3 and 4 lose their refusals because the override makes every mount succeed. That is what binds the whole file to the wire change rather than to storage-add in general. (B) Skip register_volume only, and legs 1 and 2 red while 3 and 4 stay GREEN — correct by construction, since those two assert the volume is NOT available; the host log shows the exact refusal ("no registered volume 'wzvol_example' to back the storage"). (C) Skip the mirror rebuild (load_mirror) only, and EXACTLY leg 2 reds while 1, 3 and 4 pass — which is what pins the durability claim to store_entries and to nothing else. Every damage was rebuilt before being run, and the tree was grepped clean of all three afterwards.

DIAGNOSE-FIRST on the wire half: before the parse change, the payload apfull@wzvol_example:demo/store/** could not name a volume at all — the leading field was the whole name and the host overwrote volume_id unconditionally — so leg 1's barrier could not have existed. Layer C1bv pass (1s) through run-ci: wz-volume-abi 8 passed, wz-runtime-tokio dynamic_volume:: 10 passed, wz-session-core adminspace::tests::config_hotreload:: 10 passed, clippy -D warnings clean on the host combo and on both new crates.

THREE UNIT LEGS FAILED FIRST AND WERE ROOT-CAUSED, NOT RETRIED. The example volume's configured root is PROCESS-GLOBAL — it must be, since dlopen of an already-mapped library returns the SAME mapping and the ABI specifies configure as once-per-volume — and cargo runs a crate's unit tests as THREADS in one process, so legs configuring it stomped each other. The measurement that showed it: the volume's own out-of-band put counter read 5 where the leg had made 2 puts. Fixed at the right layer, in two parts: a test-local lock making each leg's window exclusive (documented as a test-binary need, not a defect in the volume — a host configures once), and the example volume made to FAIL CLOSED on a refused configure, so the unconfigured precondition can be FORCED instead of hoped for. changes_bullets: crates/wz-capi-core: NEW, and it is a MOVE rather than a design. The ABI-neutral session model -- the face registry, the declaration SSOT replayed onto each face as it comes up, and the one-OS-thread-per-session drive loop -- left wz-capi-pico so a second C ABI could sit on it. Duplicating it was the alternative, and it would have copied precisely the two things a second copy gets wrong invisibly: the race-free close (the stop latch is set BEFORE the notify, because a Notify permit is single-use and notify_waiters would drop the wakeup) and the drop-outside-the-lock discipline (releasing the last closure reference runs a C drop(context), which is allowed to re-enter the session). 1435 lines, verified by the SIBLING's own gates rather than by review.

crates/wz-capi-pico (the DEPENDENCY INVERSION that made the move possible): the registry stored the C closure TYPES and called make_*_callback to turn them into wz callbacks, which pointed the dependency upward -- an ABI-neutral model reaching into one specific ABI's closure shape. It is inverted through three FACTORY aliases (SubscriberSink / LivelinessSink / QueryableSink): the shim hands in something that MINTS a callback and the registry never learns what it closes over. A factory rather than a ready-made callback because a callback is needed once per FACE -- every declaration is replayed onto each new face. The C drop semantics are unchanged: the factory owns the Arc<CClosure>, so the last one released still runs drop(context).

crates/wz-capi-core, the three edges the compiler and clippy found while moving: session_state(*const z_loaned_session_t) had drifted into the neutral range and went back to the shim (it takes an ABI type); open_blocking returned pico's Z_ERR_GENERIC and became a neutral OpenError, because BOTH C ABIs typedef z_result_t to int8_t and then disagree about the values, so shared code returning one ABI's constant is silently wrong in the other; and a blanket pub(crate)->pub widening made two Result<_, ()> functions public API, which became FanoutError (named to avoid wz-runtime-tokio's own PublishError, already imported in that file).

crates/wz-capi-c: NEW -- the zenoh-c ABI. It ships NO header, unlike its sibling's R1: zenoh-c's header is cbindgen OUTPUT so it IS the ABI, and a wz-authored header would make the drop-in claim untestable by construction. Twelve symbols, and the SCOPE IS AN UPSTREAM PROGRAM rather than a symbol list -- z_put.c links and runs. That distinction paid immediately: a hand-picked list drafted before measuring named four symbols zenoh-c never calls and missed three it does, including zc_init_log_from_env_or, which nothing about implementing a put would suggest.

crates/wz-capi-c/src/abi.rs: the opaque owned/loaned/moved families with const-asserted footprints, plus a `wz_capi_c_layout` export so a gate can READ the numbers out of the shipped cdylib instead of re-transcribing them into a test. THE FOOTPRINTS ARE FEATURE-DEPENDENT and that was measured, not read: upstream's published standalone archive is built WITH Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API and a build without it is a different ABI (z_owned_bytes_t 40 vs 32, z_put_options_t 56 vs 48), so "wz is a zenoh-c drop-in" is incomplete until the build is named. Expressed as the `zenoh-c-no-unstable-api` cargo feature, default = the published archive.

crates/wz-capi-c/src/config.rs: z_config_default / zc_config_from_file / zc_config_insert_json5 / z_config_loan_mut. The json5 VALUE parser handles the three shapes upstream's parse_args.h actually passes (a quoted scalar, a list of quoted scalars, a bare literal) and REFUSES everything else with Z_EPARSE. The refusal is the load-bearing half: a config engine that silently accepted a nested object would let a program believe it configured something wz never reads, which is what makes a drop-in claim hollow.

crates/wz-capi-c/src/{session,put,keyexpr,bytes,log,result,ffi}.rs: z_open (mapping the core's neutral OpenError onto zenoh-c's Z_ENETWORK), the session ownership family with zenoh-c's gravestone contract, z_put (payload taken FIRST and unconditionally, because zenoh-c specifies it consumed on return whether or not the publish succeeds), the view keyexpr (wz COPIES where upstream aliases -- a superset, recorded because it is observable in one direction), z_bytes_from_static_str (likewise copying), zc_init_log_from_env_or, and zenoh-c's own Z_E* codes, which are NOT zenoh-pico's and have a test saying so.

crates/wz/: api-compat-c stops being a no-op `= []` facade and pulls the cdylib, and `wz::capi_c` re-exports it under the atom's cfg toggle (the A3 active-site). It is NOT added to preset-ap-full, and that is the round's most instructive correction: the first draft added it beside its pico twin and a full sweep reddened eight lanes with `rust-lld: error: duplicate symbol: z_session_loan_mut`. zenoh-pico and zenoh-c SHARE the `z_*` namespace -- both export z_open, z_put, z_session_loan, z_session_loan_mut with different type layouts -- so a binary offers one ABI or the other. The facade now carries a `compile_error!` for the pair, because the linker's message names a symbol and no reason, and the operator who enabled both should not have to read rust-lld output to learn a fact this crate already knows.

scripts/lib/apfull_membership.py: a NEW exclusion category `alt-abi` with its own predicate (an `api-compat-*` other than the one the preset names), mirroring alt-platform / alt-runtime. api-compat-c sits in it. The category is not bookkeeping: it records a constraint the facade's compile_error already enforces, and its predicate refuses to cover an atom that is not an alternative ABI.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/zenoh_c_examples_on_wz_capi_dropin.rs: NEW, two legs. It ASSERTS the pin by reading the installed zenoh_configure.h rather than trusting what it just did, and prints the Z_FEATURE_* set, because a hosted log that does not record WHICH ABI was validated has not recorded the claim.

AN EXEMPTION IS A CLAIM, and this one was half right. wz_router_hat_connect_reconcile.rs states "Cross-impl is NOT needed for this atom: the reconcile introduces no new wire format". That is correct about the wire FORMAT and silent about the DATA PATH — what a reconcile creates is a face the router tier must then CHOOSE as a next-hop, which is a routing decision, not a codec one. A FOREIGN CLI CAN HIDE THE PROPERTY, and it did here. Leg 3 was written to assert that a real pico prints DELETE where z_put prints PUT; it was run and refuted -- the vendored pico z_sub prints only key and payload, and a scan of EVERY subscriber example in vendor/zenoh-pico (unix, zephyr, windows, freertos, threadx) found none that renders the kind. So an empty-payload PUT and a DEL are the same two lines at that observer. The leg was rewritten to claim only what the foreign decoder establishes (the Del BODY parses and is delivered) and the limit was CALIBRATED rather than asserted: a damage making z_delete emit an empty PUT PASSES leg 3, and a damage addressing a different key FAILS it. THE LESSON OF THE ROUND, and it was the user's catch, not mine. z_sample_attachment's PRESENT arm needs pico's z_pub_attachment, which publishes through a DECLARED PUBLISHER, and that delivered NOTHING in the client-to-listening-peer topology the first three legs use. I read that as a wz ingress defect, then calibrated foreign-to-foreign, saw pico z_pub fail into a real pico z_sub too, and concluded 'a pico topology property, not a wz defect'. THAT INFERENCE IS INVALID and the user said so: (1) matching the reference proves wz is not DIVERGENT, never that the behaviour is CORRECT -- wz's north star is a SUPERSET, so if full zenoh delivers where pico does not, wz still owes delivery; (2) I never measured that the two failures share a CAUSE, and a twin can be stable for an unshared reason; (3) the calibration arm itself was suspect, because a pico peer is not a router and z_declare_publisher may simply require one -- in which case the experiment says my topology was invalid, not that the path is unsupported. What I had actually established was only that the topology was not a valid vehicle. Putting a REAL zenohd in the middle decided it: pico z_pub -> zenohd -> pico z_sub delivers 3 of 3, pico z_pub -> wz --router-hat -> pico z_sub delivers 3 of 3, and pico z_pub_attachment -> zenohd -> upstream z_sub.c ON WZ renders the attachment (its serializer field names source/index appear in upstream's own printf). Measuring the live plugin BEFORE writing code showed wz's value rendering was UTF-8-driven where zenoh's is ENCODING-driven, and it diverged on five of eight measured rows: JSON payloads were stringified rather than embedded, any non-text encoding rendered its bytes as a bare string rather than base64, a schema-bearing encoding took the wrong arm, timestamp was always null, and an absent encoding hint rendered the empty string where zenoh renders zenoh/bytes. Round 311y502.decision_summary: R311y502 -- a correction to R311y501, filed as a new entry rather than an edit because the y501 entry is frozen. y501's leg 2 differential was UNSOUND, and its own verification bullet (2 passed against a live zenohd) was true but did not mean what it claimed. The leg re-published each class key on a poll cadence until both SSE streams showed it -- but every PUT mints a NEW sample with a NEW timestamp, so when one subscriber's Declare propagated a round later than the other's, each side's first event for that key was a DIFFERENT publish and the differential compared two unrelated renderings. It passed repeatedly, including through a damage probe, and surfaced only on re-running the exact Layer Z leg command: identical key, value and encoding, timestamps one publish apart, same zid. The retry was not the safeguard, it was the defect -- a retry is not a synchronisation primitive, and when the compared thing has IDENTITY, retrying to absorb propagation delay silently changes WHICH thing is compared. The fix separates the two concerns: a WARMUP key is re-published until BOTH streams show it, which is a real barrier on both subscriptions being live, and only then is each class published EXACTLY ONCE. Sample identity is now structural rather than hoped for, and an assertion that each side saw exactly one event for the key converts any recurrence into a loud failure instead of a wrong comparison. 20 consecutive runs pass, but that is corroboration and not the argument -- the old code also passed consecutive runs. The transferable lesson is the second one: a green re-run count is not a non-flakiness argument, and a brand-new e2e should be re-run before it is believed.

Round 311y505.decision_summary: R311y505 -- a real cross-impl DEFECT found and fixed on the wire, and the residual it was hiding behind was recorded backwards. The user picked the SHM establishment ext as the highest-value long-term item on the grounds that it is the only remaining unproven atom that could be silently WRONG rather than merely absent. Establishing that took two things nothing had built: `wz-ap-demo --shm` (the library's `SessionOffer::with_shm` / `connect_and_open_session_with_shm` have existed since R3b and NO spawnable binary ever set them, so wz's one occupant of zenoh's establishment ext space had never faced a foreign decoder) and a `shared-memory` zenohd oracle (`ZENOHD_SHM=1 scripts/build-zenohd.sh`, the third feature-variant oracle after unixpipe and vsock -- zenoh's `default` set omits `shared-memory` and zenohd's default is `zenoh/default`, so the STOCK oracle has no `init::ext::Shm` compiled in at all and can neither send the challenge nor react to an offer; reading its `shm negotiated = false` as an answer would have been the foreign-CLI-hides-the-property trap). With both in place the measurement inverted the inventory on both counts. REFUTED: the recorded WIRE-INCOMPATIBLE residual claimed zenoh's ZExtZBuf reader dispatches on the ID alone and would desync an SHM-enabled peer's ext chain on wz's UNIT@0x2. It does not -- `zenoh-codec/src/common/extension.rs:224` is `if iext::eid(self.header) != ID { return Err(DidntRead) }`, an identity check with the ENCODING BITS INCLUDED, and an SHM-enabled zenohd receiving wz's offer completes the handshake with zero errors. wz's UNIT@0x2 (header 0x02) and zenoh's `Shm` ZBuf@0x2 (header 0x42) are DIFFERENT extensions in one 4-bit id space, exactly as zenoh relies on itself (`QoS = zextunit!(0x1)` beside `QoSLink = zextz64!(0x1)`, `transport/init.rs:147-148`). FOUND: the defect was on the WZ side and in the opposite direction. `unit_ext::chain_has_ext_id` matched capability offers on the 4-bit id field alone, so when the SHM zenohd DIALLED wz, wz read zenoh's `Shm` ZBuf as its own UNIT offer and negotiated `shm negotiated = true` -- wz would then have put SHM DESCRIPTORS on a link whose peer had issued a challenge wz cannot answer and expects payload bytes, i.e. silent corruption at the application layer rather than a clean refusal. Fixed at the MECHANISM rather than the SHM site: `chain_has_ext_eid` matches on `iext::eid`. The same loose match sat under `peer_offered_qos`, where stock zenohd enables QoS by DEFAULT -- but there the acceptance of BOTH forms is FAITHFUL (zenoh's QoS is a genuine dual ext), so that site now names its two forms explicitly instead of inheriting them from a loose match, which is a narrower and checkable claim. Only ONE arm could catch this: zenoh sends `Shm` on the InitSyn unconditionally but on the InitAck only in reply to an offer it understood (`ext/shm.rs:455`), so a wz that merely dials never receives one -- hence `--shm` on the ACCEPT role, and hence leg 2. A4 unproven 5 -> 4 (session-extshm proven).

After the eid fix, the identical command logs `false` with the session still Established and zenohd reporting zero errors or warnings.

The REFUTATION is measured, not argued: an SHM-enabled zenohd receiving wz's UNIT@0x2 completed the handshake with 0 errors / 0 warnings in its log, and the source says why (`zenoh-codec/src/common/extension.rs:224` checks `iext::eid`, not the id field).

carry_forward_bullets: R311y506 = session-extqos BUILT and PROVEN cross-impl; A4 unproven 4 -> 3 (proven 124 -> 125, partial 39). The atom was `reserved` with 0 cfg sites and a documented residual ("the z64 QoSLink priority-range wire semantics + the config->offer path; until it lands is_qos never flips true so the wire stays DEFAULT-inert"). Both halves are now built: the z64 `init::ext::QoSLink` codec with zenoh's exact bit layout, the DIRECTIONAL containment (acceptor demands a subset and adopts theirs; initiator demands a superset and keeps its own; a declared reliability must match; every violation ABORTS the handshake as it does upstream), and the config surface `WzConfig::with_qos_link -> FaceSources::qos_link -> the _with_offer entrypoints on BOTH roles`, driven by wz-ap-demo `--qos-band` / `--qos-rel`.

THE ORACLE'S OWN SHAPE DECIDED THE FIXTURE, and only measurement found it. The natural test -- zenohd LISTENING with `?prio=`, wz dialling a non-subset band -- was run FIRST and came up GREEN, i.e. zenohd accepted a band it should have refused. The reason is upstream's: `accept.rs:672` seeds the acceptor's QoS state from `link.get_src().to_endpoint()` and zenoh-link-tcp hard-codes an accepted link's src-locator metadata to `""` (`unicast.rs:103`), so a listening zenohd has no band over TCP at all. Three of the four legs therefore have zenohd DIAL wz. Generalise the lesson, not the fixture: a foreign peer's CONFIG surface is not evidence that the config reaches the wire on the path you are using.

A SILENT DOWNGRADE WAS FOUND BY A GATE, NOT BY READING. Layer C4 red on `preset-ap-full` pointed at a `schedule_redial` call site the threading had missed -- a peer flap would have re-established on the presence-only UNIT ext, keeping none of the containment the operator configured, with nothing reporting it. Threaded. The MULTILINK open path has the same hazard and is NOT fixed: its entrypoints take `(qos: bool, band)` and stage no `SessionOffer`, so `--qos-band` there would be dropped the same way. That combination now EXITS with a named error instead of running, which is the honest state until a per-link band lands on the aggregation path (zenoh's `PriorityRange` genuinely IS per link, so this is a design step, not a thread-through).

Both integers are plain VLE (`zint.rs` `uint_impl!(u32)` delegates to the u64 VLE), so wz's existing `crate::vle` is the right codec. Its oracle needs `ZENOHD_SHM=1 scripts/build-zenohd.sh` (a SOURCE build -- zenoh's `default` omits `shared-memory`) and is NOT provisioned on hosted CI, so that lane SKIPs there. `routing-interceptor-hotreload` + `routing-interest-pending-gc` remain the ratify candidates y503 measured as probably FOREIGN_NON_OBSERVABLE -- still a decision round, and shrinking the denominator is still not a proof.

Both halves are built. zenoh's QoS establishment ext is DUAL at id 0x1 -- `QoS = zextunit!(0x1)` (presence) XOR `QoSLink = zextz64!(0x1)` (a packed priority range + reliability class), never both -- and wz had only the unit form plus a decoder that read either as "peer does QoS". Now: `State::to_u64` / `try_from_u64` mirrored byte-for-byte (3 tag bits, priority bytes at shifts 3 and 11, reliability bit at 19, INCLUDING upstream's reserved-tag reject arm); the emit choice in ONE function so the unit-XOR-z64 exclusivity is structural rather than a rule two call sites remember; and both DIRECTIONAL merges -- the acceptor demands the initiator's band be a SUBSET of its own and adopts theirs, the initiator demands the acceptor's be a SUPERSET and keeps its own, a declared reliability must MATCH, and every violation ABORTS the handshake as it does upstream (`DriverLoopOutcome::QosLinkRejected` -> `OpenError::QosLinkRejected`, the InitAckCapsRejected teardown pattern). The config path is real, not a test hook: `WzConfig::with_qos_link` -> `FaceSources::qos_link` -> the `_with_offer` open entrypoints on BOTH roles, driven by wz-ap-demo `--qos-band START-END` / `--qos-rel 0|1` in zenoh's own endpoint-metadata spelling. One deliberate strictness deviation: an out-of-range priority BYTE is REFUSED, not clamped -- `Priority::from_wire`'s permissive clamp is correct on the 3-bit Frame field where it is unreachable, but the QoSLink field is a full byte and zenoh errors on it, so reusing the clamp would negotiate a band the peer never offered. THE ORACLE'S OWN SHAPE DECIDED THE FIXTURE, and only measurement found it: the obvious test (zenohd LISTENING on a `?prio=` endpoint, wz dialling a deliberately non-subset band) was run FIRST and the session came UP, because `accept.rs:672` seeds the acceptor state from `link.get_src().to_endpoint()` and zenoh-link-tcp hard-codes an accepted link's src-locator metadata to the empty string (`unicast.rs:103`) -- a listening zenohd has no band at all over TCP. Three of the four legs therefore have zenohd DIAL wz; the limit is upstream's and is recorded in the test's module doc rather than worked around. Layer C4 then caught a SILENT DOWNGRADE the reading had missed: a `schedule_redial` call site without the band would have re-established a flapped peer on the presence-only UNIT ext, keeping none of the configured containment and reporting nothing. The MULTILINK open path has the same hazard and is NOT fixed (its entrypoints take `(qos, band)` and stage no SessionOffer), so that combination now EXITS with a named error -- a per-link band on the aggregation path is a design step, since zenoh's PriorityRange genuinely IS per link. `session-extqos` also LEAVES the `pubsub-priority` alias, where it rode as what the prior comment itself called a pre-y307 asymmetry: harmless while the key was a no-op, but as a real forward it pulls transport-qos -> alloc into `preset-cortex-m4-default`, a no-alloc MCU preset. This round built the real thing. zenoh's SHM establishment is a four-message CHALLENGE-RESPONSE over real POSIX segments (`establishment/ext/shm.rs`): InitSyn carries the initiator's AUTH SEGMENT id; the acceptor MAPS that segment, reads the random challenge stored inside, and returns it on InitAck beside its own segment id; the initiator validates the echo against its own challenge, maps the acceptor's segment, and answers with ITS challenge on OpenSyn; the acceptor validates that second echo and confirms with the literal 1 on OpenAck. Each side therefore PROVES map-ability to the other, which is the point -- a token exchange would pass between two hosts that share nothing at all. The segment is a genuine POSIX object at `/dev/shm/{id}.zenoh` (the NAME is wire format: a foreign peer opens exactly that string through `shm_open`) holding the u64 array `[protocols.len(), !challenge, SHM_VERSION, POSIX_PROTOCOL_ID]`, with the challenge stored BITWISE-INVERTED exactly as upstream stores it -- load-bearing interop, not obfuscation, and the damage below is what shows it. wz mirrors zenoh's failure ASYMMETRY rather than smoothing it: a version mismatch, an unmappable segment and a wrong echo all degrade to "no shared memory" with the session intact, while only a MALFORMED InitSyn body aborts the handshake (zenoh's single `bail!`, against its tolerant `recv_init_ack` -- a malformed challenge aimed at an acceptor is an attack surface, a malformed answer is just a peer that will not get SHM). The change is OPT-IN and cannot half-mix: the dispatch is EMPTY until an authenticator is installed and an empty one emits nothing, so a deploy that installs none keeps the pre-R311y507 UNIT wire byte-identical; the challenge REPLACES the UNIT ext at the stage seam (they share id 0x2 and must never ride one chain); and the "did the peer offer SHM" predicate follows whichever mechanism is running, which is the correction that made the exchange work at all -- keeping the UNIT predicate for both cleared the capability the moment a peer spoke the real protocol, and it presented as "the challenge-response never completes". Two wz<->wz half-mix legs pin that a ONE-SIDED authenticator leaves BOTH sides without SHM, which is the arm that matters for safety: a session ending with one side believing SHM was on would put descriptors on a wire the peer reads as payload bytes. THE EVIDENCE SPLITS HONESTLY, and the round records how: deleting the challenge CHECK reds the forged-echo unit test but leaves the wz<->wz e2e GREEN, because two cooperating wz peers genuinely map each other. So the e2e proves the exchange COMPLETES and only the forged-echo test proves the check is ENFORCED -- an end-to-end test between two instances of the same implementation can rarely show enforcement, which needs a peer that lies. What keeps transport-shm PARTIAL is now the DATA path rather than establishment: the receiver still copies once off the shared page into wz's owned Sample, there is no segment pool / watchdog / generation, and zenoh's payload descriptor (`ShmBufInfo` with its metadata-segment `MetadataDescriptor{id,index}`) is collapsed to a single segment_id, so PAYLOAD interop is explicitly NOT claimed. THIS ROUND REVERSED ITS OWN FIRST ANSWER, and the reversal is the point. It began by proposing both remaining A4 atoms as FOREIGN_NON_OBSERVABLE denominator exclusions, argued entirely from reading zenoh and wz source. The exclusion was reverted and the atom was BUILT instead. A CLAIM'S FIXTURE PRECONDITION IS PART OF THE CLAIM. The pico leg proved nothing until its host started with a non-empty ACL: admit_inbound short-circuits an EMPTY chain before the cache, so there was nothing cached for the write to invalidate, and the damage left the leg green. Generalise: when an optimisation is only consulted on a path guarded by a fast-path check, a proof must first establish that the guard was passed. The guard is invisible in the assertion.

A face with NO resolved subject caches NOTHING -- the subject can resolve later, and a cached admit would outlive its reason. verification_bullets: THE FIRST CROSS-IMPL CLAIM THIS ROUND WROTE WAS VACUOUS, AND A DAMAGE PROBE IS WHAT SAID SO. With the leg as it stood, deleting the version bump left the pico E2E GREEN. THE PROOF INSTRUMENT WORTH REUSING: zenoh-pico's CURRENT interest carries NO timeout (net/liveliness.c:348 discards the parameter), so a pico z_get_liveliness process EXITING is the DeclareFinal arriving and nothing else. Process exit as the wire observable needs no log parsing and cannot be faked. The upstream is silenced with SIGSTOP, which keeps the TCP link open while answering nothing -- a real way to make a live face go silent without mocking.

THE CONFOUND THAT SHAPED THE FIXTURE: a SIGSTOPped peer also stops KeepAlives, so the 10s session lease expires and the face-down drain finalizes the client too. That is a THIRD correct retirement path, not a bug, but it means the GC claim needs the deadline (2500ms) well inside the lease and BOTH an upper and a lower elapsed bound. The damage probe is what measured it: disabling the sweep moved the arm from 3.24s to 8.89s rather than hanging.

Its residual was MEASURED, not assumed, by enumerating every caller of qos_link_metadata(): the negotiated PriorityRange/reliability is stored, copied onto Face, and consumed ONLY by the demo's render_qos_link log line. There is no egress clamp and no SN-conduit restriction keyed on it -- establishment fidelity is proven, ENFORCEMENT is not implemented. That is the next session-extqos build if anyone wants it.

THE LESSON THAT GENERALISES, and it is a lane-hygiene one: **a lane named for a feature must compile that feature ALONE at least once.** Every C1y arm passed `--features routing-peer` WITHOUT `--no-default-features`, so it measured "default + routing-peer" and reported the feature's name. Grep for `--features <X>` without `--no-default-features` in any lane that claims to gate X.

COROLLARY on gate unions: a cfg union assembled from APP-SURFACE features silently excludes non-app originators. wz has at least three originator classes now -- the app session, the linkstate forwarder, and the router forwarder -- and only the first is named in those unions. Round 311y513.decision_summary: R311y513 -- a bare routing-peer build could not send a single Declare, and the tree had been saying so for months into a lane nobody ran. ROOT CAUSE: the send seam's Declare arm (send_network_message_qos) and dispatch_declare were gated on the declare-* APP-SURFACE origination union, while routing-peer pulls codec-declare -- its own manifest calls the Declare wire surface part of a routing peer's contract -- and none of that union. So every Declare a linkstate forwarder ORIGINATED fell to the no-emit catch arm and returned FeatureDisabled; fan_out_qos counts only successful sends, so the flood reported 0 faces reached. On such a build declare_subscription and declare_queryable flood nothing, forward_subscription and forward_queryable re-flood nothing, the tree-change re-advertise reaches no late joiner, and respond_to_interest emits neither the dump NOR the terminating DeclareFinal -- so a foreign client soliciting that peer is wedged, which is the exact hang R311y512 had just built a GC for. FIX: mirror the OAM arm's ALREADY-PRESENT routing marker onto the Declare arm and, for the same reason, onto the Interest arm -- codec-linkstate plus codec-push is what a routing peer IS inside wz-session-core, and the OAM arm two arms below carries that condition and documents it. The alternative -- adding the declare-* keys to routing-peer's closure -- looks free because each is literally a codec-declare alias, and was REJECTED on measurement: they also switch on the observer.rs session-declaration surface a mesh node never uses. The Interest half is not theoretical: the R311y512 broker propagates a client's CURRENT interest through that seam, so on a bare build every propagated copy returned FeatureDisabled and the broker degraded silently into the inline answer it exists to replace. WHY IT HID: every Layer C1y arm passes --features routing-peer WITHOUT --no-default-features, so what those pins measured was default plus routing-peer, and the default set carries the missing origination features. A lane named for a feature must compile that feature ALONE at least once, or it is measuring the default set and reporting the feature's name; C1y now carries a bare pin (200) that reds at 150 on the exact pre-fix tree. Also fixed while in there: propagate_current_interest recorded its pending entry BEFORE sending, and send_one_to_face discards the fan-out count, so a copy that never left still created an entry and would withhold the client's final for a whole GC window -- it now sends through the counted fan_out seam and records only what left. 50 failing tests -> 0; no inventory or atom-status change (this is a defect fix, not a capability).

BLAST RADIUS on a bare routing-peer build (not merely a test artifact): declare_subscription / declare_queryable flood nothing; forward_subscription / forward_queryable re-flood nothing; the tree-change re-advertise reaches no late joiner; respond_to_interest emits neither the dump NOR the terminating DeclareFinal, so a foreign client soliciting such a peer is wedged -- the exact hang R311y512 built a GC for.

WHY THE OTHER FIX WAS REJECTED: adding the declare-* features to routing-peer's closure looks free (each is literally = ["codec-declare"] in wz-session-core) but is not -- they ALSO switch on the observer.rs session-declaration surface a mesh node never uses. Measured before choosing, not assumed.
