THE LESSON THAT GENERALISES: a negotiated value is not enforced until something in the DATA path reads it. The R311y512 residual was found by enumerating every caller of the reader (three sites, all establishment or logging) and that enumeration is the technique -- for any negotiated capability, list the readers of its post-handshake state and ask which one is on the send path. session-extshm, session-extcompression and session-extauth have not been put through it.

THE FAITHFULNESS TRAP THIS ROUND AVOIDED, and it is worth reusing: transcribing upstream literally would have been WRONG here. zenoh's link.reconfigure writes None through, and copying that would have cleared wz's deploy band, because upstream has ONE band field where wz has two. The rule that resolved it: reproduce the upstream OBSERVABLE, and where the two trees' field topology differs, work out which upstream states are reachable before copying the assignment.

NEW, NAMED RESIDUAL on session-extqos (the atom stays PARTIAL): the FIELD-IDENTITY gap. wz's deploy band -- accept_loop::multilink_priority_range's FaceId-parity split, installed by set_link_priority_range at bring-up -- is never ADVERTISED, so a wz multilink deploy negotiates a band it did not tell the peer about. zenoh's prio= endpoint metadata is simultaneously the offer and the selection input. SECOND NAMED RESIDUAL: wz's LinkReliabilityPref::Any means NO PREFERENCE, where zenoh's undeclared case falls back to the link's INTRINSIC class (config.reliability.unwrap_or(Reliability::from(link.is_reliable()))). carry_forward_bullets: R311y516 = the RX SHM enforcement hole, found by RUNNING the R311y514 enumeration rather than reasoning about it. The technique -- list every reader of a negotiated capability's state and ask which one is on the data path -- produced three verdicts: extcompression already enforced both directions, extauth enforced by handshake reject with no upstream data-path consumer either, and extshm enforced on TX but NOT on RX. wz honoured the 0x2 body marker alone, so a peer that never negotiated SHM could name a /dev/shm segment and have this node map it and deliver its contents. zenoh gates the whole un-swap on the negotiated capability (rx.rs:50-51). carry_forward_bullets: R311y522 closed the accept-side liveliness flush that R311y521 registered as open debt, and the round is mostly a lesson about WHERE a fix has to land.

A FLUSH THAT STAGES IS NOT A FLUSH THAT DELIVERS. wz's liveliness registry does not call the application callback: it stages the sample on a deferred-fire queue (R311lg) so the callback can re-enter the session without self-deadlocking, and the DRIVE LOOP drains it. Any teardown path that fires samples after the drive loop has returned owes an explicit drain_deferred_fires -- otherwise the fan-out reports "1 slot fired" and the application hears nothing. That is exactly the shape of an emitter that exists on a path that does not run.

THE FIRST ATTEMPT WAS REVERTED RATHER THAN SHIPPED, and that was the right call: it flushed without draining, so the registry was cleaned and the C application still never learned. It is now pinned by its own damage probe, so the same half-fix cannot return quietly.

A LIVELINESS FACE-DEATH TEST MUST LEAK THE TOKEN. A merely BOUND token emits an UndeclToken from its RAII drop, and since R311y519's teardown drain that tail frame is actually DELIVERED -- so the gate passes through the ordinary undeclare path and proves nothing. Measured, not feared: with the token bound the test passed even with the fix removed. R311y519 made a previously-safe test idiom unsafe, which is worth remembering for any other teardown gate written before it.

INSTRUMENT TO A CONTRADICTION, THEN READ. Four probes narrowed this to "the registry fired into a slot whose sink is somehow not the C shim", which is impossible as stated -- and that impossibility is what made the deferred-fire seam findable by reading the declare path. Instrumentation bounded the search; it did not answer it.

Round 311y522.decision_summary: R311y522 -- the accept-side half of the liveliness link-loss flush, and a fix that had to be reverted once before it worked. A C program that declared z_liveliness_declare_subscriber was never told when the peer holding a token VANISHED: face_down dropped the FaceEntry and with it the whole per-face observer, in silence, and no UndeclToken can rescue that because the link that would carry one is what died. The obvious fix -- flush the per-face observer before dropping the entry -- was built, measured, and REVERTED at first, because it did not work and the reason was not guessable: wz's liveliness registry does not call the application callback at all. It stages each matched sample on a DEFERRED-FIRE queue (R311lg, session/mod.rs:3743-3752) so the callback may re-enter the session safely, and the DRIVE LOOP drains it -- but face_down runs after the drive loop has returned, so nothing ever did. Flushing therefore measured as one slot FIRED and reached the application as silence. The shipped fix flushes AND drains, and the flush-without-drain state is now pinned by its own damage probe. The gate also had to LEAK its token: a bound one emits an UndeclToken that R311y519's teardown drain now delivers, so a bound-token version passes through the ordinary undeclare path -- measured, with the fix removed.
verification_bullets: THE ROOT CAUSE WAS FOUND BY READING, after instrumentation had narrowed it to a contradiction. The measurement trail said: face_down runs, the observer holds slots=1 tokens=1, the flush drains 1 and fan_to_matching_slots reports 1 slot FIRED, on_sample calls the boxed closure with no gating -- and yet the C shim was entered only for the Put. The resolution is at session/mod.rs:3743-3752: declare_liveliness_subscriber registers a DEFERRED-FIRE staging sink (R311lg), so on_sample stages the sample on the session fire queue and the callback runs later, when the drive loop drains it. face_down runs AFTER the drive loop has returned, so nothing ever drained it. Adding drain_deferred_fires is the fix.

THREE DAMAGE PROBES, and the third is the one that matters most. (1) No flush at all -- the pre-R311y522 state -- FAILS (15.04 s, the Delete wait expiring). (2) Flush WITHOUT the drain FAILS: this pins the exact trap that caused the first attempt to be reverted, so it can never be reintroduced silently. (3) Fix removed AND the token merely BOUND rather than leaked PASSES -- which is the proof that std::mem::forget is load-bearing and that a bound-token version of this gate would be vacuous. That third probe is why the earlier attempt looked green at first.

Layer C1's actual invocation (cargo test --workspace with four --exclude flags) was run directly and prints "test a_dying_face_undeclares_its_remote_liveliness_tokens_to_the_c_app ... ok", so the gate is executed rather than merely registered. Round 311y528.decision_summary: R311y528 -- the two DEFECTS R311y527 pushed are closed and the pico C ABI advanced from 11 to 14 of 32 upstream programs LINKING WITH A REAL BODY, with the round opened by re-running the link measurement rather than by reading the carried residual list. The first defect was a genuine cross-thread race: two threads reach one C matching closure (the drive thread through the per-face callback and face_down purge, the C thread through an already-matching registration) and the aggregate mutex was released before the sink, so a peer dropping during registration produced two concurrent call(context) on one C context. The unsafe impl Sync comment ARGUED this could not happen and was wrong. The fix holds the mutex across the call, which is only sound because face_down stopped folding under the registry lock -- that was the registry-to-aggregate half of an ABBA pair. The second defect: z_undeclare_publisher left its matching entries registered, so the C closure kept firing for a released publisher; the retraction now lives on PublisherState Drop, because z_publisher_drop reaches the same state by another export. Three new planes shipped -- identity (z_info), batching plus _z_zint_len (z_pub_thr), and the whole querier family including the three matching siblings R311y527 omitted -- each DRIVEN against a foreign process, not merely linked. The strongest witness is LEG 9: zenohd prints its own zid and upstream z_info.c on wz prints that exact string under Routers IDs. And the round caught its own registered-but-never-ran leg by reading Layer E log instead of its verdict.
verification_bullets: MEASURED FIRST, as R311y527 carry_forward demands: all 32 upstream examples compiled against pico headers and linked to wz cdylib. Baseline 11 LINK+BODY / 4 stub / 17 FAIL. After this round 14 LINK+BODY / 4 stub / 14 FAIL -- z_info, z_pub_thr and z_get_lat opened.

Remaining and ranked: the handler/channel bundle (about 30 symbols) unlocks SIX; advanced pub/sub (15) unlocks two; z_scout (8) one; z_bytes needs just THREE (z_view_slice_loan, z_bytes_get_slice_iterator, z_bytes_slice_iterator_next).

z_bytes IS THREE SYMBOLS AWAY BUT NEEDS A REPRESENTATION CHANGE, which is why it was not taken. z_view_slice_t must LOAN into z_loaned_slice_t, and wz's loaned slice is a HANDLE while a view is a borrow pair. The string plane already solved exactly this (StringState caches a self_view and z_loaned_string_t is a borrow pair), so the fix is to give the slice plane the same shape. It touches z_bytes_to_slice, z_slice_clone and the existing slice ownership macro, so it is its own step rather than a tail on this one.

A REAL PICO DECLARED PUBLISHER DELIVERS NOTHING TO A WZ C-ABI SESSION. Measured three ways: pico z_put into a wz C-ABI z_sub WORKS, pico z_pub into the same subscriber delivers nothing, and pico z_pub_attachment into a wz-NATIVE subscriber works in the existing Layer E test. So it is specific to the C-ABI registry, not to the wire, and it silently blocks a large class of programs -- every pico app built on z_declare_publisher. The likely mechanism to check first is pico's write filter: a declared publisher suppresses writes while it believes there are no matching targets, so what to look for is whether the C-ABI session answers pico's INTEREST the way the wz-native session does.

z_bytes_writer_append CONCATENATES where pico keeps a slice LIST. The octets are identical on every path; only z_bytes_get_slice_iterator can tell the difference, and it does not exist yet. If the slice-view work above lands, this becomes observable and should be revisited together with it.

z_timestamp_new stamps from the session's MONOTONIC clock, not an HLC. Well-formed and monotonic within one session, NOT comparable across nodes. A program that attaches and reads back its own stamp cannot tell; one that orders events across peers by it can.

Round 311y529.decision_summary: R311y529 -- the pico serializer, encoding and attachment planes land and the C ABI goes from 14 to 18 of 32 upstream programs LINKING WITH A REAL BODY, taking the bundle the previous round RANKED SECOND on purpose: the channel bundle unlocks one more program but requires reproducing two INTERNAL pico struct layouts a C program stack-allocates, while every type in this one is opaque behind exported accessors. Two things this round found are worth more than the symbol count. First, its own encoding-table oracle test was VACUOUS and a damage probe proved it: from_str and to_string read the same table, so a round trip is invariant under any permutation of it and swapping two entries stayed green -- the fix reads the id straight out of upstream, feeding wz table entry i to the REAL pico and asserting pico assigns it i. Second, and sharper: z_pub_attachment.c LINKED and RAN while a real pico subscriber reported encoding zenoh/bytes with no attachment and no timestamp, because z_publisher_put took its options as an opaque pointer and dropped all three -- a link is not a pass, and only the foreign decoder showed it. Separately, a PRE-EXISTING gap was measured and is carried rather than closed: a real pico DECLARED publisher delivers nothing to a wz C-ABI session, while pico z_put does and a wz-native session receives the same publisher fine.
verification_bullets: MEASURED FIRST and re-measured after: 14 LINK+BODY at the start of the round, 18 at the end. z_get_attachment, z_pub_attachment, z_sub_attachment and z_queryable_attachment all opened. The last of those cost exactly ONE symbol once the rest of the bundle was in.

THE ORACLE TEST FOR THE ENCODING TABLE WAS VACUOUS AND A DAMAGE PROBE PROVED IT. The first cut compared z_encoding_from_str followed by z_encoding_to_string across wz and libzenohpico.so. Swapping two entries in wz's table left it GREEN, and the reason is structural rather than a gap in the probe list: both directions read the SAME table, so the round trip is invariant under ANY permutation. No rendering comparison can observe the id, and the id is the byte that goes on the wire.

THE FIX READS THE ID OUT OF UPSTREAM DIRECTLY. pico's z_owned_encoding_t holds a concrete _z_encoding_t at offset 0 whose id field sits at offset 32, measured. For each entry i of WZ's table the string is handed to PICO's z_encoding_from_str and pico's own id is read back and compared with i. Nothing circular is left. Re-running the same swap now reds with wz's encoding table has text/json5 at index 10, but the REAL pico assigns it id 11.

THE WIRE SHAPE IS COMPARED BYTE FOR BYTE, not read back through wz's own reader. serialized_bytes_agree_with_the_real_pico_library drives both libraries through ze_serializer_empty / serialize / finish and diffs the octets, across VLE rungs for sequence lengths, multi-byte UTF-8 for strings, and the fixed-width little-endian arithmetic form. It also CROSS-DESERIALIZES both ways. Damage probe: writing a sequence length as a fixed 8-byte word instead of a VLE reds exactly that test and nothing else.

TWO ABI TRAPS WERE HIT AND FIXED IN THE HARNESS, both worth recording because they are silent. z_bytes_get_reader and ze_deserializer_from_bytes return 32-byte structs BY VALUE, which SysV classifies as MEMORY, so the hidden return pointer is the FIRST argument -- declaring it second segfaulted. And a bare byte array is 1-byte aligned while every pico owned value holds pointers, so Rust's alignment check aborted the run until the slots became align(8).

A LINK IS NOT A PASS, and this round has the sharpest instance of it yet. z_pub_attachment.c linked and RAN, printing its own Putting Data lines, while a REAL pico z_sub_attachment reported encoding zenoh/bytes with no attachment and no timestamp -- because z_publisher_put took its options as an opaque pointer and dropped all three. Only driving it against the foreign decoder showed that.

LEG 13 IS WHAT PINS THE ENCODING ID, and the oracle test structurally cannot. A real pico subscriber decodes wz's bytes and prints with encoding: zenoh/string;utf8, with timestamp, and the attachment kv pairs deserialized through pico's OWN ze_deserializer -- so a wrong table id would render as a different name and a wrong framing would fail to parse.

A SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING GAP WAS FOUND AND IS NOT CLOSED HERE. A real pico DECLARED PUBLISHER delivers NOTHING to a wz C-ABI session: pico z_put reaches it, pico z_pub does not, and the same pico z_pub_attachment reaches a wz-NATIVE subscriber in the existing Layer E test. So the gap is on the C-ABI side, it is pre-existing rather than introduced here, and it blocks the whole reverse direction of this bundle.

Ranked by programs unlocked per mechanism: the handler/channel bundle unlocks SIX (z_sub_channel, z_get_channel, z_queryable_channel, z_pull, z_querier, z_get_liveliness) behind ONE mechanism; advanced pub/sub unlocks two; z_bytes needs three symbols.

THE CHANNEL BUNDLE IS NOW SCOPED, and the scariest part of the R311y528 note is answered. Every handler is a static inline in handlers.h and the C program stack-allocates the 184-byte fifo and 136-byte ring INSIDE it -- but NOTHING in the header dereferences their fields, so wz may own those bytes as its own representation. The real constraint is different and sharper: the macro memcpys the whole handler struct into a refcounted heap cell, so wz representation must be RELOCATABLE BY MEMCPY and therefore cannot hold a self-pointer.

THE CHANNEL BUNDLE ALSO NEEDS OWNED ELEMENTS, which is the part a symbol count hides: z_owned_sample_t is 224 bytes and z_owned_reply_t is 248, both C-stack-allocated, and wz today has only their loaned accessors. Plus _z_rc_ four, the fifo five and ring six collection entries, z_liveliness_get and z_view_keyexpr_from_substr.

z_bytes IS STILL THREE SYMBOLS AWAY AND STILL NEEDS THE REPRESENTATION CHANGE R311y529 named: z_view_slice_t must LOAN into z_loaned_slice_t while wz loaned slice is a HANDLE and a view is a borrow pair. The string plane already solved exactly this shape.

THE AGGREGATE REPLY KEYEXPR IS UNPINNED BY ANY TEST. Answering an AGGREGATE interest with the subscription keyexpr instead of the interest keyexpr passes every leg here. Upstream associates by _z_keyexpr_equals so the current choice is the parity-correct one, but a test that can tell them apart does not exist yet and would need a peer whose interest is aggregate AND whose match would fail under equals.

THE SCOUT PLANE HAS ONE NAMED DIVERGENCE: pico calls the user closure the instant a Hello decodes, wz drives cycles and emits each cycle new peers when the cycle returns, so a callback can lag the wire by up to one cycle. The delivered SET over the budget is the same. A program timing Hello latency from inside the callback would measure the cycle.

Round 311y530.decision_summary: R311y530 -- the pico C ABI goes 22 to 23 of 32 upstream programs linking, the SCOUTING plane lands with the real zenoh-pico library as its oracle, and a carried defect is retracted and then UN-retracted by measurement. The round opened on R311y529 carry that a real pico DECLARED publisher delivers nothing to a wz C-ABI session. A first reproduction was flawed (a bare sleep where the test harness uses an accept barrier), and the new leg written to replace it passed repeatedly against an unfixed tree -- so the carry was written off and the fix discarded as unproven machinery. Layer E then red on that same leg, and repeats settled it: 12 of 12 red without the interest response, 8 of 8 green with it. The mechanism is that pico arms a write filter per z_declare_publisher and drops every put locally until its subscriber Interest is answered, and wz answered it for FACES but never from a session own subscriptions; a publisher whose filter fails to arm writes freely, which is why single green runs pointed the wrong way. The wildcard keyexpr is load-bearing and demonstrated: an exact key passes either way. Separately the scouting plane ships and is witnessed the strongest way this tree has: upstream z_scout.c compiled twice against the same headers, linked once to wz and once to libzenohpico.so, prints the SAME line for the same zenohd.
verification_bullets: MEASURED FIRST and re-measured after: 22 of 32 upstream examples linked at the start of the round, 23 at the end. z_scout opened, and it is LINK+BODY rather than merely linked -- upstream z_scout.c on wz discovers a REAL zenohd and prints its zid, Router, and the ephemeral locator the kernel chose.

THE STRONGEST WITNESS IS A DIFF AGAINST THE REAL LIBRARY. z_scout.c is compiled TWICE from the same source against the same pico headers, once linked to wz cdylib and once to libzenohpico.so, and the two print the SAME Hello line for the same zenohd. Byte order, whatami map index and locator projection are all pinned by one equality.

DAMAGE PROBES ON THE SCOUT PLANE, three, each reding only what it should: reversing the zid bytes reds the oracle diff; removing the per-peer dedupe reds the count assertion (the real pico prints ONE line, wz without dedupe reports the peer once per cycle); swapping two slots of the whatami map reds the map unit test and leaves the other three unit tests green.

THE ROUND OPENED AS A DEFECT HUNT, RETRACTED THE DEFECT, AND THEN RETRACTED THE RETRACTION. R311y529 carried a real pico DECLARED publisher delivers NOTHING to a wz C-ABI session. A first reproduction used a bare sleep instead of an accept barrier, and re-measuring seemed to clear it: the new leg passed repeatedly against an unfixed tree, so the carry was written off as a measurement artefact and the fix was DISCARDED as unproven machinery.

LAYER E CAUGHT THAT, and the numbers settle it. The same leg red in the full sweep, then red 8 of 8 standalone, then 4 of 4 more on a rebuild without the scout feature -- 12 of 12 against the unfixed tree. With the interest response restored it is 8 of 8 green. The lesson is not that green lies at random: a publisher whose write filter fails to ARM writes freely, so it worked and the mechanism is present are different claims, and only a repeat RATE can tell them apart.

THE WILDCARD IS THE DISCRIMINATOR AND IT IS DEMONSTRATED, NOT ASSERTED. zzz slash-doublestar against the same publisher delivers ZERO, so the assertion can fail; an EXACT keyexpr passes with or without the interest response, so a leg written that way would have proved nothing. The zenohd oracle settles which behaviour is correct -- a real router between the same two pico binaries DOES deliver to a wildcard subscriber.

WHAT THE LEG DOES NOT PIN IS STATED IN IT: answering with the subscription keyexpr instead of the interest keyexpr still passes 4 of 4, so the measured discriminator is the interest-stamped reply EXISTING. The aggregate-keyexpr choice is upstream parity, not something this test discriminates.

A C program that escapes a query and never drops it holds that request's terminator open until its own process exits; there is no sweep. pico has the same shape (its rc holds the Final), so this is parity rather than a defect, but wz has no cap where it caps other per-request state.

Round 311y531.decision_summary: R311y531 -- the pico C ABI reaches 32 of 32 upstream programs linking, and the round that got there closed two divergences a link count could never have shown. The channel bundle landed first: _z_rc_* refcounting, the fifo and ring mt collections, and owned sample / reply / query families over a deep-copying escape, which together opened six programs behind one mechanism. The query half needed a new wz capability rather than a binding: wz owed exactly one ResponseFinal per dispatched request and staged it with the handler jobs, which is correct only while a handler cannot outlive its dispatch -- and z_queryable_channel.c answers from the application thread minutes later. Both upstreams instead owe the terminator to whoever HOLDS the query, so Session gained hold_response_final / release_response_final and a handler that escapes now takes the hold before its own batchterminator job runs. Without it the leg is 3 of 3 red and the failure is silent on both ends. The second divergence came from an oracle, not from a plan: upstream z_bytes.c compiled twice printed one 9-byte slice on wz where the real library printed three of 3, because wz concatenated appended payloads and the code documented that as a named divergence on the strength of a header sentence permitting any slice arrangement. The header does say that; it was still wrong, because the two implementations printed different output for the same program. ByteBuf now carries segment boundaries and the two stdouts are byte-identical.
verification_bullets: MEASURED FIRST AND LAST, by compiling all 32 upstream examples against the cdylib: 23 of 32 linked at the start of the round, 32 of 32 at the end. The nine that opened are z_sub_channel, z_pull, z_get_channel, z_queryable_channel, z_querier, z_get_liveliness, z_bytes, z_advanced_pub and z_advanced_sub.

FOUR NEW DRIVEN LEGS, not four links. LEG 16: upstream z_sub_channel.c on wz pulls a real zenoh-pico z_put's sample off a FIFO channel on its own thread. LEG 17: upstream z_queryable_channel.c on wz answers a real zenoh-pico z_get, and the FOREIGN process reports the reply. LEG 18: upstream z_bytes.c compiled twice and diffed. LEG 19: upstream z_advanced_sub.c on wz against upstream's own z_advanced_pub.c on the REAL libzenohpico.so.

THE ORACLE CAUGHT A DIVERGENCE THE LINK COUNT COULD NOT. LEG 18 red on its first run: the real pico printed three slices of 3 bytes where wz printed one of 9. wz concatenated appended payloads, and the prior code documented that as a named divergence on the grounds that upstream's header promises no slice arrangement. The header does say that, and it was still the wrong call -- the two implementations printed different output for the same program. ByteBuf now carries segment boundaries and the two stdouts are byte-identical.

THE DEFERRED REPLY IS DAMAGE-PROBED, and it is the round's real mechanism. Without the hold, LEG 17 is 3 of 3 RED; with it, 4 of 4 GREEN. The failure it prevents is silent on both ends: the Final goes out while the query is still in the ring, the querier closes its pending entry, and every later reply is discarded with no error anywhere.

THE SEGMENT BOUNDARIES ARE DAMAGE-PROBED TOO, and the FIRST attempt was void. Reverting append to a raw write left append_segments unused, which is a dead-code error under -D warnings, so the probe never built and never reded. Re-run with the allow attached: 2 of 2 RED with the damage, green without.

Round 311y532.decision_summary: R311y532 -- every upstream pico program that CAN be driven now is: the driven count goes 17 of 32 to 28, and the four that remain are stub mains at this pin plus one that dereferences pico internals. The round found two real defects, and neither was visible to any earlier leg. wz advanced publisher published nineteen times while a plain foreign subscriber received nothing, because the per-face AdvancedPublisher::declare returns NoRuntime when called from the C application thread -- which is the ordinary path, since a dialed session brings its face up before z_open returns -- and the best-effort per-face loop swallowed it. And a real zenoh-pico queryable reply arrived at upstream own z_get_attachment.c on wz with its attachment gone, because the reply marshal read none of ReplyView attachment, put_encoding or timestamp. The round also has a methodological result worth more than either fix: the first calibration of the foreign advanced pair against itself showed ZERO delivery in three topologies and would have justified writing wz off as matching a broken reference. It was the harness -- no stdbuf, block-buffered counterparty logs. Line-buffered the same pair is 7 of 7, and only then was the wz failure a finding rather than a shared limit. Two more limits are now gated rather than silent: four programs are stub mains under this pico feature config, established by running each binary and by reading the #if at the top of each source, and z_pong reads sample->payload as a struct field so it can never be a drop-in client of a handle-based ABI.
verification_bullets: MEASURED: 32 of 32 upstream examples LINK, and the DRIVEN count goes 17 to 28. The four that remain undriven are stubs at this pin and the fifth is z_pong; both groups are gated rather than left silent.

THE ORACLE PAIR WAS CALIBRATED BEFORE wz WAS BLAMED, and the first calibration was WRONG. Real pico z_advanced_pub against real pico z_advanced_sub appeared to deliver ZERO samples in three topologies including through a zenohd. The cause was the harness: no stdbuf, so the counterparty logs were block-buffered and looked empty. Re-run line-buffered it is 7 of 7, which is what made the wz-side failure a real finding instead of a shared one.

TWO REAL DEFECTS, both found by a new leg and neither visible to any earlier one. The advanced publisher on wz published 19 times and a PLAIN foreign subscriber received ZERO -- the per-face AdvancedPublisher::declare returned NoRuntime on the C application thread and the best-effort loop swallowed it, so z_advanced_pub reported Z_OK while putting to nobody. And a real pico queryable's reply attachment never reached upstream's own z_get_attachment.c on wz, because the reply marshal read none of ReplyView's attachment / put_encoding / timestamp.

THE RING'S EVICTION IS NOW WITNESSED ON THE WIRE and damage-probed. Four samples into a ring of two, drained once: the newest two present, the oldest two ABSENT. Flipping the evict to pop_back reds it 2 of 2; restored it is green 3 of 3. Before this leg a ring that kept the OLDEST passed every channel test in the tree.

z_pong CANNOT BE DRIVEN, and the reason is structural rather than a missing export. Its callback never calls the API: it reads sample->payload as a FIELD of pico's concrete _z_sample_t and writes z_owned_bytes_t._val directly. Matching the layout would not be enough either -- the by-value copy is then z_moved into z_publisher_put, which for a Box handle is a double free. Measured: the real z_ping completes ZERO round trips against it and hangs.

FOUR PROGRAMS ARE STUB MAINS AT THIS PIN, established two independent ways (running each binary, and reading the #if at the top of each source): z_pub_tls / z_sub_tls want Z_FEATURE_LINK_TLS 1 and the config has 0; z_pub_st / z_sub_st want Z_FEATURE_MULTI_THREAD 0 and it has 1. Two legs written against the single-threaded pair were DELETED once this was measured, rather than left to fail.

Renamed to measures; the lane now reads 29 passed, 2 filtered, and the two are the zenohd legs Layer Z owns.

The two that remain are z_pub_tls and z_sub_tls, and the blocker is PROVISIONING, not a wz export: Z_FEATURE_LINK_TLS 1 makes pico's link.h include mbedtls/*.h, so neither the header arm nor the example compiles without Mbed TLS development headers. This box has the runtime .so and not the headers. Whoever installs them gets two real legs for the price of a cmake flag -- the single-threaded arm this round added is the template, and it needs no second cdylib.

THE BORROW TAG IS EXERCISED BY EXACTLY ONE PRODUCER AND ONE CONSUMER. SampleMarshal::bind sets it, take_moved_bytes and the ownership macro's drop read it. No test drives a C program that z_drops an aliased bytes rather than moving it into a put, so that arm of the contract is written and unwitnessed.

THE SAMPLE LAYOUT PREFIX STOPS AT payload. _z_sample_t continues with timestamp, encoding, kind, qos, attachment, reliability and source_info, and a C program reading any of those still gets wz's own fields misread as pico's. Only z_pong needed the payload; the next program that reads a different member will need the same treatment and should extend the prefix rather than special-case itself.

A SINGLE GREEN RUN CONVICTED THE WRONG CHANGE FOR HALF AN HOUR THIS ROUND. The bisect that blamed the sample-layout edit rested on one pristine pass; the leg was 2-in-6 at HEAD. Any bisect over a leg whose rate has not been measured is reading a coin flip, and the cheap guard is to run the pristine arm as many times as the damaged one.

Round 311y533.decision_summary: R311y533 -- the driven count goes 27 to 30 of 32, and every one of the three came out of an EXCLUSION whose observation was right and whose consequence nobody re-checked. The single-threaded pair was excluded as needing a different pico build AND a second cdylib arm; the first half costs one cmake configure with no compile, and the second was measured false -- across the two configs only z_owned_mutex_t and z_owned_condvar_t change size and neither example names either type. What it really needed was one missing export, zp_spin_once, and the linker said so. z_pong was excluded as needing pico internal arc-slice representation reproduced; what it needed was a 48-byte layout prefix on SampleMarshal and a borrow tag, because pico itself solves that aliasing with an _aliased flag rather than with refcounting. The real zenoh-pico z_ping now completes 5 of 5 round trips through upstream z_pong.c running on wz. The round also fixed a REAL defect that a flaky leg had been hiding: z_liveliness_get arms a 10 second deadline that no host under the C ABI ever swept, so an unanswered snapshot blocked the C caller in z_recv forever. And it nearly convicted the wrong change on the way -- a single green run on the pristine tree read as proof of a regression when the leg was 2 in 6 at HEAD, and calibrating that leg oracle showed the reference implementation cannot serve its topology at all: real pico against real pico is ZERO tokens and a hang, 6 of 6.
verification_bullets: MEASURED: upstream programs DRIVEN goes to 30 of 32, counted from the test file itself rather than from a tally. The two that remain are z_pub_tls and z_sub_tls, and their blocker is now stated in kind: turning Z_FEATURE_LINK_TLS on makes pico's link.h include mbedtls headers, so the header arm cannot even be configured without Mbed TLS development headers. Measured on this box: libmbedtls.so.2.28 is installed, mbedtls/entropy.h is not, and cc stops at that include. A provisioning prerequisite, not a wz export gap.

THE SINGLE-THREADED EXCLUSION WAS RIGHT ABOUT ITS OBSERVATION AND WRONG ABOUT ITS CONSEQUENCE. It said a zp_spin_once build needs a different pico build (true, and it costs one cmake configure, no compile) and that a different build needs a second cdylib arm (false). Measured across the two configs: only z_owned_mutex_t and z_owned_condvar_t change size, and neither example names either type. Two claims, one checked.

z_pong IS DRIVEN, and it was carried as structurally impossible. The real zenoh-pico z_ping completes 5 of 5 round trips through upstream's z_pong.c running on wz. What it needed was a 48-byte layout prefix and a borrow tag, not a reimplementation of pico's refcounted arc-slice vector -- pico itself solves the same aliasing problem with the _aliased flag in its svec header, not with refcounting.

BOTH z_pong MECHANISMS DAMAGE-PROBED SEPARATELY. Leaving the pico payload slot unbound: 0 round trips, red. Keeping the slot but dropping the borrow tag so the copy reads as owned: the drop-in dies before it accepts, red. Restored, green.

THE ST LEGS DAMAGE-PROBED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Renaming the zp_spin_once export: both legs red with `undefined reference to zp_spin_once`. Pointing the ST helper at the primary header arm: both legs red on the stub main's own ERROR line. Restored, green.

A FLAKY LEG NEARLY CONVICTED THE WRONG CHANGE. The liveliness snapshot leg went red after the sample-layout edit and a single green run on the pristine tree read as proof of a regression. Re-measured at HEAD with no changes at all: 2 pass in 6. The bisect had been reading a coin flip.

CALIBRATING THAT LEG'S ORACLE OVERTURNED ITS PREMISE. The real zenoh-pico z_get_liveliness against the real zenoh-pico z_liveliness, line-buffered, in the leg's own peer-to-client topology reports ZERO alive tokens and hangs: 6 runs of 6. With a zenohd between them the same foreign pair answers at once. The topology was one the reference cannot serve, and wz's one-in-three was wz being MORE permissive than pico. Rebuilt on the router topology it is 5 of 5, and damage-probed: the get asking for a key the token holder did not declare reds it.

THE FLAKINESS ALSO EXPOSED A REAL DEFECT, FIXED RATHER THAN ROUTED AROUND. z_liveliness_get arms a 10 s deadline (pico's own rule for timeout_ms == 0) that NO host under the C ABI ever swept -- the only sweeper in the tree was wz-ap-demo's ticker reaching into the observer by hand. Instrumented: on a hang, CClosure::drop never ran, so the channel never closed and the C caller blocked in z_recv forever. With the sweep wired the same failure terminates at 11.1 s, which is the 10 s timeout doing its job.
LANES, all local: A3 pass 7s (85 remaining, EXACT, unchanged -- a witness moves no atom status), A5 pass (201 of 213 atoms, 12 justified exclusions), C0 pass 2s.

carry_forward_bullets: THE MEASUREMENT THAT CLOSES THE ARC: 32 of 32 upstream zenoh-pico examples LINK and 32 of 32 are DRIVEN. What it actually needed was a pinned upstream Mbed TLS with its own pkgconfig, and then one cmake flag. Turning that flag on rides the PRIMARY header arm rather than a fourth configure, which was measured rather than assumed: across TLS 0 and 1 all 86 public types keep identical size and alignment, so one cdylib still serves every leg. The wz side was the real work -- the C ABI read two of pico's twelve TLS config keys, only in their PATH form, and fed them to the QUIC acceptor alone, while the dial path used DialConfig::default() unconditionally and so could not complete a tls/ handshake at all. Now all twelve resolve, path or inline base64, into an ABI-neutral CapiTlsConfig that fills both the TLS acceptor slot and a real dial config. The two new legs put wz on opposite halves of the handshake: LEG 35 is wz ACCEPTING a real zenoh-pico subscriber over TLS, LEG 36 is wz DIALING a real zenoh-pico publisher, and three damage probes separate them in both directions. The topology was calibrated against the reference first, and the obvious arrangement was wrong -- a client-dialing declared publisher delivers zero samples between two real picos, on TCP as well as TLS, so the publisher listens in both legs. AP-full was re-measured at the same time rather than re-read: A5 is complete and gated at 201 of 213 with 12 justified exclusions, and the only one that was not a platform/runtime tautology is enforced by a compile_error!.

Round 311y535.decision_summary: R311y535 -- the matching-plane flake y534 measured and left open, root-caused and closed. It was never a test race: z_undeclare_matching_listener was returning with the C context still alive, and instrumentation showed the drop landing about 5 ms later on the drive thread, so pico's contract that undeclare frees the context was being met only by luck. The cause was ownership. The C sink was an Arc CLONED into the SSOT entry, into every per-face callback, and into face_down's purge snapshot, so the drop(context) ran when the LAST clone fell -- and face_down holds both a snapshot and the departing face's own entry across a window the C thread can land in. The fix makes the aggregate the ONE owner: MatchEntry no longer carries a sink, the per-face callbacks carry only the shared state, and the purge snapshots state alone. Retirement then becomes deterministic for free, because the mutex that already serialises C delivery is exactly the exclusion a synchronous free needs: retire_matching_sink takes that lock, which cannot be granted while a thread is inside the callback, takes the sink out, and returns it so the caller drops it outside the guard. The one case that cannot be made synchronous -- a callback undeclaring its own listener, where the lock wanted is the lock held -- is detected by a thread-local delivery depth and falls back to release-by-Arc-drop rather than deadlocking. Measured 1 fail in 21 before and 60 of 60 after, but the proof is three new unit tests on the production function plus three damage probes that separate them, not the streak.
verification_bullets: DIAGNOSED BEFORE FIXED, and the diagnosis changed what was built. Instrumenting the failing assertion to poll instead of assert: 40 runs produced one `immediate=0 after=1 settled_ms=5`. So the context was NOT leaked -- it was freed ~5 ms later on another thread. That is what identified the defect as a RELEASE-TIMING contract divergence rather than a leak, and pointed at the Arc clone holders rather than at the undeclare path itself.

THE RATE WAS MEASURED ON BOTH ARMS BEFORE AND AFTER. Before: 1 fail in 21 on the PRISTINE tree (6 + 15 runs), 1 in 6 on the working tree. After: 60 passes in 60. The unit tests below are what make that a proof rather than a longer green streak.

Round 311y536.decision_summary: R311y536 -- main had been red on hosted CI for at least five consecutive runs and nobody had looked, because every round had been recording that its lanes were green LOCALLY and that is a statement about a different set of things. Seven lanes, four causes. Two of them are wz-session-core failing to COMPILE in feature subsets: send_declare was gated on liveliness-token, the feature that happened to introduce it, while two of its three callers are gated on declare-subscriber, so a routed-declare build without liveliness compiled callers of a method that did not exist; and flush_peer_tokens_on_link_loss reached an alloc-gated field, alloc::vec::Vec and String carrying no gate at all, so every no-alloc build failed with four errors. The third is Layer A4, red on three static findings that turned out to be one defect wearing three hats: two corpus files reached the real zenoh-pico LIBRARY, and one of them wz's own cdylib, through resolvers they built by hand, and the audit derives a file's foreign class and its binary-under-test from the RESOLVER FUNCTIONS a file names -- so the strongest api-compat proofs in the tree read as wz-versus-wz tests, and a scout leg carried a KIND the grammar never had. The fourth is Layer Z, which runs the three zenohd-named drop-in legs and never built the cdylib they link; locally invisible because Layer E builds it into the same target dir first, and on hosted CI they are separate jobs on separate machines. All four fixed, four damage probes, ten lanes locally green -- and hosted, which is the arbiter, has not yet reported.

What made it survive was not the wrong number but the guard's shape: a bare pipe into  throws away the child's output and every word of the reason, so the lane failed in three seconds stating neither what it expected nor what it saw, and diagnosing it meant running the commands by hand. carry_forward_bullets: R311y538 = api-compat-c 4 -> 11 of 22, and the six planes that moved it are all shims over the SHARED wz-capi-core model rather than new protocol. That is the reusable finding: the pico ABI had already built the liveliness SSOT, the peer_identities enumeration and the matching aggregation, so the zenoh-c side cost a spelling each. Expect the same of the query plane -- declare_queryable and the reply machinery are already in the core.

THE ELEVEN THAT REMAIN, ranked by what they need. z_pull (5 symbols: the ring channel handler plus z_owned_sample_t); z_queryable (8: closure_query, declare_queryable, the four query accessors, query_reply); z_get (12: the fifo reply handler plus z_get and the reply family); then z_non_blocking_get, z_queryable_with_channels, z_querier and z_storage fall out of those two families; z_get_liveliness needs z_liveliness_get, which the pico ABI has including its sweeper; z_ping needs the mutex/condvar family the pico ABI already wrote in src/sync.rs; z_scout needs the hello family; z_bytes needs 34 ze_serialize/deserialize symbols and is the only one that is genuinely its own subsystem.

THE FOOTPRINT GATE IS NOW THE LOAD-BEARING CHECK and it must widen with every new stack-allocated type. Twenty types are measured against the installed header; the two publisher options structs are the ones to keep watching, because they are the only ones whose size RUSTC computes from a mirrored field list rather than a transcribed constant, and both move with Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API.

NAMED RESIDUALS, written down rather than left to be inferred from silence: z_publisher_options_t and z_publisher_put_options_t are ACCEPTED AND IGNORED, so a program that sets an encoding, congestion control, priority, express, locality, timestamp or attachment on a publisher is not misled about the API and IS misled about the wire. z_declare_publisher does not alias a declared keyexpr. Only the BACKGROUND matching listener exists; the owned form needs z_owned_matching_listener_t.

CALIBRATE THE ORACLE BEFORE WRITING THE LEG, again. The liveliness retraction cost one red test and one calibration run to find out that the arrangement was unserveable by the reference. The rule that would have saved it: run the leg foreign-to-foreign FIRST, and if the reference cannot produce the observation, the leg is asking the wrong side.

Round 311y538.decision_summary: R311y538 -- the zenoh-c C ABI went from 4 to 11 of upstream's 22 linkable examples, and the six planes that moved it were spellings of code the pico ABI had already built rather than new protocol. Five modules landed over the shared wz-capi-core session model: liveliness (token plus subscriber, retraction in the state's Drop so the explicit and implicit paths cannot drift), the zid family (z_id_t at alignment one, z_id_to_string LSB-first and never trimmed, and the three z_info_* enumerations whose routers/peers split is made at the ABI boundary because the core serves both ABIs), the publisher plane with both feature arms of its two TRANSPARENT options structs mirrored field-for-field so rustc computes the layout, the encoding constants, and the background matching listener whose verdict is aggregated across faces. The check that matters is the footprint gate, widened from 8 to 20 types measured against the installed header by a C compiler: all twenty agree, including the two options structs whose sizes move with Z_FEATURE_UNSTABLE_API. A link is not a pass, so three legs drive the new planes against a real zenoh-pico, and the fourth leg written was WRONG in a way only the oracle could say: it asserted that killing a wz token holder makes a foreign subscriber report the drop, and two real picos in the same arrangement report nothing, because a process SIGTERMed without a handler cannot emit its own retraction. The claim moved to the direction where wz is the observer. Separately, the z_info drop-in leg had been a one-in-sixteen flake since it was written, asserting its oracle was 32 hex characters where uhlc trims leading zero nibbles; the guard now states what upstream guarantees and a new leg pins the short case deterministically.
verification_bullets: MEASURED, NOT CLAIMED: api-compat-c went 4 -> 11 of 22 upstream zenoh-c examples linking, reported by Layer C1cc's own coverage script on every run. The six that moved are z_liveliness, z_sub_liveliness, z_sub_thr, z_info, z_pong, z_pub_thr and z_pub. The 7 ORACLE-ONLY examples stay out of the denominator.

THE FOOTPRINT GATE IS THE PROOF THAT MATTERS, and it widened 8 -> 20 types measured against the INSTALLED header by a C compiler: all 20 agree, including z_publisher_options_t and z_publisher_put_options_t, whose sizes are FEATURE-DEPENDENT and were computed by rustc from a mirrored field list rather than transcribed. A stack-allocated type whose size wz gets wrong corrupts the caller's frame rather than failing anything.

A LINK IS NOT A PASS, so three legs drive the new planes against a REAL zenoh-pico: upstream z_pub.c on wz reaches a real pico z_sub AND its matching listener is told about that foreign subscriber (two barriers, both caused by the foreign process); z_liveliness.c on wz is seen alive by a real pico z_sub_liveliness; z_sub_liveliness.c on wz sees a real pico token come AND GO.

THE RETRACTION LEG EXISTS BECAUSE THE FIRST ONE WAS WRONG AND THE ORACLE SAID SO. The first draft asserted that killing a wz token holder makes a foreign subscriber print Dropped token. It red. Calibration foreign-to-foreign -- real pico z_liveliness against real pico z_sub_liveliness, same topology -- prints New alive token and then NOTHING on SIGTERM: the holder has no signal handler, so nothing runs in that process. The claim was moved to the direction where wz is the OBSERVER and must synthesize the delete from face_down, which is a property the reference does not have.

A FLAKE THAT HAD BEEN THERE SINCE THE LEG WAS WRITTEN. pico_zinfo_source_on_wz_capi_reports_a_real_zenohd_as_a_router asserted its oracle was 32 hex characters; zenohd came up as 9c3a1e13dd2689ece0c232e62887fbc, which is 31. uhlc::ID renders through {:x} over a u128 (uhlc-0.8.2/src/id.rs:281), so one random zid in 16 is short. The C side never trims (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/utils/uuid.c:38-41). DAMAGE PROBE: making z_id_to_string trim leaves the old leg GREEN and reds LEG 9z with both spellings side by side -- so the old leg could not discriminate the rule at all.
